Company Description
Are you a skilled engineer who enjoys variety, problem-solving, and working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment? 2 Sisters Food Group in Scunthorpe is looking for a Site Services Engineer to join our Engineering team and play a vital role in keeping our site running safely, efficiently, and reliably. You'll be involved in everything from planned maintenance and fault finding to supporting major site services and continuous improvement initiatives.
2 Sisters Food Group is one of the largest and most stable employers in North Lincolnshire. The site has been in operation for over 35 years and continues to grow and develop with significant investment from the business.
If you are looking for work with a stable employer, where you get support, development, a team environment, excellent benefits and an hourly rate of £21.50ph, then a position at 2 Sisters Food Group in Scunthorpe could be for you.
Job Description
As a Site Services Engineer, you'll be responsible for maintaining and repairing a wide range of site services equipment and infrastructure. No two days are the same, and you'll be expected to tackle both electrical and mechanical challenges across a large manufacturing site.
Key responsibilities include:
Carrying out electrical and mechanical maintenance and repairs across the site.
Diagnosing faults and undertaking effective repairs to plant and equipment.
Supporting plant start-up and shutdown procedures, including boilers, refrigeration systems, and other critical utilities.
Performing routine inspections, checks, tests, and Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) activities.
Completing maintenance records accurately using the Piranha Planned Maintenance System.
Assisting with audit preparation activities, including customer, technical, and pest control requirements.
This is not an exhaustive list and daily tasks will vary significantly.
Qualifications
We're seeking a versatile and proactive engineer who can work independently and respond effectively to a wide range of maintenance challenges.
Requirements
Time-served Electrical or Mechanical Engineer (multi-skilled experience highly advantageous).
Qualification in electrical installation and commissioning would be highly advantageous or willingness to undertake training in this area.
Strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work with minimal supervision.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships at all levels.
Experience supporting and working alongside contractors.
Forward-thinking approach with a passion for continuous improvement.
Additional Information
Why Join Us?
This is an excellent opportunity to join a dynamic engineering team where you'll have the chance to develop your skills, work on a diverse range of equipment, and make a genuine impact on site performance. If you're an engineer who enjoys variety, autonomy, and continuous improvement, we'd love to hear from you.
What’s in it for you?
Other than an hourly rate of £21.50, we also pride ourselves on developing staff potential, with many opportunities for in house training along with externally supplied qualifications and support, to help drive your career forward.
Other benefits include:
A subsidised company bus service (7 pickup locations across Ashby & Scunthorpe).
Refer a friend scheme (£100).
Subsidised and recently upgraded canteen (hot meals from £1.60).
Free onsite parking.
Staff chicken sales at a heavily discounted price.
Seasonal events and family fun days.
Great discounts from a number of different sources (up to 50% off), details in the link.

Editor - Sport, Entertainment & F1
At 50 Sport, we turn sport into entertainment. And great editing is at the heart of it. 
We take the best of sport and find new ways to tell its stories through sharp, creative and entertaining content. From big moments that shake an industry, to raw and authentic stories that make fans feel like they’re right there. We want to create content that stops the scroll, gets people talking and makes them fall even harder for the sports and teams they love. 
We’re The Sports Entertainment Agency. We work with some of the biggest names in global sport, from leading F1 teams and international tournaments to some of the world’s most recognised Sporting brands. We bring sport, entertainment and culture together to create content that fans actually want to watch. 
Now, we’re looking for an Editor to join our Studio Team. 
We want someone who gets sport. And if F1 is your thing, even better.  
Someone who knows what motorsports fans are interested in, understands the tension of a race weekend and gets excited by the stories happening both on and off the track. You don’t just need to know how to edit; you need to know what makes a moment worth watching.

• Develop and deliver the Trust’s communications strategy, ensuring activity is measurable, impactful and aligned to organisational priorities.
• Lead integrated internal and external communications campaigns supporting funding programmes, research publications, charity partnerships and wider social impact initiatives.

• Drive colleague engagement by developing campaigns that increase participation in volunteering, fundraising, skills-based support and other Trust initiatives.

💬 ACCURX IS WHERE CONVERSATIONS HAPPEN WITH AND ABOUT PATIENTS.
For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. We’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that connects everyone through communication.
What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.
Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.
The team
We are a mission-driven team of 80 engineers based in London and the surrounding areas, united by the challenge of fixing healthcare communication. We are innovating for the NHS at a scale and depth that has never been done before, solving the real-world problems that stand between millions of patients and the care they need.
We are a highly cross-functional group where engineering, product, data, and security collaborate as true peers. We foster a low-ego, high-impact environment that values expertise and new ideas, maintaining the high standards required to build and scale a national healthcare communication platform. Within this ecosystem, our teams operate with high autonomy, owning everything from initial system design to long-term service stability.
As a Senior Data Engineer, you’ll sit at the intersection of our Analytics Engineering, Product, and ML teams, designing and scaling the pipelines and data architecture that everything else is built on, and building the foundations that turn data from a support function into a strategic asset.
Challenges you’ll solve…
- You will design and scale a robust data architecture that handles massive event-driven communication flows across nearly every GP practice in the UK.
- You will build and own ingestion and ELT pipelines end-to-end, from source systems through to our Snowflake data warehouse, using Python and SQL in production.
- You will make and own architectural decisions that support analytics, experimentation and machine learning at scale.
- You will partner closely with Analytics Engineering, Product and ML teams to turn raw healthcare communication data into reliable, high-performance datasets they can build on.
- You will set and uphold standards for data integrity, security and reliability, in an environment where getting data right is part of keeping patients safe.
- You will lay the data foundations for our AI and ML work, helping take models from experimentation into production.
- You will take on greenfield problems, shaping how data works at Accurx from the ground up.
- You will mentor teammates and contribute to a strong engineering culture through rigorous code reviews, sprint planning and open collaboration.
You should apply if…
- You have strong, proven experience as a Data Engineer, designing and building ingestion and ETL/ELT pipelines from scratch using Python and SQL in production environments.
- You have a deep understanding of modern cloud data platforms such as Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift, and transformation tools like dbt, with a focus on creating clean, reliable and reusable datasets.
- You are comfortable owning decisions around data architecture, and working with cloud environments and software engineering best practices like Git and CI/CD.
- You have experience, or a strong interest, in building and operationalising machine learning models, and understand how strong data foundations enable better AI outcomes.
- You think beyond pipelines. You care about how data drives real-world outcomes, especially in healthcare, and can work cross-functionally to shape problems and deliver solutions.
- You actively leverage AI tools to automate routine tasks and continuously explore ways to integrate AI into your workflows, improving quality and speed.
What’s in it for you?
You’ll join a high-performing team on a mission to solve healthcare productivity, building a platform used by around 300k NHS staff every week, supporting the care of over 50 million NHS patients every year. We set a high bar, move fast, and give people the ownership and support to do the best work of their careers.
- £85,000 - £105,000 base salary, plus a discretionary recognition bonus for exceptional performance and impact, nominated by managers and awarded by our leadership team
- Equity: £30,000 in equal share options, so you share in the value you help create
- Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life
- Built for collaboration: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office for a minimum of 3 days a week
- Close to our users: Regular hackathons, plus dedicated time to visit GP practices and other healthcare settings to see first-hand how our products are used
- Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year
- Support at home: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support
- We have our very own chefs: Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches, plus a weekly sweet treat

job_title: Group Head of Technology Cyber and Resilience Risk
job_description:
We’re looking for an experienced and collaborative senior risk leader to join us as Head of Technology, Cyber and Resilience Risk.
This is a high-profile and meaningful leadership role within our Group Risk function, where you’ll have the opportunity to shape how we understand, manage and respond to some of the most important risks facing our organisation.
As a trusted adviser to the head of Digital Risk, EUI leadership, senior executives and relevant Board committees, you’ll provide thoughtful, independent insight to help ensure our most significant risks are well understood, effectively managed and transparently reported.
This role reports into the Digital Risk team and you’ll work closely with senior leaders and colleagues across Risk, Technology, Cyber and Operational Resilience, bringing together different perspectives and building strong, trusted relationships. Through clear insight, constructive challenge and open collaboration, you’ll help us make well-informed decisions that support our customers, colleagues and long-term ambitions.
Alongside your technical knowledge, how you lead and support others will be just as important. You’ll have the opportunity to influence significant strategic, technology and investment decisions, while creating an environment where a talented specialist risk team can grow, contribute and do their best work.
Why join us?
This is a rare opportunity to shape the organisation’s approach to some of its most important and rapidly evolving risks. You will have the visibility and influence to support significant decisions, strengthen resilience and help protect our customers, colleagues and long-term strategic ambitions.
If you are a forward-thinking risk leader who combines technical credibility with commercial judgement, clear communication and the confidence to challenge at the highest level, we would love to hear from you.
Main Responsibilities • Providing independent second-line oversight across technology, cyber and operational resilience risk.
• Offering clear and balanced risk opinions on material exposures, control weaknesses, emerging threats and management responses.
• Building trusted relationships with the Head of Digital Risk, EUI leadership, senior technology and cyber leaders, executives and Board committees.
• Making complex technical risks accessible by translating them into clear business implications, recommendations and decisions.
• Working collaboratively to ensure technology, cyber and resilience considerations are embedded early in strategic, investment and transformation decisions.
• Providing thoughtful and constructive challenge on technology strategy, architecture, cloud, cyber security, business continuity, disaster recovery and operational resilience.
• Bringing together Group and EUI risk perspectives to identify shared exposures, concentrations and dependencies.
• Overseeing the organisation’s ability to prevent, withstand, respond to and recover from significant disruption.
• Providing independent insight across important business services, impact tolerances, scenario testing, third-party resilience, crisis management and recovery arrangements.
• Supporting and leading regulatory engagement on material technology, cyber and operational resilience matters.
• Setting a clear strategic direction and quality expectations for the Technology, Cyber and Resilience Risk team.
• Leading, supporting and developing a specialist team, creating an inclusive environment where colleagues feel empowered to share their expertise and provide effective challenge.
Essential skills and Experience
• You’ll be an experienced senior leader with strong knowledge of technology risk, cyber risk and/or operational resilience, ideally gained within a complex and highly regulated organisation.
• Experience working with executive teams, Boards and Board Risk Committees.
• Sound judgement and the ability to provide constructive challenge and raise concerns appropriately.
• Strong knowledge of technology, cyber security and operational resilience risk management.
• Experience assessing risk exposure against appetite and evaluating control environments.
• A good understanding of cloud, technology resilience, cyber security, business continuity, disaster recovery and third-party resilience.
• Experience of important business services, impact tolerances, scenario testing and resilience planning.
• The ability to identify wider or systemic risks and communicate the issues that need executive or Board attention.
• Strong commercial awareness, with the ability to connect technical risk to customer outcomes, strategic delivery, investment decisions and business performance.
• Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with an ability to make complex information clear, accessible and decision-focused.
• A track record of supporting, motivating and developing specialist teams and creating an environment where people can thrive.
• Experience engaging collaboratively with regulators, Internal Audit and other assurance functions.
• A calm, thoughtful and pragmatic approach to leadership, including when navigating complex or high-pressure situations.
Desirable Skills and Experience • Relevant professional qualifications in technology risk, cyber security, operational resilience or IT control assurance. These could include CISM, CISSP, CRISC, CISA, CCSK or CCAK

job_title: Quantum Error Correction Scientist / Senior Quantum Error Correction Scientist
job_description:
The Role
We are looking for a Quantum Error Correction Scientist to join our team developing the architecture and technologies needed for scalable, fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.
You will research, develop and evaluate quantum error correction codes, decoders and fault-tolerant protocols, with a focus on their implementation in Aegiq's photonic quantum computing architecture. Your work will involve modelling realistic hardware noise, evaluating logical performance and understanding the resources needed to build reliable quantum computers at scale.
Working closely with our quantum architecture, software and experimental teams, you will help translate theoretical approaches into practical system requirements and engineering decisions. You'll investigate how different error correction strategies interact with our hardware and contribute directly to the development of our next-generation quantum computing systems.
This is an opportunity to tackle challenging problems in quantum computing, contribute to the technical direction of our architecture and see your research inform the development of real quantum hardware.
Depending on experience, the position may be offered at Senior Quantum Error Correction Scientist level.
What You’ll Be Doing • Quantum Error Correction: Research, develop and simulate quantum error correction codes, decoders and fault-tolerant protocols for scalable quantum computing.
• Photonic Architecture: Investigate QEC approaches suited to photonic and measurement-based quantum computing, considering the capabilities and constraints of Aegiq's hardware architecture.
• Noise Modelling: Develop realistic models of hardware noise and loss, including photon loss, erasure errors and other relevant physical error mechanisms.
• Performance & Resource Analysis: Evaluate fault-tolerance thresholds, logical error rates, resource overheads and scalability. Compare different QEC approaches to understand their practical advantages and limitations.
• Decoder Development: Develop, implement and benchmark decoding algorithms, considering accuracy, computational performance and integration with quantum computing control systems.
• Hardware & Software Integration: Work closely with quantum architecture, experimental and software teams to translate QEC requirements into hardware specifications, control strategies and compilation approaches.
• Scientific Computing: Develop numerical simulations and research software to evaluate error correction protocols, validate theoretical models and support architectural decisions.
• Research & Collaboration: Contribute to technical publications, patents, research programmes and collaborative activities, communicating findings to colleagues across the company.
About Aegiq
Aegiq is a Sheffield-based quantum technology company developing scalable, fault-tolerant photonic quantum computers. Founded in 2019, we work across the full quantum computing stack, from semiconductor chips and photonic hardware to software and real-world applications.
In 2025, we delivered our first-generation quantum computer to the UK's National Quantum Computing Centre. We're now developing our second-generation platform and expanding our team to tackle the scientific and engineering challenges involved in building quantum computers at scale.
We're a growing team of scientists, engineers and specialists who enjoy solving difficult problems and turning new ideas into working technology. At Aegiq, you'll have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, contribute directly to the technology we're developing and help shape the future of the company.
We value different backgrounds, experiences and ways of thinking. If you're excited about the work we're doing, we'd encourage you to apply, even if your experience doesn't match every requirement listed.
Requirements
What We're Looking For
• Education: A PhD in Quantum Information, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent relevant research or industry experience.
• Quantum Computing Knowledge: A strong understanding of quantum information, quantum error correction, fault-tolerant quantum computing or closely related topics.
• Analytical Skills: Strong mathematical and numerical problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex theoretical and computational problems.
• Scientific Programming: Experience using Python, C++ or similar programming languages to implement numerical simulations, algorithms or scientific software.
• Research & Development: Ability to independently investigate open-ended research problems, evaluate competing approaches and critically assess results.
• Technical Understanding: Ability to connect theoretical methods with practical implementation challenges, considering the capabilities and limitations of quantum computing hardware.
• Communication & Collaboration: Ability to communicate technical findings clearly and work effectively with colleagues across quantum theory, software and experimental engineering.
Nice to Have
• Experience designing, implementing or simulating quantum error correction codes and decoders.
• Knowledge of photonic quantum computing, measurement-based quantum computing or distributed quantum architectures.
• Experience modelling photon loss, erasure-biased noise or other hardware-specific error mechanisms.
• Familiarity with stabiliser codes, topological codes, subsystem codes or quantum LDPC codes.
• Experience with fault-tolerant logical operations, logical state preparation, lattice surgery or magic-state distillation.
• Experience performing fault-tolerance threshold calculations, logical error analysis or quantum resource estimation.
• Familiarity with QEC simulation and decoding tools such as Stim, PyMatching, Qiskit, Cirq or equivalent frameworks.
• Experience developing efficient decoding algorithms or evaluating computational requirements for real-time decoding.
• Experience with collaborative scientific software development, including Git, automated testing and continuous integration.
• Experience working with quantum hardware teams or translating theoretical requirements into experimental implementations.
• Experience contributing to collaborative research programmes or technical publications.
• Experience working in a startup, growing technology company or commercial research environment.
For Senior Scientist Applicants
Candidates considered for Senior Quantum Error Correction Scientist level should demonstrate an established track record in quantum error correction, fault-tolerant quantum computing or closely related research.
We would expect you to take ownership of substantial research activities, define technical approaches, make independent scientific decisions and contribute to the direction of Aegiq's fault-tolerant quantum computing architecture.
You should also be comfortable providing technical guidance and supporting the development of other team members.
We know that no two people have the same experience. If you're interested in the role and meet most, but not all, of the criteria, we'd still encourage you to apply.
Benefits
• Competitive salary, based on experience and skills.
• 25 days of annual leave, in addition to bank holidays and company closure days.
• A Sheffield-based workplace, with excellent transport links and a great balance of city life and affordability.
• The opportunity to join a growing company developing some of the most exciting technology in quantum computing.
• Meaningful responsibility from the outset, with opportunities to develop your skills, take on new challenges and grow your career as Aegiq expands.
• A friendly, collaborative and supportive working environment where different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued, and everyone is encouraged to contribute.

Specialist with a strong background spanning both Information Security and
Privacy compliance. This individual will deliver external audits and regulatory
examinations across security and privacy domains, working across multiple
jurisdictions and regulatory frameworks. The role demands someone who can
operate with equal confidence in a payments audit environment as in a DMA or
GDPR compliance assessment — applying domain-agnostic assurance methodology

supervisory authorities across all domains.

management, and report issuance

requirements to specific controls, evidence requirements, and testing procedures

preparation of management responses and corrective action plans

services, entities, and systems fall within scope

At Anaplan, we are a team of innovators focused on optimizing business decision-making through our leading AI-infused scenario planning and analysis platform so our customers can outpace their competition and the market.
What unites Anaplanners across teams and geographies is our collective commitment to our customers’ success and to our Winning Culture.
Our customers rank among the who’s who in the Fortune 50. Coca-Cola, LinkedIn, Adobe, LVMH and Bayer are just a few of the 2,400+ global companies who rely on our best-in-class platform.
Our Winning Culture is the engine that drives our teams of innovators. We champion diversity of thought and ideas, we behave like leaders regardless of title, we are committed to achieving ambitious goals, and we love celebrating our wins – big and small.
Supported by operating principles of being strategy-led, values-based and disciplined in execution, you’ll be inspired, connected, developed and rewarded here. Everything that makes you unique is welcome; join us and let’s build what’s next - together!
What you’ll be doing:
As a Security Engineer within the Security Operations team, you will help design, build, and continuously improve the technical capabilities that underpin how we detect, investigate, and respond to threats. You will work at the intersection of engineering and operations — helping turn security problems into scalable, automated solutions. Your core responsibilities will be to:
• Alert Investigation & Triage: Investigate and triage security alerts from across our detection tooling, analysing logs, endpoint, identity, cloud, and network telemetry to determine impact and root cause. Work alongside the wider SOC to escalate and resolve confirmed threats, document findings clearly, and feed what you learn back into detections, tuning, and automation.
• Incident Response & DFIR: Support the investigation and response to confirmed security incidents, applying digital forensics and incident response skills across endpoint, cloud, and identity data. Help with evidence collection and preservation, timeline reconstruction, containment, and root cause analysis, and contribute to post-incident reviews that turn lessons learned into improved detections and tooling.
• SIEM Engineering: Contribute to the engineering of our SIEM platform, including onboarding and normalising log sources, building and maintaining parsers, and supporting high-fidelity data pipelines that underpin detection and investigation. Help improve log coverage, data quality, and platform performance.
• Detection Engineering: Help develop and maintain a library of high-quality detections using a Detection as Code methodology — working with version control, peer review, and automated testing pipelines. Map detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework and contribute to improving coverage, precision, and resilience against evasion.
• AI-Augmented Security Operations: Help explore and apply AI and machine learning to enhance security operations capabilities — including alert triage, incident response acceleration, threat intelligence analysis, threat hunting, and the enrichment and prioritisation of detection content. Contribute to evaluating emerging AI tooling and embedding it responsibly into team workflows.
• Threat Intelligence Integration: Help consume and operationalise threat intelligence from internal and external sources, integrating indicators and adversary context into detection logic, response playbooks, and hunting activities. Work with threat intelligence feeds and platforms to support a timely and structured flow of actionable intelligence into security operations.
• Threat Hunting: Take part in proactive, hypothesis-driven threat hunts across the environment to identify attacker activity that evades existing detections. Document and share findings in a structured way, using hunt outcomes to inform and improve detection engineering and tooling.
What you’ll bring to the role:
We are looking for a technically capable security professional with hands-on experience in security operations. The ideal candidate will possess:
• Technical Security Experience: commercial experience in a security operations role, with a solid grounding in securing cloud-native environments and modern application stacks.
• Incident Response & Digital Forensics: Hands-on experience supporting security incident investigations, including evidence preservation, log and artifact analysis, timeline reconstruction, and root cause identification. Familiarity with forensic tooling and methodologies is highly sought after, as is experience contributing to post-incident reviews and translating findings into actionable improvements.
• Detection & Response Skills: Practical experience developing and tuning SIEM detections, writing threat hunting queries, and participating in incident response activities.
• SecOps Tooling: Hands-on knowledge of administering and operating core security operations tools, including SIEM platforms, EDR/XDR solutions, vulnerability scanners, and ticketing or case management systems. Experience integrating these tools to support detection, investigation, and response workflows.
• Threat Intelligence & Threat Hunting: Experience working with threat intelligence platforms and feeds, and integrating intelligence into security tooling, detection logic, and operational processes. A working knowledge of threat hunting methodologies and the ability to proactively identify indicators of compromise or attacker behaviour across the environment is highly desirable.
• Scripting & Automation: Proficiency in one or more scripting or programming languages (e.g. Python, Go, Bash) to build security tooling, automate workflows, and integrate security capabilities.
• Application Security Knowledge: Familiarity with secure development practices, OWASP top risks, and the ability to perform code reviews or work with developers to remediate security findings.
• Security Frameworks & Standards: Working knowledge of relevant security frameworks (e.g. NIST CSF, CIS Benchmarks, MITRE ATT&CK) and compliance standards such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001.
• Communication & Collaboration: Strong ability to articulate technical security risks and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and to work cross-functionally to deliver security outcomes.

You will lead complex investigations, perform forensic analysis, conduct threat hunting, and leverage intelligence to understand who we are up against and how they operate.

Act as technical lead on our security incidents, owning the investigation end-to-end, from triage and scoping through containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review

Work alongside IT, Engineering, Identity, Service Management, legal, privacy, and communications teams during major incidents, and with external incident response partners where needed
Rapidly assess emerging threats, zero-days and actively exploited vulnerabilities for real-world exposure across our environment, and drive preemptive response where needed
Lead proactive, hypothesis-led threat hunts informed by investigation findings, intelligence, and emerging tradecraft, and work with the SOC to turn the results into tested, high-fidelity detections
Produce internal threat reporting that translates what we're seeing in our environment, and across the threat landscape relevant to us, into clear assessments and actions for security teams and leadership
Contribute to our threat intelligence capability, including intelligence requirements and the sources and tooling that support them, keeping it directly connected to investigation, hunting, and detection work
Expand incident response playbooks, forensic procedures, and evidence handling standards, raise the standard of how we run complex investigations, and coach SOC analysts through live investigations
Design and run tabletop exercises for technical and executive audiences
Track post-incident remediation actions through to closure
Use AI as a core part of how you work, building and applying AI-assisted workflows and automation for evidence collection, enrichment, triage, and analysis, and integrating them with our security tooling

ABOUT THE JOB
As the Head of Talent Acquisition, EMEA, you own the build-out of Anduril's talent acquisition capability across
the EMEA region. Reporting to the Senior Director of Talent Acquisition and partnering closely with the Head of
Strategic Planning for Talent Acquisition, you are a key member of the TA Leadership team with a specific
mandate: geo-specific scaling. You own the in-country, site-specific, and division-specific hiring build-out across
EMEA, working in close partnership with the Head of Talent Acquisition, APAC and with each Divisional Head of
TA who is adding headcount into your region.
This is not a divisional leadership seat. You are not embedded in any single business unit's leadership team; you
are the connective tissue across all of them for one geography. Multiple divisions will be scaling into EMEA at
once, often into the same countries and talent pools, and your job is to make sure their combined demand lands
on a coherent, compliant, and well-resourced regional hiring capability, rather than five uncoordinated efforts
competing for the same candidates.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
Regional Strategy and Build-Out
• Define and execute Anduril's EMEA talent acquisition strategy, directly informed by the combined hiring
demand of every division scaling into the region.
• Own EMEA hiring outcomes (time-to-fill, quality, acceptance rates) as the single accountable owner for
regional delivery.
• Own EMEA hiring governance, compliance, and workforce planning across the region's countries, each with
distinct labor law, works council, and candidate market dynamics.
• Develop EMEA hiring playbooks, and partner with the Head of Talent Acquisition, APAC to share what's
working across both regions rather than each building in isolation.
• Partner with the Head of Strategic Planning for Talent Acquisition to evaluate where EMEA needs additional
in-country or sub-regional leadership as demand grows (e.g., a dedicated UK or Germany lead), and help
build the case and the structure for it.
Cross-Divisional Partnership and Prioritization
• Serve as the senior talent advisor to EMEA-based business leaders and to every Divisional Head of TA adding
headcount into the region, synthesizing what could otherwise be five disconnected divisional views into one
coherent regional talent picture.
• Partner with in-region recruiting resources and EMEA business leaders to ensure the regional model reflects
on-the-ground reality, not just headquarters assumptions.
• Act as the tie-breaker when multiple divisions' hiring demand converges on the same country, site, or talent
pool with more need than the region can serve at once, using an objective, business-impact-driven
framework.
• Drive continuous improvement through data and feedback loops, standardizing what should be consistent
across EMEA while preserving the flexibility each country and division genuinely needs.
Operational Cohesion with Peer Regions
• Partner closely with the Head of Strategic Planning for Talent Acquisition, a peer, not a manager, who is
accountable for cross-regional cohesion, shared playbooks, and consistency of operating rhythm across
EMEA and APAC.
• Loop in the Head of Strategic Planning early on build-out choices (tooling, process, governance) so that
EMEA and APAC remain coherent for divisions scaling into both regions.
• Resolve cross-regional alignment issues collaboratively, escalating to the Senior Director of Talent
Acquisition only when peer alignment can't be reached.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
• 10+ years of progressive TA experience, including demonstrated success building or scaling EMEA hiring
specifically, not just supporting it from a distance.
• Deep understanding of EMEA labor markets, employment law, works councils, and compliance
considerations across the region's key countries.
• Proven experience designing and executing an end-to-end regional talent acquisition strategy.
• Demonstrated ability to lead and influence across a matrixed structure, partnering with multiple Divisional
Heads of TA and business leaders who do not report to you.
• Strong track record of driving continuous improvement through data-driven decision making, with the ability
to report regional hiring outcomes credibly to Global TA Leadership.
• Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to reconcile competing divisional demand
for the same regional capacity and drive consensus without formal authority.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
perience partnering with or building out in-country resources as part of a broader regional build.
• Experience building a regional operating model that other regions (e.g., APAC) have adapted or could adapt.
• Prior experience as part of a broader transition from a U.S.-led to a localized, globally scalable TA model.
• Experience in defense, aerospace, or other hardware and software-intensive industries.
• A background in or strong familiarity with BizOps, program management, or business strategy.

job_description:
National Security Consulting Opportunities (eDV Cleared)
Location: Gloucester or Manchester | This role normally requires four days per week on site, with five days per week on site likely depending on the project.
Grade: GG08–GG12 
Quick Overview
 
Bring your consulting experience to challenges that contribute to the safety and prosperity of the UK.
 
We are recruiting across several consulting disciplines, including:
 
Business Consulting
Business Analysis
Technical Consulting
Security Consulting
Business Change and Transformation
 
You could help customers clarify a strategic challenge, understand business and user needs, examine technical or security considerations, or translate complex evidence into practical recommendations. Depending on your experience and assignment, you may support work from initial analysis and business justification through to design, planning, implementation and adoption.
 
You will work alongside customers and multidisciplinary teams, building your expertise while contributing to work with a clear National Security purpose.
 
National Security in Digital Intelligence
 
Digital Intelligence brings together consulting, technology, cyber, data, engineering and operational expertise to support important National Security outcomes.
 
Our consultants help customers understand complex situations, make informed decisions and deliver sustainable change. This can mean bringing structure to an emerging problem, connecting operational and technical perspectives, examining security implications or helping an organisation move from strategy to implementation.
 
The work can involve ambiguity, competing priorities and incomplete information. You will be supported by colleagues from different professional backgrounds who can test your thinking, contribute specialist knowledge and help the team reach a well-evidenced outcome.
You will have the opportunity to build consulting breadth while developing specialist expertise relevant to your profession and career goals.
 
Your SubAccount
 
Consulting opportunities exist across all four National Security SubAccounts. Each addresses a different area of the mission and needs people who can understand complex environments, bring together different perspectives and turn evidence into effective action.
Your experience, professional discipline and the needs of the available work will help determine the most appropriate SubAccount.
 
Core Machine
Core Machine focuses on the underlying digital capabilities, platforms and services that enable wider National Security outcomes.
 
Consultants may help customers understand business and user needs, define requirements, examine existing services, evaluate options or plan organisational and technical change. Assignments may involve connecting strategic objectives with the processes, operating models and capabilities needed to achieve them.
 
Business Consultants and Business Analysts could help clarify outcomes, map processes, define requirements and develop business cases. Technical Consultants could help connect organisational needs with technical options and delivery considerations. Security Consultants could help ensure that relevant risks and security requirements are considered as capabilities develop.
 
This environment may suit you if you are interested in how strong digital foundations enable complex organisations and mission teams to operate effectively.
 
Cyber Engineering
Cyber Engineering brings together cyber and engineering expertise to help customers understand and address evolving security challenges.
 
Consultants help connect operational priorities, organisational needs, security considerations and technical delivery. Work may include understanding a cyber-related problem, analysing requirements, assessing risks, supporting transformation or helping stakeholders make evidence-based decisions in technically complex environments.
 
Business Consultants and Business Analysts could examine the organisational implications of cyber change, define needs and support implementation. Technical Consultants could help customers assess technical options, dependencies and delivery approaches. Security Consultants could contribute specialist analysis and advice to help teams understand and manage security risks.
 
Deep cyber expertise will be important for some opportunities, but it will not be essential for every consulting role. Requirements will reflect the specific assignment and advertised grade.
 
Emergent Mission & Tech
Emergent Mission & Tech considers developing mission needs and how new or evolving technologies could help address them.
 
Consulting assignments may begin with an emerging problem rather than a fixed requirement. You could help identify the outcome that matters, investigate user and organisational needs, test assumptions, evaluate options or turn an early concept into an actionable strategy.
Business Consultants and Business Analysts could structure the problem, gather evidence and develop requirements or investment cases. Technical Consultants could help assess the feasibility, implications and potential value of different technologies. Security Consultants could help teams consider risks and security requirements while ideas are still being explored and shaped.
 
This environment may suit people who are comfortable working with uncertainty, adapting their approach as evidence develops and bringing together business, operational, technical and security perspectives.
 
Mission Operations
Mission Operations focuses on the people, processes, services and capabilities that support effective operational outcomes.
 
Consultants may help customers understand how work is currently performed, identify barriers and design practical improvements. Assignments could include service and process analysis, requirements definition, organisational change, implementation support or helping teams introduce new capabilities into an operational environment.
 
Business Consultants and Business Analysts could examine processes, user needs and operating models. Technical Consultants could connect operational requirements with technical possibilities and constraints. Security Consultants could help ensure that change is informed by an appropriate understanding of risk and security.
 
The emphasis is on making change workable for the people and teams who will use it, while remaining focused on the wider mission outcome.
 
What You Will Be Doing
 
Your responsibilities will depend on your consulting discipline, experience and assignment. You may be involved in:
 
Working with customers and colleagues to understand strategic, operational, business, technical or security challenges
Gathering and analysing information from stakeholders, users, documents, systems and existing processes
Defining problems, requirements, desired outcomes and measures of success
Mapping processes, services, capabilities, dependencies or stakeholder needs
Bringing together business, technical, operational and security perspectives
Developing strategies, options, recommendations and business cases supported by clear evidence
Examining organisational structures and operating models to identify opportunities for improvement
Evaluating technical approaches and explaining their organisational or operational implications
Identifying risks, assumptions, constraints and dependencies
Helping customers understand security considerations and make proportionate, evidence-based decisions
Planning and facilitating workshops, interviews and collaborative working sessions
Producing concise reports, briefings, presentations and decision-support materials
Supporting change from initial analysis through planning, implementation and adoption
Working with multidisciplinary teams that may include consultants, engineers, architects, cyber specialists, delivery professionals and operational subject-matter experts
Contributing to the Digital Intelligence consulting community by sharing knowledge, developing professional practice and supporting colleagues
 
At more senior grades, responsibilities may also include:
 
Shaping consulting assignments and agreeing appropriate approaches
Leading engagements, workstreams or multidisciplinary teams
Advising senior customer stakeholders
Managing consulting outcomes, risks and delivery commitments
Coaching and developing other consultants
Supporting the continued development of consulting capability and methods
 
Essential Skills
 
We are interested in the capability you can demonstrate, rather than one prescribed professional background or career path.
 
You will need experience in consulting, business analysis, technical consulting, security consulting, business change or another relevant advisory discipline.
 
You should also be able to demonstrate that you can:
 
Understand complex problems and turn them into structured analysis
Gather information from different sources and identify the issues that matter
Adapt your approach when requirements, priorities or evidence change
Develop clear findings, options or recommendations supported by evidence
Explain complex information in a way that meets the needs of different audiences
Build constructive working relationships across organisational and professional boundaries
Offer objective advice while understanding customer priorities and constraints
Work independently and contribute effectively within a multidisciplinary team
 
Depending on the specific opportunity, useful experience may include:
 
Business analysis, requirements definition or process mapping
Strategy development and strategic advisory work
Business change, transformation or implementation
Technical consulting or technology-enabled change
Cybersecurity, information assurance or security risk
Business-case and investment-case development
Operating-model, organisational or service design
Digital transformation
Policy or regulatory advice
Workshop design and facilitation
Public-sector consulting
Briefing and advising senior stakeholders
Working with UK government organisations
Supporting complex programmes or projects
 
You do not need to demonstrate every area listed above. Your skills will be assessed proportionately against the consulting discipline, assignment and grade under consideration.
 
Security Clearance
 
Due to the security requirements of this role, applicants must hold a current and active Enhanced Developed Vetting (eDV) clearance to be considered for this opportunity.

Our Consumer Products & Retail practice is looking for an experienced Senior Manager or Director to join the team and help our clients deliver complex, business-critical transformation.
We are seeking a highly motivated consulting leader with a strong track record of designing and delivering large-scale transformation programmes within the consumer products and retail sectors. This could include experience across supply chain transformation, S&OP, planning and forecasting, ERP-enabled transformation, or operating model design and implementation.
This is a broad transformation leadership role rather than a position focused on a single functional specialism. The right person will combine strong consulting and programme leadership capabilities with the commercial confidence to lead client relationships, manage complex engagements, and identify opportunities to deepen and grow existing accounts.
Candidates may have built their career entirely within consulting or combined consulting with relevant industry experience. However, substantial consulting experience and a clear understanding of how to lead clients through complex transformation are essential.
What we are looking for
You will be a pragmatic transformation leader who is comfortable moving between strategic thinking and the realities of implementation. You will understand what it takes to mobilise and deliver complex programmes, engage senior client stakeholders, and create alignment across business and technology teams.
You do not need to be a pure business development or new-logo origination specialist. However, you must be comfortable owning senior client relationships, leading the day-to-day development of accounts, and identifying opportunities to broaden our impact with existing clients.
You will also bring enough depth in consumer products or retail to understand the commercial and operational context in which clients are transforming, while retaining the breadth to work across different types of transformation challenge.
What you will be doing
• Lead complex transformation engagements for consumer products and retail clients, taking responsibility for successful delivery from initial design through to implementation.

• Provide clear leadership to multidisciplinary project teams, creating an environment in which consultants can perform effectively and develop their capabilities.
• Manage programme risks, dependencies, budgets, resources, governance, and senior stakeholder expectations.
• Support business development activity through proposal development, solution design, client presentations, and the expansion of existing relationships.
• Contribute to the continued development of our Consumer Products & Retail practice, including its propositions, delivery capabilities, market profile, and people.
Your skills and experience
• Significant experience within consulting, with a strong track record of leading complex transformation engagements for consumer products or retail clients.
• Experience operating at Senior Manager, Director, or an equivalent level within a recognised consulting organisation.
• Demonstrable expertise in one or more of the following areas:
• Supply chain transformation
• Sales and operations planning, or S&OP
• Demand, supply, or integrated business planning
• Forecasting and planning transformation
• ERP-enabled business transformation
• Operating model design and implementation
• Complex programme leadership
• Experience leading major transformation programmes from strategy and design through to implementation and business adoption.
• A strong understanding of how business processes, operating models, data, technology, organisation design, and change management come together within a successful transformation.
• Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary consulting teams and manage multiple workstreams within complex client environments.
• Strong client engagement and account management skills, with the confidence to work with senior client stakeholders and manage important day-to-day relationships.
• Evidence of growing or expanding existing client accounts by identifying additional client needs and converting them into relevant opportunities.
• Strong commercial judgement, including experience managing engagement economics, delivery quality, scope, risk, and client expectations.
• The ability to communicate complex transformation topics clearly and credibly to both business and technology stakeholders.
• Excellent problem-solving, facilitation, influencing, and stakeholder management capabilities.
• A collaborative leadership style and a strong commitment to coaching and developing consulting talent.
• Industry experience gained before, during, or after a consulting career would be valuable, but candidates must bring substantial and current consulting capability.

Company Description
Bicycle Therapeutics is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing a novel class of medicines, referred to as Bicycle® molecules, for diseases that are underserved by existing therapeutics. Bicycle molecules are fully synthetic short peptides constrained with small molecule scaffolds to form two loops that stabilize their structural geometry. This constraint facilitates target binding with high affinity and selectivity, making Bicycle® molecules attractive candidates for drug development. The company is evaluating nuzafatide pevedotin (formerly BT5528), a Bicycle® Drug Conjugate (BDC®) targeting EphA2, a historically undruggable target; a pipeline of Bicycle® Radioconjugates (BRCs) and imaging agents; zelenectide pevedotin (formerly BT8009), a BDC® targeting Nectin-4, a well-validated tumor antigen; and, through various partnerships, the use of Bicycle® technology to develop therapies to treat diseases in a range of therapeutic areas.
Bicycle Therapeutics is headquartered in Cambridge, UK, with many key functions and members of its leadership team located in Lexington, Massachusetts, USA. For more information, visit bicycletherapeutics.com
Culture is key and all Bicycle employees actively embrace and role model our company values:
We are Adventurous. We believe it’s the way to deliver extraordinary results for our patients. We are Dedicated to our Mission. You can’t change the world if you don’t have determination.
We are One Team. We only succeed when we work together.

This is a fully onsite position based at our Cambridge, UK facilities. Given the collaborative and laboratory-based nature of this role, daily onsite presence is required to work closely with our teams, access our cutting-edge resources, and drive our science and operations forward.
Job Description
Are you driven by scientific curiosity and passionate about pushing the boundaries of drug discovery?
As a Senior Scientist in Biophysics, your mission is to apply deep biophysical binding characterization expertise—predominantly leveraging Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR)—to interrogate novel Bicycle® molecules, unpick complex molecular interactions, and triage screening cascades. Embedded within our innovative Platform Technology group, you will lead assay design, champion exploratory methods, and deliver decisive, high-integrity data that powers therapeutic discovery programs from target engagement to candidate selection.
Responsibilities
Scientific Strategy & Binding Characterization
Design, optimize, and perform robust biophysical binding assays (predominantly SPR) for the kinetic and affinity characterization of Bicycle® peptides, conjugates, and molecular targets.
Deliver high-quality, reproducible data with in-depth analysis and insightful kinetic interpretation to triage screening cascades and inform lead optimization.
Drive exploratory investigations and tailor bespoke biophysical assay formats for novel and historically challenging therapeutic targets.
Biophysical Innovation & Laboratory Excellence
Explore, implement, and validate orthogonal biophysical technologies (e.g., Carterra high-throughput SPR, AlphaScreen, DSF, FP, HTRF, or mass photometry) to broaden the lab's screening capabilities.
Partner with computational and structural biology teams to integrate biophysical datasets into Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD) and AI-driven platform workflows.
Champion laboratory excellence, maintaining rigorous data integrity standards, electronic notebook documentation, and contributing to ongoing operational enhancements.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence
Serve as a key biophysical subject matter expert across multidisciplinary project teams, communicating technical findings clearly to diverse stakeholders.

Act as a collaborative role model and mentor, supporting the development of less experienced colleagues and fostering an inclusive, high-performing research environment

Royal National Institute for the Blind – London, UK What degree would I be studying? We welcome people into our team with a broad range of experience. However for this particular opening, we would be very keen to hear from students who have studied (or still studying) one of the following degrees;

Communication:But it’s not about the tools – our focus is on being able to communicate the results to our clients across key technical areas such as noise break-in, internal sound transmission, reverberation control, building services noise, structural dynamics, audio-visual design, public address and voice alarm, and vibration. A key focus is engagement. An example of this is our work with the prestige gym chain Equinox which often retrofit their facilities inside existing listed buildings. Our relationship allows us to understand the unique aspirations of each site, and tailor a dynamic, vibration isolation and sound insulation solution to each development based on the specific activities proposed. Challenge: We’re excited and motivated by the challenging, complex and difficult. Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. More about the role:
We are looking for a highly organised, proactive and adaptable Executive Assistant to join our EMEA HQ team based from London. This is a pivotal role, working closely with two senior leaders at the heart of our business and acting as a trusted partner across a fast-paced, complex and highly connected environment. You will bring significant Executive Assistant experience, ideally gained within an international, matrixed and professional services organisation. You will be confident working at pace, managing competing priorities and handling sensitive information with complete discretion. The role requires someone who is calm, well organised, highly detail-oriented and able to build trusted relationships with stakeholders at all levels. This is a visible and varied role requiring excellent judgement, strong communication skills and a positive, solutions-focused approach. Experience working within a global network organisation would be a distinct advantage. Please note that this role requires some office-based working.

Manage complex and fast-moving diaries ensuring meetings are well coordinated, prioritised and prepared for effectively. Coordinate internal and external meetings, including senior leadership sessions, client meetings, board-level engagements and key business forums. Handle high volumes of communication with professionalism and discretion, prioritising responses and escalating urgent or sensitive matters where appropriate. Arrange all aspects of domestic and international travel, including flights, visas, accommodation, itineraries and associated logistics. Act as a key point of contact for senior internal and external stakeholders, representing the business with confidence, warmth and professionalism. Build strong relationships across the leadership team and wider business, ensuring the two key stakeholders are well supported and connected. Support onboarding for senior hires and help coordinate company-wide meetings, leadership sessions, events and key cultural moments. Work collaboratively with colleagues across EMEA HQ teams and the wider EA team to support new business activity, marketing initiatives, senior recruitment and the smooth running of day-to-day operations. Experience that contributes to success:
Significant experience as an Executive Assistant or Senior Personal Assistant, ideally supporting C-suite or senior leadership in a fast-paced, complex environment. Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, anticipate needs and deliver work with accuracy and pace. Complete discretion and sound judgement when handling confidential, commercially sensitive or personal information. Strong communication skills, with the confidence to engage effectively with colleagues, clients and stakeholders at every level. A proactive, positive and can-do approach, with the ability to stay calm, flexible and solutions-focused under pressure. Strong attention to detail, combined with the ability to understand the bigger picture and operate with professionalism and maturity. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Outlook, PowerPoint, Word and Excel. Experience or confidence working with social media platforms would be advantageous. Confident working with AI tools and digital resources to enhance productivity, streamline ways of working and support high-quality, efficient delivery. #LI-SF2

The Head of Pre Sales Solutions will be responsible for building, developing and leading Captify's demand side Client Strategy function, with a particular focus on Presales, RFPs, pitches, and sales enablement.

Develop and lead the Presales function

• Set KPIs for the function and report on its impact on pipeline, win rates and revenue.

• Design and deliver a sales enablement programme that equips the commercial team to sell Captify's full proposition with confidence.

• Onboard new commercial hires on Captify's offering, positioning and competitive landscape.
• Keep enablement materials current as products, market conditions and client needs evolve.

• Craft clear, compelling narratives that connect Captify's search intelligence, insights and media solutions to client and agency business objectives.
• Develop strategic solutions for priority clients and agencies, identifying opportunities to grow existing partnerships.
• Stay close to market, industry and competitor trends, turning them into points of view and thought leadership that strengthen our positioning.
• Partner with Insights to bring data-led stories and audience insight into pitches and client conversations.
Cross-functional leadership
• Act as the bridge between Sales, Marketing, Product, Insights and senior leadership, aligning teams around client needs and commercial priorities.
• Feed client and market feedback into Product to inform roadmap and proposition development.
• Work with Marketing to keep positioning, messaging and sales materials consistent.
• Influence senior stakeholders and help shape commercial strategy at leadership level.

• Significant experience in presales, solutions consulting or commercial strategy within ad tech, media, a media agency or a data business.
• A track record of leading complex RFPs and winning pitches with major advertisers and agencies.
• Experience building or scaling a team or function, ideally from early foundations, including hiring and developing people.

• A collaborative approach, with experience working closely with Sales, Product, Marketing and Insights teams.
• Experience designing sales enablement or training programmes is a strong plus.

• You have built strong relationships across Sales, Marketing, Product, Insights and leadership, and understand how Presales works today.
• You have reviewed recent RFPs and pitches, identified what's working and where the gaps are, and shared a clear plan for the function.
• You are already leading key strategic opportunities and making a visible difference to their quality.

• A clear operating model is in place, with a defined engagement process, prioritisation criteria and consistent templates for RFPs and pitches.

• The first phase of a sales enablement programme has launched, and new joiners are onboarded through it.

• Pre Sales is seen by Sales as a critical, trusted partner, and is involved early in priority opportunities.
• You can show measurable impact, such as improved win rates, larger deal sizes or faster RFP turnaround.
• The team is resourced and structured to scale, with clear roles, KPIs and ways of working.
• Client insight from the function is regularly informing Product and Marketing priorities.

Job Purpose
To manage a caseload of both litigated and non-litigated personal injury claims, with a primary focus on Road Traffic Accident (RTA) matters. This includes handling complex cases that have exited the portal, typically fast track or lower-value multi-track claims. These cases often involve overlapping injuries, significant pre-existing conditions, stayed proceedings, and/or challenging client circumstances. The role requires progressing such claims to a satisfactory resolution, with a key emphasis on transitioning them from portal to fast track and/or multi-track stages, while maximising both damages and recoverable costs. Key Responsibilities
• Maintain regular and proactive communication with both lay and insurance clients throughout the lifecycle of each claim. • Build rapport through calls and meetings to ensure consistent service delivery and foster insurer loyalty to the firm. • Verify the authenticity and validity of claims by engaging with clients on complex or sensitive files. • Develop strong client relationships to minimise complaints and enhance the firm’s reputation. • Keep insurers fully informed of claim progress to mitigate potential exposure and maximise savings. • Ensure all heads of claim are discussed with clients from the outset and revisited throughout the claim. • Collect all relevant documentation from clients at the earliest opportunity. • Obtain medical reports and progress claims efficiently and within appropriate timeframes. • Discuss liability and quantum offers with relevant parties, prioritising telephone communication over written correspondence where possible. • Advise clients on contributory negligence issues as they arise. • Prioritise and manage daily incoming correspondence, addressing urgent matters promptly and handling remaining items in order of importance and productivity. • Drive portal claims into Fast Track and/or Multi-Track, maximising damages and recoverable costs. • Deliver excellent client service and secure positive outcomes. • Support junior or less experienced team members with client, referrer, agency, and procedural queries. • Collaborate with the Team Leader and/or Head of Department to take on more contentious files under supervision, expanding personal expertise. • Where applicable, increase the number of Multi-Track cases within the caseload to further develop professional experience. Experience & Knowledge
• A Solicitor or CILEX qualified experience in the personal injury field technical Fast Track claims • Portal experience is essential as a number of the cases referred into the team are stayed and require applications to lift or extend the stay. • Experience of dealing with complex claims or claims which are technical in nature • A proven track record of running a successful fast and/or multi track caseload within a personal injury environment • Excellent client care and analytical skills, to include providing written and oral advice in a clear concise manner • Have a good working knowledge of the CPR and/or and other relevant case law and/or legislation and progressing defences in a timely manner in accordance with the CPR. • The ability to liaise and build up a rapport by using effective communication with all external agencies during the life of a claim including medical agencies, investigators, barristers etc. • The ability to create and foster a “can do” culture to raise efficiency and productivity • Good IT skills with a sound working knowledge of Solcase or a similar case management system and essential MS Office knowledge • Excellent time management and organisational skills, with a calm and methodical approach to work, and a flexible and adaptable attitude to resolving issues

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
CircuitHub builds circuit boards on demand, every order different. Each day thousands of decisions are made: which orders run on which machines, which parts to buy and when, what to promise a customer and what to charge. You'll build the models behind those decisions.

- Price and promise. Estimate what an order really costs in labour, machine time and parts, and help set prices and lead times that win work and make money.
- Buy smarter. Decide what parts and consumables to stock, when to order them, and how much risk of a shortage to accept.

job_title: Financial Services Regulatory Lawyer - Senior Vice President
job_description:
Are you looking for a career move that will put you at the heart of a global financial institution? Then bring your skills to Citi’s Financial Services Regulatory Legal team.
By joining Citi, you will become part of a global organisation whose mission is to serve as a trusted partner to our clients by responsibly providing financial services that enable growth and economic progress.
Team/Role Overview
As Senior Regulatory Counsel, you will serve as a trusted legal advisor on the laws and regulations shaping Citi's wholesale markets and trading businesses across the UK, EU, and beyond. Based within Citi's Financial Services Regulatory Legal team ("FSR Legal"), you will partner with senior stakeholders across trading, operations, technology, and compliance to interpret complex regulatory change, including MiFID II/MiFIR, EMIR, and SFTR reforms. This role offers the opportunity to lead high-profile regulatory transformation programs at the intersection of law, policy, and market structure.
What you’ll do
• Act as senior regulatory counsel, advising business stakeholders, trading desks, and legal entity management teams on UK, EU, and cross-border wholesale markets regulations, including MiFID II/MiFIR, EMIR, and SFTR.
• Lead the legal workstream for major regulatory change programs, including the FCA's UK MiFIR transaction reporting reform and the EU MiFIR Review.
• Guide legal readiness for revised Regulatory Technical Standards, including RTS 22, RTS 24, and RTS 25, as well as EMIR Refit requirements.
• Assess the extraterritorial application of US Dodd-Frank rules alongside UK and EU regulatory frameworks.
• Partner with trading, operations, technology, and compliance teams to translate complex regulatory requirements into practical, commercially sound guidance.
• Counsel the business on regulatory considerations tied to acquisitions, divestitures, internal reorganizations, and the structuring of new products and transactions.
• Manage the resolution of regulatory violations and significant compliance issues, escalating matters where necessary.
• Represent Citi in engagements with financial services regulators on authorization, supervisory inquiries, and remediation matters.
What we’ll need from you
Required Qualifications & Skills
• Relevant legal experience in financial services.
• Developed this experience within a leading international law firm, a global investment bank or financial institution, a regulatory authority such as the FCA, ESMA, CBI, AMF, or CFTC, or a leading regulatory consulting practice at Director or Senior Manager level.
• Demonstrates strong understanding of wholesale financial services regulations, including MiFID II/MiFIR, EMIR, Dodd-Frank, and Market Abuse Regulation.
• Advises on complex regulatory implementation projects, multi-stakeholder initiatives, and regulatory inquiries, analyzing technical standards and legislative text to produce clear, practical legal advice.
• Works effectively within a specialised legal team, partnering with peer subject leads and cross-functional stakeholders.
• Communicates and drafts with clarity and confidence, advising senior stakeholders while managing competing priorities across multi-year change projects and daily advisory demands.
• Holds qualification as a solicitor in the Republic of Ireland, England & Wales, or Northern Ireland, or is admitted to practice in the State of New York or another common law or civil law jurisdiction.
Beneficial Skills & Qualifications
• Practical exposure to or strong aptitude for transaction reporting under RTS 22, trade reporting, or market transparency rules.
• A law degree obtained in the Republic of Ireland, the United Kingdom, the United States, or another common law or civil law jurisdiction.
This position is open to regulatory lawyers, derivatives counsel, trading advisory specialists, ex-regulators, or regulatory consulting professionals who have a strong foundation in wholesale markets regulation and a strong interest or background in transaction reporting, transparency, and regulatory implementation.
What we can offer you
By joining Citi, you will not only be part of a business casual workplace with a hybrid working model (up to 2 days working at home per week), but also receive a competitive base salary (which is annually reviewed) and enjoy a whole host of additional benefits that support you (and your family)to be well, live well and save well. Alongside these benefits Citi is committed to ensuring our workplace is where everyone feels comfortable coming to work as their whole self every day.  We want the best talent around the world to be energised to join us, motivated to stay, and empowered to thrive.
Sounds like Citi has everything you need? Then apply to discover the true extent of your capabilities. ------------------------------------------------------

job_description:

In this role, you will serve as the core Subject Matter Expert for Client and Account data flows, end-to-end data lineage, transaction processing, and data governance. You will bridge the gap between business stakeholders, operations, technology teams, and data engineering to ensure data accuracy, optimal pipeline design, compliance, and actionable business intelligence.

• Define critical data elements (CDEs), data ownership models, business glossaries, and metadata catalogs for the Client and Account data domains.
What we’ll need from you
• Total Experience: 10+ years of experience as a Data Analyst, Business Analyst, Data SME, or Technical Data Consultant in enterprise environments (preferably Financial Services, Banking, FinTech, or Consulting).
• Technical Mastery (SQL): Expert-level proficiency in SQL (complex joins, aggregations, window functions, query optimization, indexing, and debugging data pipelines).
