Role Overview
Head of Infrastructure | The Bower, 207-211, Old St, Tower, London EC1V 9NR | Four days in office, Wednesdays remote
You'll own Fresha's cloud infrastructure and the teams that run it: Cloud Infrastructure, Delivery Platform, On-Call Automation and Reliability, and Performance Engineering. You'll report to the VP of Architecture and work closely with engineering leadership, Security and Data.
This isn't a classic DevOps role. We want a software engineer who chose infrastructure. You treat the platform as a product, you build systems that remove duplicated effort and low-impact work, and you build security into the design instead of reviewing it at the end.
Our product teams own their services in production, including their on-call. Your teams build the platform that makes that possible: AWS, our Kubernetes clusters on EKS, Terraform modules, CI/CD, paging, SLO tooling, and the AI agents that triage an alert before a human wakes up. You decide what goes on the golden path, and you make the tough calls when a team wants a one-off.
We want someone with strong opinions who can defend them in writing and in a room, and who changes their mind when the data says so. The cloud infrastructure budget is yours, and you lead the cost savings across our infrastructure. You work closely with Security and your product engineering peers to set the direction together.
We use AI as much as we can. Every engineer gets Claude/Codex/etc from day one, and we're building autonomous agents for SRE and security work. You'd decide how far we take that in production.
How We Build
• Production first: We have no pre-production environments. We test locally, validate in CI, ship behind feature flags, and hold a high quality bar. We ship with confidence because the platform makes it safe.
• Unix philosophy: Each service does one thing well behind a clear interface, and complexity stays at the edges. We optimise for rate of change: an engineer with one year of experience should be able to make a change quickly.
• Optional adoption, mandatory value: Teams choose their tools. Platform features win by being better, not by force. Only security and compliance are non-negotiable.
• Automate first, document second: A check that blocks the merge beats a page nobody reads. We still write down context and decisions, for people and for AI.
• Independent teams: Tribes own their code, deployments, on-call and roadmaps. The platform gives them what they need without waiting on anyone.
What You'll Do
Direction
• Set, present and execute the infrastructure strategy: what we build, what we buy, and what we stop doing.
• Own the golden path: clusters, networking, Terraform modules, CI/CD and observability. Make the right way the easy way.
• Own the cloud infrastructure budget and the vendor relationships. Lead the cost savings, know our cost per booking, and move it in the right direction.
• Keep production first safe as we grow: fast CI, feature flags, and fast rollback.
Reliability and security
• Own the availability of the shared platform and the SLOs for the services your teams run.
• Get the platform ready for seasonal peaks, with load tests and capacity plans.
• Own the disaster recovery plan and run the exercises. Set recovery targets with the business, test them for real, and fix what the exercise shows.
• Get the infrastructure ready to take Fresha multi-region: networking, deployments, observability and security across regions.
• Build security into the platform: least-privilege IAM, secrets, network policy, supply chain, and base-image patching with deadlines we meet.
• Lead the response when the platform causes an incident, and make sure the postmortem actions get done.
Hands-on
• Review designs and infrastructure changes, and challenge them when they're wrong.
• Write code when the team needs it: a prototype, a tool, a fix during an incident.
• Shape how AI agents work in production: what they can touch, what they must ask about, and how we audit them.
People and delivery
• Lead the team leads and engineers across London, Warsaw and Pristina. Hire, grow, and hold the bar. You set the tone.
• Run the infrastructure roadmap like a product: clear priorities, small increments, regular updates, and a clear no when something doesn't make the cut.
Our stack: AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka and Postgres. Services in Ruby, Elixir and TypeScript behind a federated GraphQL layer, and Go for internal tooling.
What We're Looking For
• Software engineer first: You've built and shipped production software in at least one general-purpose language. You can read a service's code to find out why it falls over.
• Cloud depth: You've run AWS and Kubernetes in production at scale. You know networking, IAM and infrastructure as code well.
• Security: You design with threat models, least privilege and secrets management from the start. You've taken a platform through a security audit.
• Reliability: SLOs, error budgets, incident command and capacity planning.
• Disaster recovery and multi-region: You've owned a disaster recovery plan and run the exercises, not only documented them. You've built cloud infrastructure across more than one region, including networking, traffic routing and failover.
• Leadership: 10+ years in engineering, with 4+ years leading infrastructure, platform or SRE teams. You've led other leads, and you've hired well.
• Opinionated: You have a clear view on how infrastructure should work, and you can explain it to an engineer, a product lead and the CFO.
• Communication: You write RFCs and strategy docs that people read and act on. You align teams through influence, not only through authority.
• Product and delivery basics: You run a roadmap, cut scope, track outcomes, and keep stakeholders informed without being chased.
• Bonus: Postgres at scale, Kafka, or LLM agents in production.
This isn't the role for you if you want to manage people without touching the technology, or if you see infrastructure as a ticket queue.
At Fresha, we value passion and potential as much as specific skills. If you're enthusiastic and eager to learn, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every listed requirement.

Job Description Summary

The role is for a Staff Power Systems Engineer in GE Vernova’s Wide Area Monitoring, Protection and Control (WAMPAC) Centre of Excellence in Edinburgh.

• Fluent in English and be able to communicate effectively over teleconference and in face-to-face meetings.
• Must be a fast learner, with a willingness to develop knowledge in new areas and with an ability to conduct robust research.

At Genomics England, we’re looking for a Full Stack Software Engineer with a demonstrable track record of delivering and owning backend software, alongside experience developing user-facing applications, and a passion for making a difference in genomics and healthcare.

• Expertise in Python and the ability to create scalable solutions.
• Expertise in JavaScript, alongside a strong understanding of frontend development and a passion for delivering an optimal user experience.
• Experience working with AWS and serverless architectures.
• Experience working with relational databases and SQL, ideally Postgres.
• Experience designing, developing and consuming REST APIs.
• Familiarity with agile methodologies and test-driven development.

Senior Product Designer, Knowledge Graph
This is a remote position based in Ireland. 
The Opportunity:
As a Senior Product Designer at Grafana Labs, you will join a growing Product Design organization of more than 25 designers, researchers, engineers, and design leaders distributed across six continents. You will work within a 100% remote R&D organization, so strong, proactive remote communication, collaboration, facilitation, and relationship building skills will be essential to your success.
As Senior Product Designer for Grafana Cloud’s Knowledge Graph, you'll design experiences for the context layer of Grafana Cloud that powers our entity graph, entity catalog and RCA workbench. Knowledge Graph automatically discovers services, infrastructure, and databases from the telemetry teams already have, maps how they depend on each other, and runs anomaly detection. This gives engineers, SREs, and their agents an up to date picture of their systems. We want anyone to be able to understand a system and resolve an incident faster, without writing queries or maintaining alert rules, not just the one person who happens to know it best.
Over time, you will develop deep expertise in your product area and associated customer and user personas, use cases, and workflows, which will enable you to design tailored, role-driven experiences. • Enabling customers to easily understand and explore how their systems connect to each other. Find clear, simple ways to show complex, constantly-changing information without overwhelming the user
• Translate research and data to experiences that are easy to digest and break down complexity
• Tailor the experience to different target audiences, covering multiple user perspectives
• Work cross-functionally with peers and leaders in engineering, product management, technical writing, and GTM functions, as well as other members of the Product Design team
• Prioritise for delivering impact while balancing business priorities, customer wishes and technical considerations 
• Document user needs and pain points, design directions, UX trade-offs, and detailed designs for specific features and enhancements
• Execute research and contribute to quantitative and qualitative research initiatives with researchers, cross-functional collaborators, customers, and members of the Grafana user community

• 7+ years of relevant design experience working on B2B/enterprise software products, ideally designing tools and services for developers or other highly technical users
• A portfolio of effective designs for complex products delivered in a fast-paced environment
• Experience running qualitative research in complex fields, building empathy with users and humans, their needs and pain points even when you have very little in common with them
• Ability to make design decisions that appropriately balance business goals, product priorities, customer feedback, research insights, and technical considerations
• Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams across multiple locations and time-zones to iteratively ship and evolve products while keeping the end design vision in mind
• Attention to detail and willingness to learn about a complex, very technical product space
• Experience working in a fully-remote, fast-paced environment where you are expected to share openly, default to transparency, and embrace your autonomy

• Experience designing complex, data-dense interfaces with a focus on clarity
• Ability to rapidly gain an understanding of a technical domain and associated customer needs and user workflows in order to design effective experiences within that domain
• Domain knowledge or experience related to observability, cloud infrastructure, and/or database monitoring
• Experience helping design teams, especially at engineering led companies, level up their practice, collaboration with partner functions, and user and organizational impact

What are we building?
Hard Rock Digital is a fiercely focused team working to become the best online sportsbook, casino, and social gaming company in the world. We're building a deeply curious team with a passion for learning, operating, and building new products and technologies for millions of consumers. We're customer-obsessed — we care about each customer interaction, experience, behavior, and insight, and strive to ensure we're always acting authentically.
Rooted in the kindred spirits of Hard Rock and the Seminole Tribe of Florida, Hard Rock Digital taps a brand known the world over as the leader in gaming, entertainment, and hospitality. We're taking that foundation of success and bringing it to the digital space - ready to join us? What's the position?
Every bet and payout at Hard Rock Digital is a database transaction that has to be fast and accurate. A casino game resolves in milliseconds; settling a big sporting event moves millions of balances at once, and none can be wrong.
We're hiring Senior Database Infrastructure Engineers to own the PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse databases behind our platform and work alongside the team that runs our CockroachDB clusters. Which engine you know best matters less than how well you understand what each one does underneath, well enough to explain why the same workload behaves differently on two of them.
A database problem rarely stays inside the database. The people who do well here follow it into the application code, the platform, and the architecture decisions, and they want their scope at Hard Rock Digital to grow with it.
Claude Code, Codex, and similar AI harnesses are part of how this team works. We use them to investigate incidents and turn one-off debugging into durable tooling, so more time goes to work that compounds: better defaults, safer migrations, and shorter incidents.
What You'll Do
Operations
Operate PostgreSQL and MySQL on Amazon RDS across production, staging, and development: replication, failover, backup and recovery, upgrades, and each engine's own failure modes, from autovacuum and wraparound to purge and replica lag.
Run ClickHouse for both operational and analytical workloads: table engines, sort keys, partitioning, merges, replication, and the ingestion paths that feed it.
Support CockroachDB operations, and take on more of that work as you learn the system.
Performance & Reliability
Trace slow queries and lock waits behind bets, settlements, and payouts to the plan, the statistics, and the schema or code that caused them.
Assess schema-change risk before it reaches large tables, and review schemas and queries with application teams before they ship.
Build observability in Prometheus, Grafana, Mimir, and Loki, join the data-layer on-call rota, and lead incident analysis and blameless postmortems.
Tooling & Influence
Build Python and Go tooling, and automate provisioning and recovery with Terraform.
Use AI harnesses daily, and verify their output against production facts before you ship it.
Implement and audit access controls and encryption for a regulated gaming platform.
Set standards that hold across engines, take part in architecture reviews, and read the source when a problem needs a code-level answer.
What are we looking for?
5+ years operating production relational databases as a DBA, Database Reliability Engineer, or Data Platform Engineer.
Deep production experience with PostgreSQL and MySQL, or deep experience with one and serious working experience with the other.
You understand these engines underneath and can compare them: PostgreSQL's heap and row versions against InnoDB's clustered index and undo log, write-ahead logging, cost-based planning, replication and what each failover option can lose, and how a columnar engine like ClickHouse differs from both.
Enough grounding in distributed systems (consensus, distributed transactions, consistency models) to learn CockroachDB quickly
Python or Go, and enough Java to debug line-of-business code.
Linux, infrastructure-as-code, a monitoring stack such as Grafana, AWS, and willingness to join an on-call rota.
Clear technical writing and speech: you can explain a hard problem to an engineer or a product manager without losing the part that matters.
How You Work
You learn a new system from the bottom up: the source, the design documents, and experiments you run yourself.
When the documentation is wrong or silent, you find out what the system really does and write it down.
You want a bigger job than the one you were hired into, and you look for it here.
You want this role to be your main professional focus, not one engagement among several.
What You've Done
Shipped Python or Go tooling for database operations, migration safety, or incident response that other engineers then used.
Investigated production incidents end-to-end, down to execution plans and source code.
Moved a workload between engines or across major versions, and can tell us what surprised you.
Took on work outside the database because the problem needed it, and changed how another team built or shipped.
Run ClickHouse, CockroachDB, or another distributed database in production.
Worked with Kafka, Materialize, or Snowflake.
Used AI coding agents in real work, with review habits that keep output tied to evidence.

The role
As a Systems Engineer for C-UAS System-of-Systems, you own the high-level architecture of a distributed air defence capability.
You define the top-level architecture (L0 and L1), partitioning the capability into network, sensor, and effector subsystems and the interfaces between them. The architecture is open and hardware agnostic: any qualified node can join the network. It is controlled centrally but is designed to keep operating when nodes are lost or contested, so that no single point of failure breaks the chain. This is the layer that enables engage-on-remote and launch-on-remote, where the effector need not sit with the sensor that cued it.
This is a role for someone who thinks at the level of the whole system. Your decisions on architecture, networking, and interfaces determine whether a distributed capability performs as one coherent whole under real operational conditions.
The day-to-day
• Own the top-level (L0/L1) architecture of the C-UAS system-of-systems, partitioning the mission into network, sensor, and effector subsystems
• Specify the network capabilities that let distributed nodes share a common air picture and coordinate engagements, including decentralised operation when the central command node is degraded or absent
• Derive network, sensor, and effector requirements from the operational concept, and own the trade-offs between coverage, resilience, latency, and cost
• Translate operational concepts into a coherent system architecture and clear engagement concepts, then hold that architecture consistent as the design matures
• Keep the architecture open and hardware agnostic, establishing the interfaces that let any qualified node join the network
• Enable engage-on-remote and launch-on-remote by defining how cueing, track handover, and fire control flow across nodes
• Produce a structured architecture that can be exposed externally to partners and customers at the right level of abstraction, without disclosing sensitive detail
• Collaborate daily with the situational awareness and interceptor integration teams, and with AI, software, and hardware engineers, to keep the system-of-systems coherent

• Understand distributed and decentralised system design: how nodes share state, degrade gracefully, and coordinate without a single point of failure

• Hold a university degree in Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace, Computer Science, or a related field

As we scale, getting our numbers right isn’t a back-office job; it’s how we make good decisions quickly. You’ll work as a team of two as our go-to finance person, partnering with the leadership team and me to keep things running smoothly today while building the processes, controls, and reporting we’ll need as we grow.
This isn’t a role where you’ll sit in one lane. One day you’ll be closing the month, the next you’ll be modeling a new hiring plan, answering an investor question or helping get the numbers in order for our India entity. Management accounting & controls 📊

• You’ll oversee cash flow and treasury, keeping a close eye on cash and runway.

Job Title
Internal Audit Manager
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your Team:
IG is a global trading business, regulated in multiple jurisdictions, and it moves fast. Internal Audit needs an experienced manager who wants to dig into the hard questions. You will lead complex audits across IG's regulated Global entities, with a focus on regulatory, non-financial and operational risks.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
You will report to the Head of Internal Audit (UK, APAC and Middle East) and work with a growing team, co-source partners and subject matter experts. You will own the quality of each audit you lead, from scoping through to the final report. You will also feed into and support delivery of the Internal Audit strategy. Line management responsibility will follow as the team grows. What you’ll do:
Audit delivery
• Lead end-to-end delivery of complex, global audits, from planning, through fieldwork to reporting, within agreed timelines, to IG's methodology and IIA standards.
• Manage a portfolio of audits, tracking progress, resourcing and risks to delivery, and escalating issues to the Head of Audit early.
• Oversee the quality and consistency of work across the portfolio, reviewing the work of auditors and co-source teams so that reports meet IG’s standards before they are issued.
• Direct co-source partners and subject matter experts, setting clear scope and challenging their work so the output is high quality, risk-focused and commercially sensible.
• Write clear, well-evidenced findings and reports, agreeing practical actions with management.
Partnering with the business
• Work alongside senior leaders in the first and second lines as a trusted partner. Understand their objectives, give honest and constructive insight, and support real improvements to how IG manages risk and serves clients.
Planning and risk assessment
• Contribute to the annual audit plan and risk assessment, particularly for regulatory, non-financial and operational risk topics.
• Track regulatory change and industry events (for example FCA, MiFID, MAR, AML requirements and the expectations of IG's other regulators), and assess what they mean for audit coverage.
Governance and reporting
• Prepare papers for entity boards and committees, including the Audit Committee where required, drawing out themes across audits and giving independent insight. Present them where needed.
• Follow up issues and actions, challenging evidence before closure, and report progress and overdue items accurately.
Innovation and continuous improvement
• Help the function use AI, data analytics and automation in audit work, such as automated testing, document review and continuous monitoring.
• Bring a continuous improvement mindset to Internal Audit's own methodology and to the business processes you review.
• Contribute to the Quality Self-Assessment and External Quality Assessment, and to the function's adherence to the IIA Global Internal Audit Standards.
Leadership
• Act as a role model and coach for junior colleagues, reviewing work and supporting their development. Contribute to recruitment and onboarding. Take on line management as the team grows. What you’ll need for this role:
Essential
• Experience in Internal Audit within financial services or similar, with a track record of leading a portfolio of audits in a regulated environment.
• A recognised professional qualification: ACA, ACCA, CIA or equivalent.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge senior colleagues and influence without authority.
• Excellent written communication, able to turn complex issues into clear, concise, board-quality reports.
• Intellectual curiosity and a commercial outlook, balancing rigour with pragmatic, risk-proportionate recommendations.
• Fluency in written and spoken English.
Desirable
• Strong knowledge of regulatory risk e.g. AML, market abuse, consumer duty or client money.
• Experience in a trading, brokerage or other capital markets firm.
• Practical use of data analytics or automation in audit (for example SQL, Python, Power BI or AI tools).
• Experience contributing to audit methodology or transformation work.
• Prior line management experience. The Perks:
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary

• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents

You'll be the bridge between Finance, Technology and wider business teams, helping our systems evolve to meet the needs of colleagues and support our organisational goals.

Role Summary
• Owning the user experience across our finance systems and becoming the voice of the customer within the business.
• Building strong relationships with stakeholders across Finance, Technology and other departments to understand needs and priorities.
• Developing and maintaining a roadmap for system improvements and enhancements.
• Gathering requirements, writing user stories and supporting the delivery of system developments using Agile ways of working.
• Using data, insight and user feedback to inform decisions and continuous improvement initiatives.

• A demonstrable understanding of end-to-end finance processes and financial controls, including how system changes affect transaction processing, reconciliations and financial reporting.
• Experience translating finance requirements into improvements to ERP or related business systems, working collaboratively with users and technical teams.
• The ability to build strong relationships and influence stakeholders at all levels.
• Experience gathering requirements, prioritising work and managing competing demands.
• Strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to decision making.
• Experience of continuous improvement methodologies and delivering change.
• Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
• Business analysis skills, including process mapping and workflow design.
• Familiarity with Agile ways of working and the ability to apply them to finance-systems improvements, or transferable delivery experience and a willingness to learn this approach.

IQVIA UK Consulting already supports clients across most of the promotional value chain — targeting and segmentation, campaign implementation through our Direct Medical Engagement (DME) teams, and impact measurement. This is an entrepreneurial, P&L-aware role: part practice builder, part senior client advisor.
Key responsibilities
• Capability build. Define and stand up IQVIA UK's marketing strategy & media planning offer: service design, methodologies, pricing, IP/templates, quality standards and go-to-market narrative. Codify ways of working so the offer scales beyond the founder.
• End-to-end promotional strategy. Lead client engagements covering brand and portfolio strategy, positioning, messaging architecture, customer journey, channel mix, campaign planning, and KPI/measurement frameworks — linking strategy to IQVIA's existing targeting, DME execution and PromoSuite measurement assets.
• Media planning & buying advisory. Advise clients on channel strategy across HCP and (where relevant) patient/consumer audiences. Run channel selection, budget allocation, flighting and media-mix recommendations. Manage relationships with media agencies/owners and oversee buying where executed via partners.
• Sales & business development. Own a personal sales target. Generate and convert pipeline through existing IQVIA accounts and your own network. Lead proposals, pitches and commercial negotiations; cross-sell into Consulting, DME, OneKey, Real-World and Technology offerings. The role would be supported by sales specialists who will also drive client discussions.

• Thought leadership. Represent IQVIA externally — POVs, conference speaking, client roundtables — to position the new capability in the UK market.
Essential experience & skills:
• 15+ years' experience in a marketing strategy and/or media planning role within a healthcare and/or FMCG agency, consultancy or in-house brand team (agency-side experience strongly preferred).
• Demonstrable ownership of end-to-end promotional strategy — from insight and positioning through to channel plan, execution brief and measurement.
• Hands-on experience of media planning, with working knowledge of media buying processes, agency economics and the main UK media owners/platforms (HCP and consumer).
• Proven sales track record: personal book of business, owning revenue targets, closing six- and seven-figure engagements.
• Established senior client network in UK pharma/healthcare (Marketing, Omnichannel, Commercial Excellence) and/or FMCG.
• Strong commercial acumen: scoping, pricing, margin management, contracting.
• Excellent written and verbal communication; able to flex between C-suite, brand teams and delivery analysts.
• Comfortable building from a blank sheet — entrepreneurial, pragmatic, hands-on.
Desirable / additional skills:
• Omnichannel / orchestration expertise — designing HCP customer journeys across rep, email, digital, congress, paid media and content syndication; familiarity with platforms such as Veeva, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Experience Cloud.
• Performance marketing & analytics literacy — media mix modelling, attribution, A/B testing, working knowledge of GA4, programmatic, DSPs and retargeting frameworks.
• Data-driven mindset — comfortable using IQVIA assets (sales data, PromoSuite, OneKey, ALHP/Synmetrics) to shape strategy and prove ROI.
• Creative judgement — able to brief and challenge creative agencies on concept, messaging and production quality (without being a creative themselves).
• Regulatory fluency — ABPI Code, PMCPA, MHRA promotional rules; awareness of EFPIA and equivalent EU codes is a plus.
• International exposure — experience working across EU markets or with global brand teams; awareness of how UK promo strategy fits into pan-European plans.
• Therapy-area depth — at least one of: oncology, immunology, rare disease, vaccines, cardiometabolic, CNS.
• Consulting hygiene — structured problem solving, project economics, ability to QA junior deliverables, comfort with MSAs/SOWs.
• People leadership — track record of building and mentoring small teams; ability to attract talent into the new capability over time.

Quality is where a precision factory earns its customers or loses them. This role owns quality control at our London factory, on parts going to aerospace, defence, energy and other critical industries.

Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.
The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery. 
Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.
The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you. 
 
About Iso
Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.
Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.
We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.
Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.
 
Your impact 
As an Operating Partner you'll work as a member of a compact, agile, and high-impact team specialising in catalysing business critical initiatives across Iso through partnership with cross-functional organisational leaders. Together, we drive operational excellence, maximising productivity and accelerating progress toward our mission. Because agility, organisation, and flawless execution are critical, this role will dynamically evolve alongside the needs of our team and the leaders you partner with.
What you will do 
You’ll work alongside the VPs of AI and their wider organisation to deliver the highest-priority initiatives in their org areas, in particular where these are strategic in nature, require cross-organisational influence or are outside of the normal rhythms of the business.
• Thought-Partner: You’ll enable leaders and their teams to operate effectively by advising and soundboarding on their ideas for how to solve problems, accelerate, and maximise outputs across their organisation 
• Prioritise and Coordinate: You will distinguish critical leadership priorities from support tasks, establishing clear ownership and empowering teams to act. With a keen sense of timing, you will know when to revive paused initiatives, align stakeholders, and deliver actionable plans.
• Deliver and Execute: You’ll focus your time on maximising the impact of key initiatives, particularly those outside the normal day-to-day operating patterns, or of the highest strategic importance. You’ll prepare, present and gain agreement on proposals among stakeholders and then influence teams to execute - leveraging strong communication skills. You’ll follow up, problem-solve, close loops in a timely fashion and drive initiatives to completion. 
• Drive Cross-Functional Collaboration: You’ll build relationships with key stakeholders across Iso to gain a holistic understanding of the organisation, instilling high levels of trust and providing hands-on partnership on important projects.
• Translate and Communicate: You’ll translate complex technical developments into clear, high-impact executive summaries and strategic presentations for a variety of stakeholders, including board meetings and key management presentations. 
• Drive efficiency: You’ll empower others to be maximally efficient by optimising for leanness and proactively spotting and breaking down blockers and inefficiencies, balancing what the organisation needs in the short and longer term with a keen eye for how to scale most efficiently and effectively. 
 
Skills and qualifications 
Essential:

• Understand and Translate Complex Topics with Fluency: Strong ability to learn and absorb technical information, grasp key concepts of machine learning/frontier AI, with the confidence to probe, synthesize, and translate complex technical matters into actionable executive communication.
• Complex Execution & Ambiguity: Demonstrated ability to break down highly ambiguous, multi-faceted problems into concrete plans and drive them through to measurable completion with pace and precision.
• Cross-Functional Influence: Proven ability to build rapid trust and drive alignment across diverse, interdisciplinary teams (research, engineering, product, and operations) without direct line authority.
• Agility & Low-Ego Mindset: High resilience and adaptability in dynamic scale-up environments, with a roll-up-your-sleeves mentality where no task is too big or too small.
Nice to have:
• Background in a Chief of Staff, Strategic Operations, or Operating Partner role within a fast-scaling tech or AI organization.
• Familiarity or working exposure to digital biology, computational chemistry, or biopharma workflows.
• Experience facilitating executive team rhythms, planning cycles, and organizational scaling mechanisms.
Culture and values
We are guided by our shared values. It's not about finding people who think and act in the same way. These values help to guide our work and will continue to strengthen it. 
Thoughtful
Thoughtful at Iso is about curiosity, creativity and care. It is about good people doing good, rigorous and future-making science every single day.
Brave
Brave at Iso is about fearlessness, but it’s also about initiative and integrity. The scale of the challenge demands nothing less.
Determined
Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.
Together
Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.

We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. Klarna, briefly At Klarna, we’re building an everyday finance network, helping over 120 million consumers across 26 countries save time and money, and worry less about their finances. Working here means taking on problems most companies never get to solve, and being hands-on enough that the interesting part of the work lands with you, not someone else — you’ll build with AI, not watch it happen. This is the stretch zone. Come find out what you’re capable of. About the role Klarna Financial Services UK Limited is regulated by the FCA, and the UK MLRO is the senior individual accountable for its financial crime controls. This position is the deputy to that function. You’ll provide day-to-day secondary review of the decisions that carry the most financial crime risk, and you’ll step into the UK MLRO’s responsibilities when they’re absent. You’ll work across Klarna’s UK financial crime control framework, from suspicious activity reporting and sanctions matches to the policies and procedures that govern them. You’ll also work with first-line control owners to make sure controls are changed and communicated in line with UK law. What you’ll do You’ll provide secondary review and challenge on suspicious activity reports, PEP and high-risk customer decisions, incident escalations, and sanctions matches. You’ll submit external reports to the NCA and OFSI under the direction of the UK MLRO. You’ll contribute to Management Committee and Board reporting, the Annual MLRO Report, and the Business Wide Risk Assessment. You’ll oversee outsourced and third-party AML/CTF functions with the UK MLRO, and run thematic reviews of the control framework. You’ll update AML/CTF and sanctions policies, procedures, and routines, and communicate the changes to first-line control owners. You’ll run regulatory horizon scanning and gap analysis, and bring control gaps to first-line control owners for resolution. You’ll advise first-line colleagues on control changes that affect financial crime risk. You’ll assess non-SAR, PEP, sanctions, and fraud customer escalations, such as FOS complaints, for financial crime compliance input. You’ll prepare the data for Klarna’s Annual Financial Crime Report to the FCA (REPCRIM). You’ll assess new products against UK financial crime obligations and give the UK MLRO clear recommendations. Who you are You’ve spent 7+ years in financial crime compliance, including time as a Deputy MLRO or Senior Compliance Manager, with hands-on experience of suspicious activity reporting, OFSI reporting, and PEP and high-risk customer assessments. You’ve worked in financial services, fintech, or a firm offering products under the Consumer Credit Act. You hold an AML/CTF or sanctions qualification, such as the ICA Certificate in AML or ACAMS, or an equivalent. You have a working knowledge of financial crime typologies across money laundering, sanctions, terrorism, fraud, and bribery and corruption. You keep your AML/CTF knowledge current through training, workshops, and regulatory publications. Things you should know before applying Working together: this position is UK-based, and most teams currently meet in the office 2–3 days per week. This varies by team and can change over time. Travel: this position requires travel between the UK and Sweden. Approval: the successful candidate must be approved by Klarna Financial Services UK Limited as a Certified Function holder. Non-obvious backgrounds are welcome. Diversity of skills, perspectives and backgrounds is how we create, innovate, and disrupt like no other. Final compensation will be based on the candidate’s qualifications, skills, and experience. Please include a CV in English. Concrete beats comprehensive — what you built, what it did, what it cost. About the Role:
Kong is hiring an ADR Team Lead to support our Benelux, and Nordics regions. This is a player-coach role. You'll be taking an active hand in developing the team around you, especially the newer ADRs still finding their footing.
You'll work closely with, and report into, the Senior Manager for NEMEA. You're shaping how the team operates, not running it solo. Think of this as a high-impact individual contributor role with a leadership layer built in: the natural next step for an ADR who's ready to start making other people better, not just themselves.
Our NEMEA team is already strong. Driven, independent, hitting their numbers. What they need isn't more oversight. They need someone who sharpens how the team works, especially around process and tooling, while making sure newer reps get the support to ramp fast.
You'll report to Oscar Winberg. He moves fast, sets a high bar, and expects people to bring solutions, not just flag problems. He's direct, so you'll always know exactly where you stand, and he expects that same directness back: if you disagree, he wants the pushback, backed by data, not silence. Earn his trust and he'll hand you real ownership. What he won't do is hand-hold, so this role suits someone who'd rather be given room to run than told exactly what to do.
What You'll Do:
Support newer ADRs. You'll be the first point of contact for less tenured reps, helping them ramp faster and build good habits early. You'll help with onboarding alongside the Senior Manager and Enablement, and run regular 1:1s with newer ADRs. Different reps need different things from you, so you'll read where each person is and adjust your coaching accordingly rather than running the same playbook on everyone. You'll help build individual development plans grounded in a real read of each rep's attitude, process, and results, and you'll flag underperformance early, with context, instead of letting it fester.
Coach and upskill the team. You'll support team coaching sessions: live dialling, pitch practice, feedback loops. You'll run or contribute to upskilling initiatives, on your own or with Enablement. You'll share what's working, best practices, sequences, outbound approaches, with the wider team, and give direct, specific feedback often, recognizing strong work and not letting bad habits slide.
Sharpen process and tooling. You'll help spot where the team's workflows and tooling could run more efficiently, and support the Senior Manager in rolling out improvements without stripping reps of their autonomy. You'll be the go-to person for best practice on Salesforce, Outreach, and the team's automation tools.
Contribute to the wider GTM motion. You'll keep strong alignment with your AE partners and take part in pipe review cadences. You'll support the Senior Manager in preparing performance updates and regional insights, and join bi-weekly RD cadences where it makes sense.
What You'll Bring:
- Hands-on ADR or SDR experience. You know what this job feels like from the inside, not just what it looks like from a deck.
- A real coach's instinct. You get energy from making other people better, not just from hitting your own number.
- The ability to juggle competing priorities without dropping the ball. Your own quota, coaching newer reps, and process work will all pull on your time in the same week, and you know how to decide what actually matters right now.
- Strong time management. This is one we screen for directly, not something we assume comes with experience.
- A bias for building. You spot what needs fixing and go build it, rather than working only through a list of tasks someone else handed you.
- Analytical rigor. You make calls based on data, not gut feel, and you're comfortable being specific about why a number moved, including when that number is going the wrong way.
- A track record of top-tier performance that holds up on both counts: the day-to-day discipline that drives it (activity, sequence execution, pipeline hygiene), and the results that discipline produces, quarter over quarter, not just once.
- Real trust with your AE and RD partners, earned through consistency, not just alignment on paper.
- Transparency, especially with leadership, especially when something isn't on track. We'd rather hear it early than find out later.
- The kind of presence the team actually looks up to, not just reports to.
- Comfort in an allbound model with a heavy outbound emphasis.
- Self-awareness and a genuine investment in growing as a leader.
- Language skills: English is a core requirements, with Dutch OR Swedish
Culture and Value:
The EMEA SDR team are weather makers. We don't wait for opportunity, we create it. We're accountable, relentless, and we invest in each other like no other team does.
- Relentless. Energy and intention every day. Every challenge is a chance to get stronger.
- Character. Good humans first. Integrity, humility, and keeping our word.
- Together. No one gets left behind. Differences make us better, not harder to manage.
- Truth. Radical honesty. We say the hard things with care. That's how we move fast.
- Accountable. We own our results, bias toward action, and don't wait to be told.
- Pioneering. We take up space, experiment, and bring creative thinking to every challenge.
In NEMEA specifically, we operate in mature markets. We don't manufacture urgency, we earn entry by knowing the landscape better than the prospect does. We're pipeline gardeners: patient, precise, persistent.
"We don't book meetings. We build pipeline."
This role is a genuine development opportunity. For the right person, it's the foundation of a leadership career at Kong.

• Champion a world-class customer experience across the region, create strategic deal governance, risk mitigation and pricing judgement decision.
• Partner closely with Customer Success, Product, Consulting and Marketing teams to shape the priorities across functions to deliver outstanding client value.
• Improve customer satisfaction, retention and advocacy
• Ensure customer feedback is incorporated into regional and global planning processes.
Market & Competitive Intelligence
• Interpret Market trends, competitor activity and client workflow changes to guide commercial strategy
• Maintain a strong understanding of commodity markets, market intelligence trends and evolving customer requirements.
• Demonstrate detailed knowledge of ICIS competitors, their products, commercial strategies, strengths and market positioning.
• Equip the Account Management team with competitive intelligence and effective value propositions.
• Represent ICIS at customer meetings, industry events and regional forums.

• Experience managing strategic and complex enterprise accounts.
• Proven ability to build relationships and negotiate with senior stakeholders and executives.
• Experience leading geographically distributed teams across multiple countries.
• Demonstrated success in coaching and developing high-performing commercial teams.

Market Knowledge
• Strong understanding of commodity, energy, chemicals or data and analytics markets.
• Knowledge of the competitive landscape across market intelligence, data, pricing and analytics providers.
• Understanding of customer workflows and decision-making processes across both industrial and commercial customer segments.
Languages

• Additional European language skills would be advantageous and support engagement across Southern European markets.

• Strong commercial and customer-focused mindset.
• Excellent communication and influencing skills.
• Strategic thinker with strong execution capability.
• High emotional intelligence and coaching capability.
• Ability to lead through change and drive organisational performance.
• Collaborative leader who can operate effectively within a matrix organisation.
Location & Travel

• Ability to engage effectively with customers at a C Suite level and teams across multiple cultures and markets.

• Expansion revenue growth.
• Customer satisfaction and advocacy.
• Strategic account development.
• Team engagement and performance.
• Forecast accuracy and operational excellence.
• Market share growth within existing accounts.

We're looking for a full-stack engineer to join our growing team.
We value small and high performing teams and are looking for a full-time software engineer to join alongside the current core team. The responsibilities will go beyond just the technical stack: you'll help shape product direction and company strategy, and you'll have a lot of influence over how we build and how we work.
Some things we're looking for:
You're a high-ownership builder. You take a fuzzy customer problem, decide what to build, and get it shipped.
You're AI-native. You build with coding agents and LLMs every day, you understand how they work under the hood, and you have real projects to show us.
You have product experience. You've built products that real users and customers depend on. You appreciate good design (UI/UX) and are passionate about building products that people love to use.
You care about security but know how to build secure systems without slowing down. An interest in networking or security operations is a plus.
You're a fantastic communicator and happy to keep challenging existing ideas.
You're thoughtful about creating and maintaining a world-class engineering culture.
What the job involves:
Build and own features from start to finish: plan, build, test, deploy, iterate.
Working directly with our users in the community (through Slack, X, Github), reviewing their issues and using the feedback to prioritise our work.
Having an ownership mindset: being comfortable with both responsibility and accountability.
Being comfortable when faced with a lot of ambiguity, both technically and organizationally.
Making good trade-off decisions between moving quickly and launching features versus optimising for engineering excellence. You're happy to ship something at ~80% and iterate.
Location
This is a hybrid role based in London. Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for a role if they don’t have experience in 100% of the requirements outlined in a job description. Please know that even if you don’t have experience in all the areas above, but think you could do a great job and are excited about shaping company culture, finding great people and building great teams, we’d love to hear from you!
How we work at Lightdash
We build in public, by default. We’re an open source product, so having shared context is important so that people can contribute effectively to Lightdash. As a team, we also think that we make the best decisions when everyone has a lot of the same information. We don't oversell and under-deliver: we want the experience of using Lightdash to be as awesome as the experience we're selling.
We challenge problems, not people. We ask ourselves “why is this broken?” not “who is breaking this?”
We’re highly collaborative. We’re a group of people that are happy working independently, but love being part of a team. ****We not only work on problems as a team, but we also listen to the feedback from our community and our users. We invest in tools and processes that allow us to do this, even while fully remote.
We bias towards impact. We’d rather build something to 80% and get it in front of users so we can iterate on fast feedback than build something to 100% just to find out it’s not the right thing. We spend a lot of time thinking about how our work solves real user problems. We work on the highest impact problems even if they’re something a bit “out of your remit”.
Our tech stack:

Primary stack: Typescript, React, Node, SQL
Frameworks: express, react-hooks
Infrastructure: Docker, GCP

We achieve this not through targets and incentives, but by fostering a collaborative, supportive and inclusive culture where talented people can do their best work. We are looking for someone with the intellectual curiosity and learning agility to build that knowledge quickly, combined with the judgement, energy and commercial awareness to help translate an evolving strategy into action.
Operating as an extension of senior leadership, you will develop a deep understanding of their priorities and help maintain momentum across a broad and sophisticated stakeholder landscape. At times, you will represent senior leaders in meetings and discussions, ensuring their priorities are understood, influencing outcomes and progressing the agenda without requiring their presence in every conversation.
You will bring structure to ambiguity, connect activity across different parts of the firm, identify where intervention is needed and ensure priorities continue to move forward at pace. You will be comfortable getting to grips with unfamiliar subject matter quickly and translating complex ideas into clear, practical actions.
You will work across legal practice groups, Business Teams, technology, data, knowledge, learning, communications, finance and HR, as well as engaging with external technology providers, clients, regulators and industry partners. The role will also provide exposure to the continued development of Linklaters' Applied Intelligence practice and its client-facing strategy.
This is an opportunity to work at the centre of a fast-evolving area, where the technology, operating model and ways of working continue to develop. You will need to be comfortable operating without an established playbook and excited by the opportunity to learn quickly, adapt and help turn an ambitious agenda into tangible outcomes.
About you
We are looking for someone who combines intellectual curiosity and strong commercial judgement with a genuine bias for action. You will be comfortable working at pace, navigating ambiguity and influencing people without relying on formal authority.

• Comfort with ambiguity and change, particularly where strategies, technologies and ways of working are still developing.
• A collaborative, low-ego approach, with the confidence to contribute, challenge constructively and learn from those around you.
Direct experience of AI is welcome, but it is not essential (and deep technical or engineering expertise is not required).
We see this as a role in which the successful candidate will grow and develop, supported by a team that is genuinely invested in building the knowledge, confidence and impact as the AI agenda continues to evolve.

ROLE SUMMARY:
The Test Architect will own the automation test strategy, architecture, standards, tooling choices, and governance for the FTSE Russell Test Framework within the Equities Product & Operations team. The role combines hands-on engineering with technical leadership across teams, shaping how quality is designed, automated, measured, and improved throughout the software delivery lifecycle. The framework operates in an AWS environment and uses Python, Pytest, CI/CD (GitLab). Testing scope covers functional, integration, API, data, performance, resilience, security, and regression testing.
YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: - Define and maintain a coherent automation test strategy for the FTSE Russell Test Framework, aligning test coverage to product, operational, and delivery risks.
- Establish the target test architecture, reusable patterns, and design principles that enable teams to build consistent, maintainable, and scalable automated tests.
- Set guidance for selecting the appropriate test level and approach across functional, integration, API, data, performance, resilience, security, and regression testing.
- Partner with engineering, product, and architecture stakeholders early in design to make testability a consideration and identify quality risks before implementation.
- Identify gaps, duplication, and brittle areas in test coverage; agree practical improvements with the teams responsible for delivery.
Framework Engineering
- Remain hands-on in designing, developing, and reviewing framework capabilities and representative automated tests using Python and Pytest.
- Define standards for test structure, reusable components, configuration, test data, execution, and results so that automation is reliable and understandable across teams.
- Promote repeatable, isolated, and maintainable tests, and address sources of instability that reduce confidence in test results.
- Guide tooling decisions for the framework, assessing suitability against testing needs, maintainability, and fit with the AWS environment and GitLab delivery workflows; pilot options where appropriate before recommending adoption.
Quality Across the Delivery Lifecycle
- Integrate automated testing into CI/CD workflows in GitLab to provide timely feedback during software change and delivery.
- Define proportionate validation and quality-gate principles for automated checks, making test outcomes and significant quality risks visible to delivery teams.
- Shape data-testing approaches that validate relevant data quality characteristics, including accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reconciliation where applicable.
- Establish approaches for performance, resilience, security, and regression testing that complement functional and integration coverage.
- Use test results, coverage evidence, and recurring failure patterns to identify quality risks and guide continuous improvement.
Governance & Technical Leadership
- Own framework standards, architecture guidance, and governance, keeping them clear, documented, and practical for teams to adopt.
- Provide technical direction across engineering teams through design discussions, code and framework reviews, and support on complex testing challenges.
- Coach and mentor Test engineers, SDETs, and developers on test automation practices, framework use, and quality engineering principles
- Work with product, engineering, and operations partners to understand quality needs, communicate trade-offs, and encourage shared ownership of testing.
- Support consistent adoption of the framework and standards across teams, identifying barriers and helping resolve them through technical guidance.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING: - 12+ years of professional experience in software testing, test automation, or quality engineering, including substantial hands-on technical work.
- Demonstrated experience defining or owning test automation strategy, test architecture, engineering standards, tooling choices, and governance.
- Strong practical experience designing and developing automation using Python, Pytest, and libraries such as Playwright, Pytest-bdd, Requests.
- Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD workflows using GitLab.
- Experience working with systems and test environments hosted in AWS, containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), and database/SQL architecture. - Broad knowledge of functional, integration, API, data, performance, resilience, security, and regression testing, and the ability to select suitable approaches for different quality risks.
- Experience building or evolving reusable test frameworks and improving the maintainability, reliability, and adoption of automated tests.
- Knowledge of the financial services domain is essential.
- Ability to influence technical direction across teams while remaining hands-on.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain architecture, test strategy, and quality risks to technical and non-technical partners.
Key Attributes
- Balances system-level architectural thinking with practical engineering judgment and hands-on delivery.
- Takes a risk-based, evidence-led approach to quality, prioritising meaningful coverage over automation for its own sake.
- Builds alignment through clear communication, sound technical reasoning, and constructive challenge.
- Works collaboratively across product, engineering, and operations, encouraging teams to share responsibility for quality.
- Shows ownership of the framework's effectiveness and adapts standards as delivery needs and risks change.

The Role: Category Manager - BPO
Role Purpose
The Category Manager is the commercial owner of the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) category and acts as an internal commercial consultant to the business. The postholder offers senior stakeholders three things: deep knowledge of the category and its supply market, strategic sourcing capability, and negotiation expertise. Using these, the postholder builds and owns the category strategy and savings plan, competes with vendors on commercial strategy, and influences how the business specifies and buys. Success is measured by realised cost reduction across the category and by the value the business places on Procurement’s advice.
Context
M&G Procurement is on a transformation journey, our objectives include: Identifying and delivering material, recurring cost reduction on M&G third-party spend; and materially improving how the business experiences Procurement, measured through an internal NPS. To achieve these objectives, Procurement is moving from a business unit aligned, generalist model to a category structure that operates as an internal commercial consultancy. The UK team offers the business deep category knowledge, strategic sourcing capability and negotiation expertise, so that M&G can compete with its vendors on commercial strategy.
Key Responsibilities
Category Strategy and Commercial Leadership
• Build, own and execute the category strategy for Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), based on a detailed understanding of supply market structure, vendor commercial models, cost drivers and market trends.
• Maintain living category plans covering market analysis, supply base segmentation, demand profiling, route to market and savings opportunities.
• Develop commercial strategies for key vendors well ahead of renewal, so that M&G negotiates from a position of insight and has credible alternatives.
• Lead high-value sourcing events and negotiations, including setting the negotiation strategy, BATNA and walk-away position, managing concessions and holding positions with incumbents. Manage senior supplier relationships under commercial pressure.
• Design sourcing events and evaluation criteria, and decide how much process each event needs based on its value, risk and complexity. • Introduce competitive tension into renewals and new commitments, moving from single-source and incumbent renewal to structured market engagement, preferred supplier frameworks and normalised rate cards.
Savings and Value Delivery
• Build and own the category savings plan against an agreed share of the group cost reduction target, sizing and prioritising opportunities by value and deliverability.
• Agree baselines and savings methodology with Finance before work starts, and follow savings through until they show in budgets and run rates.
• Build total cost of ownership and should-cost models, model the budget impact of sourcing options and how savings will be recognised in each department’s P&L cost reports, and make sourcing recommendations on that basis.
• Use price, volume and demand levers, including rate reduction, volume aggregation, supplier consolidation and specification change.
• Challenge demand and specification using category and industry knowledge: question whether a requirement is needed at all, and at what volume, service level, specification and term; identify over-specification, duplicate purchasing and avoidable demand; and propose options such as a lower service tier, a shorter term or reuse of existing contracts, setting out the trade offs in commercial terms.
• Report savings and cost avoidance separately and accurately, and maintain a forward pipeline that gives Finance and the business visibility of upcoming activity.
Internal Consultancy and Stakeholder Influence
• Act as a trusted commercial adviser to senior business owners across the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) spend area, engaging early in their planning rather than at the point of purchase.
• Influence stakeholder decisions on sourcing, demand and specification without formal authority, and present category insight, evaluation and commercial recommendations to governance forums.
• Act as the Procurement relationship lead for nominated senior stakeholders where assigned, bringing in other category colleagues as their agenda requires.
• Seek and act on stakeholder feedback, contributing to the improvement in how the business experiences Procurement.
Supplier Management
• Set the commercial direction for key suppliers in the category and lead the commercial input to vendor strategy.
• Influence and partner with in-business vendor management and vendor performance teams so that supplier reviews, contract changes and renewals secure the strongest commercial outcome for M&G.
• Find value in the existing supply base, including through rate review, supplier consolidation and contract optimisation.
Working with the M&G India Procurement Team
• Direct category execution work delivered by the India team, providing clear briefs, priorities and commercial context.
• Review the quality of execution outputs and work with India leads to maintain a responsive, consistent service to the business.
Contract, Risk and Governance
• Shape commercial terms, including pricing mechanisms, indexation, service credits and exit provisions, working with Legal.
• Apply third-party risk management, outsourcing and regulatory requirements as they apply to Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), and identify regulatory risk such as material outsourcing.
• Apply procurement standards and governance proportionately, and record activity in the system of record and eSourcing tooling.
Data, Digital and AI
• Use spend data, Power BI dashboards and AI tools to analyse trends and anomalies, identify future sourcing opportunities and present a clear commercial account of what the management information shows.
• Question data rather than accept it at face value, and work with India colleagues to keep category data accurate.
Person Specification Essential
• Substantial category management or strategic sourcing experience, with a track record of delivering measurable savings in a complex organisation.
• Category knowledge and experience as set out in the Category Knowledge Requirements above.
• Demonstrable experience of planning and leading negotiations on high-value contracts with major vendors, including setting negotiation strategy and BATNA.
• Credibility with senior stakeholders, evidence of influencing business decisions without formal authority, and experience of presenting commercial recommendations to senior governance forums.
• Strong commercial and financial judgement, including total cost of ownership and should-cost analysis, and the ability to explain budget and P&L impact to stakeholders.
• Confident using spend data and management information to identify trends, anomalies and sourcing opportunities.
• Able to work from the London or Kildean (Stirling) office for the majority of the working week.
People and Capability
• Coach and develop Category Specialists and India colleagues working in the category, reviewing their work and building category capability across the UK and India.
• Plan how onshore and offshore capacity is used across the category, so that effort is directed at the highest value work.
• Share category intelligence across the Procurement team and support cross-category opportunities.
Working Pattern
This role is based in London or Kildean (Stirling). The postholder is expected to work from their base office for the majority of the working week. Regular, in person contact with senior stakeholders is central to the role, because building trust and influencing business decisions depend on it.

The Role: Category Manager - ITO
Role Purpose The Category Manager is the commercial owner of the IT Outsourcing (ITO) category and acts as an internal commercial consultant to the business. The postholder offers senior stakeholders three things: deep knowledge of the category and its supply market, strategic sourcing capability, and negotiation expertise. Using these, the postholder builds and owns the category strategy and savings plan, competes with vendors on commercial strategy, and influences how the business specifies and buys. Success is measured by realised cost reduction across the category and by the value the business places on Procurement’s advice.
Context M&G Procurement is on a transformation journey, our objectives include: Identifying and delivering material, recurring cost reduction on M&G third-party spend; and materially improving how the business experiences Procurement, measured through an internal NPS. To achieve these objectives, Procurement is moving from a business unit aligned, generalist model to a category structure that operates as an internal commercial consultancy. The UK team offers the business deep category knowledge, strategic sourcing capability and negotiation expertise, so that M&G can compete with its vendors on commercial strategy.
Key Responsibilities
Category Strategy and Commercial Leadership • Build, own and execute the category strategy for IT Outsourcing (ITO), based on a detailed understanding of supply market structure, vendor commercial models, cost drivers and market trends. • Maintain living category plans covering market analysis, supply base segmentation, demand profiling, route to market and savings opportunities. • Develop commercial strategies for key vendors well ahead of renewal, so that M&G negotiates from a position of insight and has credible alternatives. • Lead high-value sourcing events and negotiations, including setting the negotiation strategy, BATNA and walk-away position, managing concessions and holding positions with incumbents. Role Purpose
The New Markets and Instruments Specialist leads the end-to-end assessment and implementation of new markets, exchanges and instruments, enabling Fund Managers to expand their investment universe safely and efficiently. The role coordinates investment, operations, risk, compliance, technology and external service providers to evaluate feasibility, identify and mitigate risks, design appropriate operating models and confirm operational readiness.
Working from initial request through to implementation, the role captures the investment rationale and detailed requirements, leads cross-functional due diligence, resolves issues and dependencies, and ensures that all required approvals, controls and implementation activities are completed. It provides clear governance, communication and escalation throughout delivery.
The assessment may include clarifying the investment strategy, designing a new operating model and evaluating the full investment lifecycle. This includes pre-funding requirements, non-standard working days, cross-time-zone dependencies and the processing of complex instruments. The analysis identifies material risks and supports the development of proportionate mitigating controls with the New Markets and Instruments (NMI) Process Champions.
The role acts as a subject-matter expert and contributes to the development of a centre of excellence for new markets and instruments across M&G plc, promoting consistent standards, reusable knowledge and continuous improvement.
Key Responsibilities
• Leads the end-to-end delivery of new market, exchange and instrument initiatives from initial feasibility assessment through to implementation and operational readiness.
• Captures and documents Fund Manager requirements, investment rationale and expected outcomes at the level of detail required by impacted teams.
• Coordinates cross-functional due diligence across investment, operations, risk, compliance, technology and legal teams, including internal, overseas and third-party dependencies.
• Assesses the proposed investment lifecycle and operating model, identifying requirements relating to trading, funding, settlement, custody, collateral, valuation, accounting, reporting and lifecycle-event management.
• Ensures that material risks—including operational, regulatory, compliance, scalability and third-party risks—are identified, assessed and either mitigated or formally accepted through the appropriate governance process.
• Designs or coordinates changes to operating models, processes and controls, working with NMI Process Champions and impacted teams to develop proportionate and sustainable solutions.
• Plans, manages and, where necessary, performs implementation activities to ensure that all approvals, documentation, system changes, testing, training and operational-readiness actions are completed.
• Collaborates with custodians, third-party administrators and other external service providers, including State Street and HSS, to define and implement required service and operating-model changes.
• Provides Fund Managers and senior stakeholders with clear reporting on scope, delivery status, timelines, risks, dependencies and capacity constraints, escalating issues where requirements or delivery dates are at risk.
• Critically evaluates information and consolidates input from multiple teams to support executive decision-making and formal approval.
• Develops and shares specialist knowledge of investment markets, instruments, risks and operational requirements across the NMI Process Champion network.
• Identifies and implements improvements to the NMI process to strengthen controls, remove inefficiencies and reduce time to market.
• Maintains accurate and current procedures, implementation artefacts and records of approved markets and instruments, including approval conditions and supporting evidence.
