The Role: Strategic Supplier Value Lead
The Strategic Supplier Value Lead unlocks value from M&G’s most strategic suppliers and cross-business unit suppliers, beyond what the contract delivers. The postholder works with a named portfolio of around ten suppliers and, for each, brings business unit leadership and the supplier’s executive team together around a forward agenda of innovation, joint savings initiatives, co-investment and access to the supplier’s wider client network and expertise. Opportunities are originated and shaped by this role and handed to the Technology or Services procurement teams to negotiate and contract. Success is measured by the net value that lands for the group.
M&G Procurement is on a transformation journey, our objectives include: identifying and delivering material, recurring cost reduction on M&G third-party spend; and materially improving how the business experiences Procurement, measured through an internal NPS. A strategic supplier reaches the group through many doors. Its delivery teams sit inside each business unit and department, and its sales team deals with the Procurement category teams on price, terms and renewals. Today there is no single executive door into the whole relationship. This role is that door.
Most organisations combine delivery oversight and relationship value in one supplier management role. M&G’s operating model deliberately separates them. Delivery oversight stays with the business units that consume the service. Negotiation stays with the Procurement category teams. Strategic Supplier Value is a horizontal role, organised by named supplier, that works across every business unit on what the whole relationship can give the group.
Role Boundaries
The role sits alongside two existing layers and does not duplicate either. These boundaries are fixed and are central to how the role operates.
What this role does not do
• Own or oversee service delivery, SLAs, supplier performance, contract management or vendor governance. These remain with in-business vendor management teams.
• Act as an escalation route for operational or delivery issues. These are directed back to the accountable business vendor management team.
• Negotiate, contract or renew. All negotiation, including the terms of co-investment and joint savings initiatives, is led by the relevant category team.
• Make commitments or give signals to suppliers on price, volume, term or renewal intent.
• Work with suppliers outside the contracted portfolio.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Supplier Portfolio
• Maintain the named portfolio of around ten strategic suppliers, typically around seven anchor suppliers selected mainly on spend and dependency, plus three rotating slots for smaller suppliers where value headroom and our importance to them are high.
• Apply the agreed eligibility criteria (top tier group spend, critical service or high strategic dependency, use by more than one business unit) and prioritisation scoring (value headroom, our importance to the supplier, network value, innovation capacity, cross business unit breadth).
• Lead the annual portfolio review and present recommendations for approval at group executive level, rotating suppliers so the role does not drift into permanent account management.
Executive Convening and Value Agenda
• Build and maintain a forward value agenda for each portfolio supplier, setting out the opportunities the group intends to pursue and the value expected.
• Convene business unit CEOs and leadership with the supplier’s executive team around that agenda, keeping the focus on forward value rather than issue escalation.
• Bring a single group view to each supplier, so that value found in one business unit is offered to all of them.
• Build an understanding of each supplier’s strategy, investment roadmap, capabilities and client base, and of where M&G sits in their priorities.
Opportunity Origination
• Identify and shape opportunities for innovation, joint savings, co-investment, capability the group does not use or has failed to exploit, and benchmarking and insight from the supplier’s wider client network.
• Build the business case for each opportunity, including net value to the group, costs, dependencies and risks, with input from Finance and the business owners affected.
• Test supplier proposals for whether they deliver net value to the group or are mainly footprint expansion, and hold the group’s commercial position when they are not.
• Hand qualified opportunities to the Technology or Services procurement teams to negotiate and contract, and support them through to close.
Working with Procurement Category Teams
• Align with the relevant category lead before any supplier executive conversation with commercial implications, so that no position is pre-sold or tested away from the people who negotiate.
• Share supplier intelligence and executive insight with category teams to strengthen their negotiation strategy and renewal planning.
• Operate the agreed joint attribution model with the category heads, crediting value jointly with the category team that closes the deal.
Working with In-Business Commercial Teams
• Maintain an informed view of supplier delivery through the business commercial teams, so that value conversations take account of current performance.
• Redirect delivery, performance and contract issues raised through executive channels to the accountable vendor management team, without taking ownership of them.
Value Measurement and Reporting
• Track and report value that lands: savings ideas converted to cost reduction, cost avoidance secured, co-investment obtained, innovation adopted and benchmark insight delivered.
• Agree baselines and value methodology with Finance, and report cost reduction and cost avoidance separately.
• Report progress against each supplier value agenda to Procurement leadership and group executive stakeholders.

• Use group spend data, Power BI dashboards and AI tools to build an enterprise view of each portfolio supplier across business units, and present a clear commercial account of what the data shows.
• Question data rather than accept it at face value, and work with Procurement colleagues to keep supplier data accurate.
This role has no delivery ownership and no negotiation authority. Its influence comes from access to business unit leadership, the enterprise view of spend and the quality of its insight. The postholder succeeds through other people’s deals. Candidates whose background is in conventional supplier relationship management or vendor performance roles should note that this role does not include those responsibilities.

We are recruiting a Paralegal to join our Fund Formation and Sponsor Solutions group on a 12-month fixed-term contract.
About Macfarlanes
Macfarlanes is a pre-eminent law firm that serves a global client base in Private Capital, Private Wealth, M&A and Disputes. Personal connection, an entrepreneurial spirit and a commitment to excellence are at the heart of our firm. These values drive our ability to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients.
We are big enough to undertake the most complex and demanding mandates yet small enough to know each other well and to be agile, adapting to the needs of our clients. We seek to strengthen the firm by recruiting talented people from all backgrounds who want to build long-lasting and impactful careers with us. Our culture is challenging and supportive, creating an environment where individuals can thrive.
What this means for you
Joining Macfarlanes means being part of a collaborative, Partner-led team where you’ll develop and learn from experienced lawyers and business professionals. Our size means you’ll be given genuine responsibility early on and often be involved at the heart of client matters, gaining insight into how our high-quality legal advice is developed and delivered to help clients overcome their most pressing issues.
You’ll work closely with senior colleagues who are approachable and who want you to succeed. You’ll be encouraged to get involved in client and business development activities, and you’ll be recognised for your contribution.
The majority of our work has a cross-border focus, so you’ll often collaborate with global clients and specialist advisers in overseas jurisdictions. You’ll build connections with international law firms, broaden your experience, and be part of a multidisciplinary team that comes together to achieve the best results.
We also place real importance on your development. Our training and mentoring programmes are second to none, and designed to help you strengthen your legal and commercial skills.
Above all, you’ll be part of a firm where we all work together as part of a cohesive and supportive team, where you’ll be recognised and appreciated, and encouraged to succeed.
Practice overview
Our Fund Formation and Sponsor Solutions group consists of eight Partners, two Senior Counsel, four Senior Associates, 16 Associates, six Trainee Solicitors, 14 Paralegals and one Senior Knowledge Lawyer.
Our Fund Formation and Sponsor Solutions group combines market leading funds and M&A expertise to advise sponsors, managers, investors and service providers across the full spectrum of global funds. We support at every phase of the lifecycle, providing counsel to UK and international managers on establishing funds in multi jurisdictions advising institutional investors, sovereign wealth funds and family offices on primary fund investments, co-investments and secondaries. Combined with our extensive sponsor-side experience, we have sharp market insight and positions us at the forefront of evolving industry practice. In addition, we advise on transactions across private capital and investment management, including seed capital arrangements, GP stake transactions, continuation vehicle structures and preferred equity solutions.
The role
This role will involve providing support to a key client of the firm and the successful individual will work full time with the client, who is one of Europe’s leading alternative asset management firms.
The individual will be required to carry out work that is accurate, well-structured and decision-ready. Key duties will include:
- assisting the deal team with the incorporation and set-up of various deal SPV structures in a variety of jurisdictions;
- overseeing the ongoing monitoring of these SPV structures working alongside the deal team and service providers;
- overseeing the sale or wind-up of these SPV structures;
- assisting the deal team with management of service providers relationships;
- leading corporate governance-related workstreams and tasks as and when required; and
- assisting with ad hoc administrative tasks as and when required including maintenance of internal records for SPV structures.
This job description encompasses the main duties of the role and is by no means exhaustive. It is anticipated that duties may vary from time to time according to the needs of the practice area.
The individual will receive the departmental training provided to all new joiners, as well as that provided to trainees.
The candidate
The successful candidate will:
- have worked as a paralegal before, ideally in entity management, corporate governance or company secretarial work;
- be confident and comfortable dealing with senior stakeholders and deal teams;
- like getting to grips with structure charts and understanding how complex group and deal structures fit together;
- be highly organised and pays close attention to detail, with the ability to manage many filing deadlines across a large number of entities;
- take a pro-active stance, able to work independently following appropriate instruction or in a team and take responsibility for the work product delivered; and
- be adaptable and quick to learn, comfortable picking up new structures, jurisdictions and local requirements as deals demand, and able to work out the right process where there is no precedent to follow.
Paralegal development programme
We have a paralegal development programme which is designed to equip our paralegals with the broad range of skills and knowledge they need to be effective in their roles. The programme also includes sessions covering essential legal and business skills required at the start of a career in law, recognising the fact that many solicitors begin their careers as paralegals.
Routes to qualification
Paralegals looking to qualify as associates are encouraged to apply for our Training Programme.
Some paralegals may prefer not to (or are unable to) undertake the Training Programme route for a variety of reasons, choosing the Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE) and Qualifying Work Experience (QWE) route instead. The firm will offer study leave and exam leave for paralegals sitting the SQE, and will sign off QWE (that meets the SRA’s requirements) gained at Macfarlanes. Internal paralegals that have qualified in this way may be considered for NQ vacancies not filled by those qualifying through the firm’s Training Programme and where the firm is or may be looking to recruit externally providing they have completed at least one year of their QWE at Macfarlanes and passed both SQE 1 and SQE 2 on the first attempt.
Application screening
Any offer of employment with us is subject to our pre-employment checks which are conducted by a third-party screening provider. These may include but are not limited to your professional and academic qualifications, any criminal records and employment references. These checks will be initiated with your consent and your offer will be subject to the successful completion of these checks.
Our commitment to inclusion
Inclusion is one of our key priorities and it is a goal we are actively working towards. We believe that an inclusive, forward-thinking culture is intrinsically important and enables us to provide innovative solutions to our clients.
We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, bringing different perspectives and experiences, making Macfarlanes an exciting and stimulating place to work. We seek to recruit the best candidates, regardless of age, gender, race, ethnicity, social or economic background, religion, disability, sexual orientation or any other characteristic.
As part of this commitment, we will ask you certain diversity data questions. We would really appreciate you and/or your recruiter completing these questions when submitting an application to Macfarlanes as this data enables us to measure our progress and identify any actions needed to continue to support an inclusive culture. This data is anonymised to maintain the privacy of applicants. If you have any questions relating to how this data is used, please contact a member of the recruitment team.
Should you require any adjustments during the application and/or interview process, please do not hesitate to inform your recruiter or a member of the recruitment team. Please note, the job description is available in other accessible formats (for example, large print).

The opportunity
We are looking for an experienced Area Facilities Manager to lead the management of our office, warehouse and depot facilities. You will also lead the reception team and help create workplace environments that support operational performance, employee wellbeing and employee experience.
Key responsibilities
• Manage the property portfolio, including lease reviews, renewals, negotiations, new premises, lease exits and dilapidations, in partnership with Legal and Corporate Real Estate.
• Assess current and future facilities requirements and develop practical plans that support capacity, business growth and effective use of space.
• Lead the procurement and contract management of facilities services, including cleaning, catering, utilities, pest control and local authority services, ensuring clear service levels, strong supplier performance and value for money.
• Maintain strong supplier and landlord relationships, ensuring suppliers are onboarded correctly, contractual obligations are clear and value for money is achieved, while driving continuous improvement in service quality and performance.
• Own facilities budgets, forecasting and cost control, maintaining accurate records of commitments and identifying opportunities to improve utilisation and reduce cost.
• Partner with business leaders to assess investment needs and deliver improvements that support operations, employee experience, security and health and safety.
• Plan and deliver refurbishment, repair and maintenance programmes, ensuring required inspections, statutory checks and landlord obligations are completed, while promoting preventive maintenance practices that improve asset reliability and reduce long-term costs.

• Work closely with the Area HSE Lead to ensure incidents are reported, escalated and investigated appropriately, with corrective actions completed to reduce recurrence.
• Lead and develop the reception team, ensuring a professional service that meets the day-to-day needs of each location.
• Promote sustainable facilities practices, including energy efficiency, waste reduction and responsible use of resources where appropriate.
What success looks like
• Facilities capacity, workplace services and working environments consistently support business and operational needs.
• Lease commitments, supplier relationships and service contracts are proactively managed and deliver value for money.
• Maintenance programmes, statutory compliance and audit outcomes demonstrate strong governance and effective risk management.
• Budgets and forecasts are accurate, well-controlled and delivered within agreed parameters, excluding approved investments.
• Workplaces are safe, compliant, well maintained and provide a positive employee experience across all Area locations.
• Health, safety and security issues are addressed promptly, with effective corrective actions implemented and sustained.
About you
• A number of years’ experience in multi-site or mixed-use facilities management, or in a comparable role with directly transferable experience.
• A NEBOSH General Certificate qualification.
• Experience of acquiring new facilities, managing lease exits and overseeing dilapidations.
• A sound understanding of commercial lease agreements, legal clauses and commonly accepted terms.
• Strong commercial, procurement and negotiation skills, with experience managing contracts, suppliers, budgets and forecasts.
• Proven ability to plan and deliver maintenance, refurbishment or facilities improvement projects.
• Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage schedules, records and competing priorities.
• A confident, collaborative stakeholder manager who can build effective relationships across a geographically dispersed business.
• A proactive, employee-focused approach and the ability to translate business strategy into an area facilities plan that improves workplace experience and operational effectiveness.
• Willingness to travel regularly across the Area to support all facilities.
Key relationships
• You will work closely with the Area Leadership Team, Area CFO, Area HSE Manager, Security Manager, Corporate Real Estate, Legal, landlords and facilities service providers.

job_description:
Job Summary
The Director, Commercial AI & Automation Product Delivery, EMEA provides dedicated leadership and execution capacity to identify, prioritise, design and deliver high-value AI and automation solutions across the wider Commercial Services organisation.
The role operates at the intersection of Commercial business expertise, process improvement, product delivery and applied technology. It works with Commercial leaders and operational teams to identify the most important business problems, map and simplify the underlying process, determine where AI or automation can add measurable value, and move selected opportunities from concept through prototype, proof of value, deployment and adoption.
This is not a pure strategy, portfolio coordination or software engineering role. The Director is accountable for converting Commercial priorities into practical, adopted solutions and measurable outcomes. The role requires sufficient technical capability to prototype and deliver fit-for-purpose solutions using approved tools, including Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate and Power Apps, while recognising when enterprise technology, data, security or specialist development support is required.
The Director serves as the senior Commercial product and delivery owner for this portfolio, making recommendations on where to invest, scale, route, revise or stop work. The role partners with EMEA AI governance and central orchestration, while remaining anchored within Commercial Services where business context, process ownership and accountability for execution sit.
Key Responsibilities
• Own and actively manage a prioritised portfolio of Commercial AI and automation opportunities aligned with profitable revenue growth, Commercial 30, HOME, and productivity priorities.
• Evaluate opportunities using business value, user impact, process and data readiness, feasibility, risk, scalability, adoption potential and alignment with enterprise capabilities. Recommend which initiatives should proceed, combine, route, defer or stop.
• Partner with Commercial discipline leaders, regional teams, subject-matter experts and users to diagnose material business pain points and determine whether the answer is process change, clearer accountability, automation, AI or a combination.
• Translate ambiguous business needs into clear problem statements, process maps, requirements, test scopes, success measures and proof-of-value plans. Challenge requests constructively where technology would automate the wrong process or create insufficient value.
• Lead selected use cases from discovery through prototype, testing, governance review, deployment, adoption and benefit measurement, maintaining clear stage gates, owners, decisions and delivery momentum.
• Act as the senior Commercial product owner, making or facilitating decisions on scope, priorities, user experience, business requirements and release readiness across multiple disciplines and stakeholder groups.
• Use practical knowledge of Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps and related approved tools to explore solutions, build prototypes and deliver appropriate low-code automations.
• Assess when a solution can be delivered within Commercial and when it requires support from IT, HQ AI Studio, Data & Analytics, Information Security, Privacy, Legal or specialist engineering teams. Ensure solutions use approved pathways and do not create unsupported shadow technology.
• Build adoption, communication, training, change impact and support requirements into delivery from the outset. Engage users throughout discovery, testing and refinement so solutions fit real workflows and can be sustained.
• Track usage, user feedback, operational performance and realised benefits after implementation. Establish clear ownership and support arrangements before broader deployment.
• Capture reusable components, patterns and playbooks so successful solutions can be applied across Commercial teams, markets or hotels where appropriate.
• Partner with the EMEA AI orchestration team to provide visibility of the Commercial portfolio, identify overlaps and reuse opportunities, and route solutions appropriately without duplicating central orchestration responsibilities.
• Provide Commercial leadership with concise, evidence-based updates on progress, benefits, risks, resource needs, blockers and decisions required. Surface recurring process, data or capability barriers that limit delivery.
• Influence senior stakeholders across Commercial, continent and HQ teams, balancing competing priorities while protecting scarce delivery capacity and maintaining a strong bias toward practical execution and measurable outcomes.
Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is a commercially grounded, technology-fluent delivery leader who can move comfortably between senior stakeholder discussions, business processes, user needs and hands-on solution development. They must be credible enough to make continent-wide portfolio and prioritisation recommendations, practical enough to work directly with process owners and users, and technically confident enough to prototype, challenge solution design and make sound delivery decisions.
This role is not intended for a narrow technical specialist whose primary strength is coding, or for a general strategist whose contribution ends with recommendations and roadmaps. It requires a balanced leader who can determine what should be built, shape how it should work, mobilise the right contributors and remain accountable until the solution is operating and delivering value.
• Significant experience in Commercial e.g. revenue management, sales, marketing, digital, distribution, loyalty, commercial operations, or a closely related field.
• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from ambiguous business need through implementation, adoption and measurable outcome.
• Strong Commercial acumen and judgement on value, feasibility, operational impact, scalability, adoption risk and return on investment.
• Practical experience with AI, low-code and workflow automation, particularly Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate and Power Apps. Able to build prototypes or fit-for-purpose solutions while recognising when specialist technical development is required.
• Strong capability in process mapping, requirements gathering, testing, change adoption, benefit tracking and product or programme delivery.
• High credibility with senior business and technical stakeholders, with the ability to influence across functions and geographies without relying on direct authority.
• Good understanding of enterprise data, privacy, security, responsible AI and governance considerations.
• Ability to simplify complex issues, challenge constructively, communicate in clear business language and maintain disciplined follow-through in a matrix organisation.
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. Relevant Microsoft Power Platform, AI, product, agile, process improvement or change qualifications are advantageous but not essential.
Leadership Scope and Role Boundaries
The Director owns Commercial use-case prioritisation, business problem definition, process clarity, product decisions, proof-of-value design, appropriate hands-on prototyping, delivery momentum, adoption planning and benefit realisation. The role carries end-to-end accountability for a cross-discipline EMEA portfolio rather than executing assigned automation requests.
The Director partners on enterprise governance, cross-discipline portfolio visibility, technical architecture, security, data access, complex integrations and scaled production support. The role does not own enterprise AI governance, central EMEA orchestration, general Commercial strategy and planning, technology architecture or specialist software engineering.
Success Measures
• Measurable business value, productivity or Commercial performance improvement delivered through implemented solutions.
• A focused, transparent portfolio with clear priorities, ownership, stage gates, risks and evidence-based scale, route or stop decisions.
• Improved speed from validated business need to usable prototype or solution, without compromising approved governance and technical pathways.
• Strong adoption, usage, user feedback and sustainable ownership for deployed solutions.
• Reduction in duplicated, disconnected or low-value experimentation and improved reuse of successful solutions across teams, markets or hotels.
• Quality of business problem definition, process mapping, requirements, testing and benefit measurement.
• Effective collaboration with Commercial disciplines, EMEA governance and orchestration, IT, HQ AI Studio, Data & Analytics and other enterprise partners.
• Clear evidence that Commercial AI and automation work is moving from discussion and experimentation to practical execution and measurable outcomes.
Key Working Relationships
EMEA Commercial Services leadership; Commercial discipline and process owners; regional and field stakeholders; EMEA AI governance and orchestration; EMEA and HQ IT; HQ AI Studio; Data & Analytics; Information Security, Privacy and Legal; HR/L&D and change partners; Digital Operations, low-code builders and approved external partners.
Right to work
At the time of application, applicants must have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Unfortunately, this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.

Overview of the job
Our prisons have industry-standard engineering workshops across the estate which manufacture products for the Prison Service as well as other government departments. 
Typical products manufactured includes metal beds, in cell bins, staff and visitor lockers, bespoke staircases, storage pallets, chairs, fence posts and anti-drone window grills.
Our workshops are well equipped with modern machinery including CNC machines, laser punches, tube benders, welding stations, and powder coat plants.
As a specialist production instructor in fabricating and welding, you will be responsible for using your knowledge and experience to train and supervise the prisoners in the workshop so that they undertake the manufacturing work required to meet production targets.
This is an opportunity to genuinely change lives of prisoners – imparting your knowledge and enabling prisoners to develop a strong work ethic, on the job skills, and a passion for the work that they do.  Developing new employable skills, a thirst for knowledge and a structured working day is key to reducing reoffending by supporting post-release employment.
You will be responsible for delivering nationally recognised qualifications to prisoners where relevant, ensuring that the course content is covered and that progress is recorded.  Support is given as required.
Within the prison environment you will be responsible for maintaining control of prisoners under your supervision, as well as following all relevant security processes such as using a radio and security, undertaking tool checks and maintaining a prisoner roll count.

Job description
Proud to Serve. Proud to keep justice going.  
Our Court Associates are essential to ensure Magistrates Court hearings run smoothly.  They have the self-assurance to communicate confidently with the Judge and all participants and the skill to produce accurate and timely Court documents.   
About us    
HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS) is responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family Courts and Tribunals in England and Wales. Our roles support our service users and colleagues within HMCTS, where people and businesses access potentially life-changing justice.  We’re looking for individuals who are committed to public service and making a difference in people’s lives to deliver justice. If you are interested in developing a career with a real purpose, please apply.    
About you   
You’re a confident communicator; able to speak publicly, with the self-assurance to confidently liaise with the Judge, the defence, prosecution, media, members of the public and more, regarding complex and sensitive matters in a calm and professional manner.    
A real team player, working within a Legal Team and with a Judge, you’ll ensure the smooth running of all the Magistrates Courts sitting daily, able to intervene in Court when required and maximise judicial sitting time.  With experience in producing exact and time critical documentation, your ability to focus will be key in taking pleas, producing Court orders and recording hearing outcomes accurately and efficiently.  
Resilient and keen to learn, you’re familiar with working within process and have the IT skills to adapt to new systems and technologies as we’re constantly investing in digital solutions to improve the way we deliver the justice people deserve in today’s world.   
 Your skills and experience 
* Ability to be a supportive team player delivering excellent customer service and achieve effective performance. 
* Able to speak publicly and within a court room environment.
* Excellent communication, organisational and prioritisation skills.
* Ability to complete documents accurately and to deadlines.
* IT proficient with the ability to learn and adapt to different technologies and software packages. 
This role gives you the opportunity to make a difference in delivering justice and gives you the benefits developing your career in the Civil Service.

Overview of the job
This is a management role within the National Probation Service (NPS).
The Senior Probation Officer supports the Head of Operational Function to provide management and a leading role within a Local Delivery Unit (LDU) or other operational unit.
Summary
The job holder will be expected to manage and lead staff within the operational area to the required standard, and will offer support and cover to other teams/functions during periods of absence.  
In line with NPS policies and procedures, the job holder must at all times demonstrate a commitment to equality and inclusion and an understanding of their relevance to the work they do. 
The post holder must adhere to all policies in respect of the sensitive/confidential nature of the information handled whilst working in this position.

Responsibilities, Activities & Duties
               Senior Probation Officers may be required to undertake any combination, or all, of the duties and responsibilities set out below. 
•             To provide effective management and leadership to the team
•             To be accountable for the quality delivery of good practice and team performance improvement within policy and national standards
•             To ensure that all team resources, including interventions, are deployed cost effectively and provide best value in terms of both budget control and realising the organisation’s strategic aims

Role title: JCL Content Administrator
Team/Directorate: Judicial College Content Team
Overview of the Judicial Office
The Judicial Office (JO) reports to, and is accountable, to the Lady Chief Justice (LCJ). It was established in 2006 to provide support to the LCJ and to the wider judiciary in upholding the rule of law and in delivering justice impartially, speedily and efficiently, following the Constitutional Reform Act 2005.
In addition, we support, and are accountable to, the Senior President of Tribunals, whose responsibilities extend to Scotland and Northern Ireland.
The JO is an interesting and unique place to work. Everything we do is in support of upholding the independence and impartiality of the judiciary. We work closely with HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS), the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) and others across Government as well as with the legal professions.
We are an Arm’s Length Body sponsored by the Ministry of Justice. This creates an interesting and complex environment in which to work where we agree our priorities with the senior judiciary and receive our funding to deliver them from the Ministry of Justice. The Judicial Office has been through a period of significant growth resulting from an expansion of our remit and responsibilities.
See JO staff talk about working here: https://design102.wistia.com/medias/uhgtmbtnlv
Overview of the team  
The Judicial College is part of the Judicial Office ─ a unique part of the Civil Service, independent from government and dedicated to supporting the judiciary and promoting and safeguarding judicial independence to maintain confidence in the rule of law. The College supports the Lady Chief Justice, Senior President of Tribunals and the Chief Coroner to fulfil their statutory responsibilities for training the judiciary in an evolving justice system. We support the judicial leadership of the College to set strategic direction and advise on the design and delivery of the training programme. We deliver around 1800 courses to around 25,000 office holders every year. We aim to be a world leader in judicial education.
For more information see:
 www.judiciary.uk  and https://www.linkedin.com/company/judicial-office/
Working with the College Board, the Judicial College supports these senior members of the judiciary in setting the direction for training and ensuring the College has the right support in place to provide advice on the design and delivery of training, innovative digital systems to support delivery and that seminars are well organised. Our purpose is to strengthen the rule of law and improve the administration of justice through delivery of essential training for the judiciary in courts and tribunals, as well as a framework of training for magistrates. 
The Judicial College Learning Team plays an integral part in supporting the training programme and judicial office holder access to resources through our digital learning platform, Judicial College Learning (JCL) which is a Totara based platform.  The team works closely with colleagues across the College, Digital Services and judicial stakeholders to ensure the system meets user needs, identify improvements, develop new functionality and make the best use of data held on the system. The team serves as the central coordination point for all matters related to the JCL, including content held on the platform, the governance around the system and its content, using feedback to make improvements and deal with any emerging issues relating to functionality, content and date.
In addition to the management of the digital platform, the JCL team plays a key role in coordinating and management of future developments to the system to meet business and user needs and new design principles.  The team lead on project management, stakeholder engagement and change management.  This includes developing and delivering guidance and training to both staff and the judiciary on how to use the system where changes are made.  In managing content on the system and functionality, the team oversee the design, layout and content held on the system to ensure that users have the best possible experience, and that features, and content are accessible.

Job description
Introduction
The Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority (CICA) is an executive agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ). We receive over 40,000 applications every year for compensation, from people who have lost loved ones or have been injured as a result of violent crime. We know financial compensation can never fully redress what they have suffered. Nevertheless, what we do is an important part of providing justice for victims and we take pride that the compensation we pay helps people move forward with their lives.
We employ around 350 people and are based in Glasgow city centre. We are a small, engaged, productive workforce with a real sense of corporate community. We want to keep improving our services and the way we work to best serve the public, meet new challenges, deliver value for money and ensure CICA is a great place to work.
The role is based 10 Clyde Place, Glasgow, G5 8AQ and we currently operate a hybrid working business model, where a typical employee works 50% of their week from the office.
The Role
The role will support CICA’s ambition to provide an accessible and trauma-informed service that treats victims with compassion, sensitivity and fairness. It will drive improvements to applicant experience, ensuring our contact strategy is efficient, effective and trauma-informed.
The post holder will manage the Applicant Contact Team and Complaints Resolution Team, with direct line management responsibility for seven Higher Executive Officers (HEO’s). They will lead the delivery of high-quality, victim-centred services, ensuring resources are managed effectively and services respond to the needs of applicants.
The postholder will coach and develop their teams, embed best practice and use insights from applicant feedback, complaints and service trends to inform improvement activity and interventions. They will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to ensure activity aligns with wider objectives and legislative frameworks including the Public Service Ombudsman and Scottish Public Service Ombudsman guidelines.
Duties and responsibilities
Applicant Engagement & Insight
* Develop and deliver engagement approaches that strengthen CICA’s understanding of applicant needs, expectations, and experiences.
* Maintain strong working relationships with key stakeholders including internal and external stakeholders; such as Ombudsman, Victim Support organisations and other MOJ departments
* Chair or support internal engagement forums to ensure staff understand the applicant perspective and contribute to service improvement.
* Promote awareness of applicant insights across operational and corporate teams to embed a culture of improvement.
* Manage complaint escalations which require senior oversight, including working with the Chief Executive office to manage enquiries submitted directly to the Chief Executive.
Leadership & Collaboration
* Provide visible leadership within the Applicant Engagement Contact Team and Complaint Resolutions team, setting clear expectations and supporting staff development
* Work collaboratively with operational leaders to implement improvements identified through complaints analysis and applicant feedback
* Ensure consistent application of guidance, templates, and processes across all engagement and complaints activity
* Represent CICA at relevant cross government networks, forums, and stakeholder engagement groups
General Responsibilities
* Contribute to - and lead on where appropriate - the development and continuous improvement of internal guidance, templates, and resources to support consistent, efficient and compliant service delivery

Working closely with the Managing Director, Commercial Operations Director, Commercial Compliance team, Global Value team and market stakeholders, the role acts as a critical link between clients, regional leadership and local market teams.
Operating across multiple markets and client relationships, the role is responsible for driving the adoption and effective delivery of Commercial Products, ensuring client commitments are clearly communicated and consistently executed, and maintaining strong governance and compliance standards. The role requires a Quantity Surveyor who demonstrates professional curiosity and competence in the appropriate use of digital tools, data and emerging artificial intelligence to support cost management, commercial advice and informed decision‑making. This includes a willingness to continuously develop knowledge of digital and AI‑enabled practices that improve efficiency, accuracy and client outcomes, without compromising independence, transparency or professional accountability. 
 
We believe in nurturing talent, celebrating achievements, and creating opportunities for growth. You’ll be empowered to contribute meaningfully, learn continuously, and help deliver projects that make a real difference to society.

We are looking to expand our Transport Modelling team within our Transport & Mobility Solutions business. You will work on a diverse range of transport modelling and appraisal projects for major clients including the Department for Transport, National Highways, East West Rail and Heathrow Airport, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across the UK and internationally.

Taking responsibility for the development and application of strategic multi-modal transport models, using software such as PTV Visum, SATURN, CUBE or equivalent.
Planning and coordinating modelling activities including data analysis, model development, calibration, validation, forecasting, scenario testing and appraisal.
Analysing and interpreting model outputs to provide evidence for transport strategies, business cases and scheme assessments, applying technical judgement to address modelling issues and identify appropriate approaches.
Reviewing technical outputs against relevant guidance, quality requirements and industry best practice.
Developing and applying data analysis, scripting and automation to improve modelling processes, quality assurance and reproducibility, and identifying useful applications of AI and emerging digital technologies.
Producing clear technical outputs, contributing to technical discussions with clients and providing guidance and support to less-experienced colleagues.
Contributing to project planning and the preparation of modelling scopes, programmes, budgets and proposals.

Essential:
Practical experience of developing and applying strategic transport models using PTV Visum, SATURN, CUBE or comparable software, including responsibility for modelling activities or work packages.
Experience across key elements of transport modelling, including model development, calibration, validation, forecasting and model application, with the ability to identify and apply appropriate technical approaches.
The ability to take responsibility for modelling workstreams, coordinate activities with colleagues and deliver high-quality outputs with appropriate senior support.
The ability to analyse modelling results, address technical issues, review the work of others and communicate evidence-based recommendations clearly.
An understanding of relevant transport modelling guidance, quality assurance and the application of modelling to support transport decision-making, with experience of discussing technical approaches and findings with clients and colleagues.
A relevant numerical or analytical qualification, or equivalent relevant experience.
 
Desirable:
Experience in one or more of the following would be beneficial:
Python or other scripting and automation tools, including developing reusable approaches that improve modelling efficiency and quality.
GIS, data visualisation, SQL, Git or other digital/data tools.
Variable-demand modelling, economic appraisal or microsimulation.
Practical use of AI and emerging digital technologies to make technical workflows more efficient, robust or insightful, including identifying opportunities to apply these approaches more widely.
Contributing to project management, technical proposals, bids or the development of modelling scopes and budgets.

• Develop and maintain freight reporting tools, dashboards and performance metrics.

• Develop clear recommendations that support planning, provider performance management and operational decision-making.

• Support peak and capacity planning through accurate forecasts, shipment profiles and analysis of expected inbound volumes.
Continuous Improvement and Cost Control
• Support continuous improvement initiatives through baseline analysis, performance measurement and benefits tracking.
• Identify opportunities to improve reporting efficiency, data quality, shipment visibility and operational performance.
• Assist with freight invoice validation by comparing charges against shipment data, agreed rates and supporting information.
• Produce cost reporting and variance analysis to support accurate accruals, financial control and informed decision-making.
Stakeholder Partnership and Communication
• Build effective working relationships with freight providers and colleagues across Supply Chain, Inventory, Supplier Compliance, Distribution Centres and Finance.
• Respond to reporting and data requests with accurate, timely and clearly presented information.
• Explain trends, exceptions and recommendations in a concise way that supports operational action and decision-making.
• Promote consistent use of Apollo, agreed reports and data standards across the business.
Experience and Knowledge
• Experience in a freight, logistics, supply chain, planning or operational analysis role, ideally within retail or consumer goods.
• Strong analytical and numerical capability, with experience interpreting large operational datasets and translating findings into practical insight.
• Advanced Excel skills and experience creating dashboards, KPI reports and repeatable reporting tools; experience with Power BI or similar visualisation tools is desirable.
• Understanding of purchase orders, international freight milestones, shipment tracking, transit times and inbound supply chain operations.
• Experience improving data quality, investigating discrepancies and maintaining reliable master or operational data.
• Knowledge of freight costs, invoice validation and provider performance measures would be advantageous.
Skills and Behaviours
• Analytical and inquisitive, with strong attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy.
• Highly organised, able to manage recurring reporting cycles, competing requests and time-sensitive operational analysis.
• Clear and concise communicator, able to present complex data and trends in an accessible, decision-focused way.
• Proactive problem-solver who follows issues through to resolution and constructively challenges poor-quality information.
• Collaborative and service-focused, with the confidence to work effectively with freight providers and stakeholders at different levels.
• Curious and improvement-minded, continually looking for better ways to report, automate and communicate performance.
• Accountable and dependable, with a strong focus on deadlines, accuracy and practical business outcomes.

job_description:
We are seeking a commercially minded lawyer to join the in-house legal team at Mountain Warehouse, specialising in data protection and commercial contracts.
Reporting to the Head of Legal, you will provide practical advice on the use of personal data across our retail, e-commerce and international operations, alongside drafting and negotiating commercial agreements. Data protection and privacy
• Advise on data protection and privacy matters across the business, coordinating local legal advice where required for international operations.

• Draft, review and maintain privacy notices, data protection policies, data processing agreements and data sharing arrangements.
• Advise on lawful bases for processing, transparency, retention and the handling of customer and employee personal data.
• Support data protection impact assessments, records of processing activities and international data transfer arrangements.
• Advise on direct marketing, cookies, customer profiling and loyalty programmes.
• Coordinate responses to data subject requests and privacy complaints, working with relevant business teams.
• Provide legal support for personal data breaches and cybersecurity incidents, including assessing notification requirements and supporting regulatory communications.
• Conduct privacy reviews of suppliers and advise on contractual safeguards for personal data.
• Advise on privacy issues arising from artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.
• Deliver practical training and monitor legal developments relevant to the business.
Commercial contracts
• Draft, review and negotiate commercial agreements, including IT, software, cloud services, digital platforms, marketing, consultancy, supplier and confidentiality agreements.
• Advise on contractual risk, including liability, indemnities, intellectual property, termination rights and service continuity.
• Support procurement and operational teams throughout negotiations, explaining material risks and recommending workable solutions.
• Assist with contractual disputes and work with the business and external advisers to achieve practical resolutions.
• Develop and maintain contract templates, negotiation guidance and approval processes.
Wider legal support
• Provide timely, accessible legal advice to colleagues across the business.
• Support e-commerce, consumer law and advertising matters connected with digital and marketing activities.
• Work with IT and information security colleagues on the legal aspects of cybersecurity and information governance.
• Support corporate transactions and business integration projects on data protection and commercial matters.
• Identify matters requiring escalation and keep the Head of Legal informed of significant risks and developments.
• Instruct and coordinate external advisers where specialist or local advice is required.
Essential
• Qualified solicitor in England and Wales with relevant experience in data protection and commercial law.
• Strong working knowledge of UK data protection and privacy requirements, including the UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018 and rules governing electronic marketing and cookies.
• Experience advising on EU GDPR requirements and international data transfers.
• Experience drafting and negotiating commercial contracts, particularly technology agreements and data processing arrangements.
• Ability to translate legal requirements into clear, proportionate advice and practical business processes.
• Strong drafting, negotiation and communication skills.
• Confidence managing a varied workload, taking ownership of matters and recognising when to seek guidance or escalate issues.
• Ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical colleagues.
Desirable
• Previous in-house experience or a client secondment.
• Experience advising retailers, e-commerce businesses or organisations handling substantial volumes of customer data.
• Experience supporting breach response, regulatory enquiries and complex data subject requests.
• Familiarity with advertising technology, customer analytics and artificial intelligence.
• A recognised privacy qualification, such as CIPP/E or CIPM.
Personal approach
You will be practical, organised and comfortable working in a fast-moving business. You should take an interest in how data and technology support our operations, identify the issues that matter and propose workable solutions. You will combine sound legal judgement with a collaborative approach and the confidence to challenge proposals constructively.

A varied in-house role working closely with the Head of Legal, with meaningful responsibility for data protection and commercial matters and the opportunity to support Mountain Warehouse’s digital development and international operations.

- We’ll look to you to suggest areas of customer and business focused improvement, contributing towards a culture of continuous improvement
- It’s a critical role, where you’ll be recognised for your subject matter expertise, within the fraud prevention team, on emerging trends and evolving customer needs

- An awareness of changes in trends, policies and regulations applicable to fraud prevention and recoveries
- An understanding of the industry and our customers, including products, processes and fraud prevention systems
- Experience of managing stakeholder relationships
- Commercial Credit Card TSYS knowledge is preferable

The Kernel team builds the storage engine and transaction machinery inside Neo4j. If you join us, you will not be building web APIs or shuffling data between services. Instead, you will be working directly on the database engine itself.
Our day-to-day is low-level systems engineering. We write and maintain custom storage engines, the page cache, transaction handling (WAL, ACID guarantees), indexing, and memory management. The code we write determines how fast queries run across billions of nodes and relationships, and how safely data is written when a machine crashes.
We are a pragmatic, engineering-led group split between Malmö and London. We read and discuss database papers (VLDB, SIGMOD, and others) to see what ideas are worth pulling into the product. We also run regular “Do What You Want” weeks so everyone has dedicated time to experiment with their own prototypes or tooling improvements.
What you will actually be doing:
• Designing, profiling, and implementing core database features, including storage formats, index structures, and recovery paths.
• Diagnosing tricky concurrency bugs, race conditions, and lock contention.
• Performance engineering: profiling CPU, memory allocation, off-heap memory, and disk I/O to improve latency.
• Reviewing designs and PRs with a heavy focus on correctness, data integrity, and long-term maintainability.
• Helping decide technical direction and architectural trade-offs as our engine evolves.
What we are looking for:
• Systems programming experience: You are comfortable working close to the hardware. Most of our codebase is Java, but if your background is in C++, Rust, or Go and you understand memory layouts and concurrency, that translates well.
• Concurrency and data structures: You have a clear understanding of threads, locks, atomic operations, cache locality, and algorithmic complexity.
• Pragmatic engineering: You write thorough tests because edge cases in database kernels are painful to debug in production.
• Collaborative attitude: You are comfortable having your technical choices questioned, you back up decisions with data or benchmarks, and you treat code review as a two-way discussion rather than a hurdle.
It is a bonus if you have:
• Prior experience with database internals, storage engines, or file systems.
• Deep knowledge of JVM internals, such as GC behavior, JIT compilation, and off-heap memory.
• Hands-on experience with profiling tools like async-profiler, JFR, or perf.

ABOUT US
People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry.
Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality.
Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.
 
HOW WE WORK
- Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents.
- Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.
- At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.
- End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.
- In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication.
- Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.
- Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.
 
THE ROLE
We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.
You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.
Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.
- Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.
- AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.
- Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.
 
WHAT WE LOOK FOR
- A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.
- Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.
- High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.
- Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.
- Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.
 
WHY JOIN
You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.

About Niantic Spatial
AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It can't yet reason about real places well enough for robots, field crews and AI agents to rely on it, and closing that gap will change how factories, power grids, cities and defense operations run.
That's one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it's the one we're solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.
In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That's why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.
Our team built some of the world's most widely used maps. Now we're building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.
About the Role
The Large Geospatial Model is Niantic Spatial's foundation model of the physical world. It learns from years of real-world captures of millions of places, and people, robots and AI agents use it to find out where they are, what is around them and what has changed. Each step up in scale has given the model capabilities it did not have before. The next problems are some of the hardest in AI: filling in the parts of a place no camera saw while marking what was inferred, measuring what changed between visits, and predicting what will change next.
Customers already use the model in production. Energy companies use it to guide field crews to equipment on large industrial sites, defense partners use it for positioning where GPS is jammed or unavailable, and robotics companies train robots in metric-scale copies of the real sites they will work in.
You will be the first product leader for the model and the data it learns from, reporting to the Chief Product Officer. You decide which capabilities it gains and in what order, the bar each release has to clear, and what data Niantic Spatial collects, licenses or partners for to get there. You set those priorities directly with the Chief Scientist and the London research team who train the model.
If you have shipped a frontier language model, most of the job will be familiar: evals, data mix and release decisions. The job differs in two ways. Every output of this model can be scored against a measured real place, so its evals rest on ground truth. And its data is collected in the physical world, so choosing what to capture next is a product decision with a real cost. Experience in 3D or mapping is welcome but not required.
By the end of your first year, research, engineering and the product leads for industrial, defense, robotics and platform customers work from one model roadmap that you own, each release ships against evals you wrote, and the model's newest capabilities are in customers' hands.
What You'll Do
Own the Model Roadmap - Decide the order in which the Large Geospatial Model gains its next capabilities, from filling in unseen parts of a site to measuring and predicting change, based on what industrial, defense, robotics and platform customers will pay for. Turn customer problems into specific research requirements, and bring new research results to the product leads who sell into each market.
Set the Release Bar - Define the evals and acceptance criteria for each capability with the Real-World Test Lab, which measures model output against ground truth in real places. Decide whether each release ships or goes back for more data or training.
Own the Data Plan - Decide what data Niantic Spatial collects, buys, licenses or gets through partners, and set the product terms of those deals with Legal and Business Development. Set the curation, labeling, consent, privacy and training-rights requirements every dataset has to meet, and keep a record of which data went into each model version.
Turn Capabilities into Products - Decide when a new model capability is ready to become something customers buy, what it promises them, and how it reaches them through Niantic Spatial's products and platform.
Set the Long-Term Direction - Decide where the model goes over the next several years, as it moves from describing places as they are to tracking how they change and anticipating what comes next, and make the case for the research and data investment that takes.
What You'll Bring
8+ years in product management, including at least three years shipping a large model to users or customers.
Experience writing evals for a model and using them to decide when a release was ready.
Direct work on training data, such as setting a data mix, running labeling or human-feedback programs, or negotiating data licenses.
Enough depth in how large models are trained, post-trained and evaluated that researchers bring you into their technical decisions. Many strong candidates for this role were ML engineers or researchers before they moved into product.
Experience setting direction for research and engineering teams that did not report to you.
A bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Nice to Have
Experience in 3D computer vision, reconstruction, localization, mapping, geospatial data, robotics or autonomous systems.
An advanced degree in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, or a related field.
Experience with Gaussian splatting, neural fields or visual positioning systems.
Experience with government or defense requirements for data provenance and security.

Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office.

We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed - you may be exactly who we're looking for.

Validating conventional silicon is a solved discipline. Validating silicon that computes with noise is not, and you will be the one who figures out how. As our FPGA Design Engineer, you will own the bridge between RTL and physical silicon: bringing our physics-inspired ASIC designs to life on FPGA platforms for pre-silicon validation and early software development, and building the test infrastructure for post-silicon bring-up and characterization. - IP Integration: Integrate in-house designs with third-party and vendor IP; serve as the expert on the AMD/Xilinx ecosystem (Vivado IP Integrator, transceivers, memory controllers).
- High-Speed Interfaces: Design, implement, and validate high-speed I/O with a focus on PCIe: our accelerators ship as PCIe cards in standard servers.

- Hardware-Software Stack: Develop the software layer around the hardware: Python/C++ hardware abstraction, register-map generation, and automated build and regression flows.
- Lab Debug: Root-cause complex timing and functional issues in real time using ILA/Vivado Analyzer, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and BER/eye-diagram characterization of high-speed links.
WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT FIT
- Proven industry experience taking FPGA designs from RTL through timing closure to validated hardware, ideally in an ASIC prototyping, emulation, or high-growth hardware environment.
- Expert-level SystemVerilog and/or VHDL for synthesis, with deep proficiency in Xilinx Vivado (synthesis, place & route, timing closure, IP catalog).
- Hands-on experience implementing and debugging PCIe, plus AXI/AHB, SPI, UART, JTAG, and other common interfaces.
- Strong Python for automation, test, and build tooling.
- Strong board-level bring-up and lab debugging skills on real hardware.
- Startup mindset: you work independently, pivot quickly, and run at ambiguous problems that span hardware, software, and physics.
BONUS POINTS
- Verification frameworks like Cocotb or UVM
- Experience deploying ML models to FPGAs (hls4ml, FINN, or custom NN-to-RTL flows), or building real-time, sub-microsecond signal processing pipelines.

job_title: Head of Customer Adoption & Value- Primary Care
job_description:
Join OneAdvanced
You will lead the national Customer Adoption & Value function for Primary Care, providing line leadership, coaching, standards and direction to Customer Adoption & Value Leads working within the regional Pod model. You will work closely with the Services Team to ensure that we remain consistent in our approach to customer success across OneAdvanced.
You will also lead the shared Community capability, with one Community Lead focused on England and one on Scotland, using customer communities, user groups, peer networks, digital engagement and advocacy to scale engagement beyond one-to-one customer interaction.
You will establish a common Customer Adoption & Value operating model across Primary Care (in conjunction with the Services Team), including customer health, adoption measures, value plans, renewal readiness, intervention playbooks, segmentation and consistent ways of working. The model must be sufficiently standardised to create visibility and accountability, while allowing for genuine differences between customers, regions, England and Scotland.
You will create a data-led approach to customer intervention, using product usage, adoption, sentiment, service and commercial signals to identify where customers need help before issues become renewal risks. For high-risk or strategically important customers, you will coordinate focused cross-functional intervention and track whether it produces measurable improvement.
Regional Account Directors remain accountable for the overall customer and commercial performance of their Pod. We are looking for a Product Manager to own Clinical Document Workflow and Clinical Document Transfer (formerly Docman GP and Docman Connect) two established products at the heart of how clinical correspondence flows into and between NHS care settings. Clinical Document Workflow is the tool that GP practices use to process, code and file the hundreds of clinical documents they receive each day. Clinical Document Transfer moves that correspondence securely from secondary care into GP systems, reaching the vast majority of practices in England. These are trusted, widely deployed products where reliability and clinical safety are non-negotiable, and there is real scope to modernise them and connect them into the wider neighbourhood health direction.
This is a role for someone who can protect a mission-critical core while moving it forward. Three things make it stand out:
• Trusted at scale. Own products used across most GP practices in England, where reliability and clinical safety come first.
• Documents that move care forward. Shape how clinical correspondence flows securely between care settings and files accurately into the patient record.

• Modernise established technology in step with the wider IQ Health platform.

• Run your own user research with practice staff and clinicians to understand real document workflows.
• Write clear, precise PRDs in an AI enabled SDLC and prioritise using objective data on usage, value and risk.

• Experience with established or mission-critical software at scale, where reliability and safety matter.

• Confidence working directly with clinicians and practice staff.
• Health IT, primary care or wider NHS context is a strong advantage.

• A clear view on where AI can help with document management, such as classification, summarisation, coding and routing of clinical correspondence, and where it introduces risk.

• Fluent using AI tooling to raise your own pace and quality, and able to write requirements precise enough for an AI-assisted build.
