Overview
The SAP Business One System Specialist will help transform Orphalan’s use of SAP Business One into an integrated ERP and operational control system. The role will work across Finance, Supply Chain, Commercial, Legal, Quality and Technology to design, configure, integrate and embed end-to-end business processes in SAP B1.
This is a hands-on specialist role combining SAP B1 functional expertise, systems configuration, process analysis, integration coordination, data governance, reporting and user enablement. The successful candidate will translate business requirements into controlled, supportable solutions and ensure that SAP B1 becomes the reliable system of record for purchasing, inventory, order-to-cash, payments, close and management reporting.
Role Purpose
Own the functional evolution, configuration and continuous improvement of SAP B1 across Orphalan.
Convert approved future-state processes and controls into practical SAP B1 workflows, authorisations, master data, integrations, reports and operating procedures.
Coordinate delivery across business owners, Finance, external SAP partners and integrated-system providers while protecting data quality, auditability and segregation of duties.
Drive adoption so users follow standard ERP processes rather than parallel email, spreadsheet or manual workarounds.
Key Responsibilities
SAP B1 Functional Ownership and Solution Design
Act as Orphalan’s internal SAP B1 functional specialist and primary point of coordination for ERP configuration, enhancement, support and roadmap delivery.
Lead discovery workshops, document requirements, map end-to-end processes and translate business needs into fit-for-purpose SAP B1 designs.
Assess when to use SAP B1 native capabilities, approved add-ons, Microsoft Power Platform or integrated solutions, balancing control, usability, maintainability and cost.
Maintain the system design, configuration documentation, process maps, decision log, change backlog and release plan.
Request-to-Pay and Supplier Management
Implement structured purchase requests, budget checks, contract references, approval workflows and purchase-order creation in SAP B1.
Configure vendor onboarding controls, mandatory fields, duplicate detection and governed vendor master-data changes, including independent verification of bank details.
Enable goods receipt and service-confirmation processes linked to purchase orders and contracts.
Inventory, Batch Management and 3PL Integration
Configure SAP B1 as the financial inventory system of record, including products, warehouses, batches, expiry dates, quarantine, release and ownership status.
Coordinate transaction-level integration with 3PL providers for receipts, releases, transfers, shipments, returns and adjustments.
Implement interface control totals, exception reporting and reconciliation for inventory movements.
Support accurate cut-off and accounting for goods in transit, consignment stock, distributor stock and third-party-held inventory.
Order-to-Cash, Shipment and Revenue Processes
Implement controlled sales-order processing with product, price, quantity, delivery terms, credit status and required shipment date.
Configure approvals for price, discount, credit and exceptional delivery terms.
Integrate approved sales orders with 3PL shipment confirmation, delivery transactions and subsequent invoicing.
Enable traceable document flows from sales order to delivery to invoice, with controls supporting revenue cut-off, credit notes, returns and distributor arrangements.
Payments, Banking and Cash Management
Complete deployment of the SAP B1 Payment Wizard across relevant legal entities and support secure bank-file integration.
Implement payment proposals based on approved, due and unblocked liabilities, with appropriate separation of preparation and approval.
Link payment batches, approvals and bank confirmations back to SAP B1 to maintain a complete audit trail.
Implement daily bank-statement imports, automated matching rules, cash application and aged ownership of unmatched items.
Financial Close, Accounting and Controls
Configure reporting and controlled workflows for accrual candidates arising from POs, receipts, service confirmations, contracts, recurring commitments and unprocessed invoices.
Enable auto-reversing accruals, controlled prepayment schedules, fixed-asset integration, intercompany postings and foreign-exchange revaluation.
Support a single close calendar, standard balance-sheet reconciliations, preparer/reviewer sign-off and evidence retention.
Partner with Finance to support a controlled working-day 5 close and the longer-term move towards a working-day 3–4 core accounting close.
Reporting, Data and Exception Management
Build reliable SAP B1 queries, alerts and operational reports for budget, commitments, inventory, sales, cash, close and exceptions.
Help establish a controlled finance data layer over SAP B1 and integrate it with Power BI once transactional processes and master data are stable.
Ensure management reports reconcile to the SAP B1 general ledger before distribution.
Design exception-led monitoring for unmatched invoices, late receipts, unusual price movements, negative inventory, overdue approvals and unresolved interface items.
Master Data, Security and Governance
Implement governance for customers, vendors, products, accounts, projects, cost centres and other critical master data.
Configure role-based authorisations for requesters, approvers, procurement, warehouse, AP, Finance, administrators and payment users.
Support periodic access recertification, prompt leaver and role-change updates, and controls preventing incompatible combinations of duties.
Ensure system changes, configuration decisions and control exceptions follow formal ERP governance and change control.
Training, Adoption and Operational Support
Create concise procedures, workflow guides, approval rules, release notes and role-based training using real Orphalan scenarios.
Provide second-line functional support, triage incidents, coordinate vendor escalation and identify root causes and preventive improvements.
Monitor adoption, system usage, workflow ageing and exception rates; work with process owners to retire unauthorised spreadsheets and manual workarounds when processes are stable.
Build a network of process owners and super-users to sustain knowledge, adoption and continuous improvement.
Required Profile
Demonstrable hands-on experience implementing, configuring, supporting and improving SAP Business One in a multi-process business environment.
Strong functional knowledge of SAP B1 across purchasing, sales, inventory, financials, banking, approvals, authorisations, master data and reporting.
Experience translating business processes and internal controls into system configuration and practical workflows.
Experience with SAP B1 integration approaches and coordinating interfaces with third-party platforms, 3PLs, banks or invoice-processing systems.
Working knowledge of SQL-based queries and reporting for SAP B1; ability to diagnose data and transaction issues logically.
Understanding of finance and accounting processes, including AP, AR, general ledger, accruals, prepayments, fixed assets, intercompany, FX, bank reconciliation and period close.
Good understanding of role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails, change control and master-data governance.
Strong stakeholder engagement, workshop facilitation, documentation and training skills.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and coordinate effectively with external implementation partners.
Desirable Experience
Experience in pharmaceutical, life-sciences, healthcare or another regulated environment.
Experience with batch-managed and expiry-controlled inventory, third-party logistics and multi-entity operations.
Exposure to SAP Concur, Power BI, Microsoft Power Platform
Knowledge of SAP B1 Service Layer, integration framework, APIs or common SAP B1 add-ons.
Relevant SAP Business One certification or equivalent evidence of implementation expertise.
Experience supporting ERP transformation`, process standardisation and business adoption beyond Finance.

Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence
PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.
Chemistry and materials underpin many of PhysicsX’s highest-priority sectors, spanning semiconductors, electrochemistry, specialty and commodity chemicals, mining, and oil & gas. We work from atoms to systems, transforming how chemists, materials scientists, and engineers exploit new materials, design new processes and devices, monitor performance, and optimise the operation of existing assets. This includes identifying the key chemical phenomena and mechanisms that must be captured, and the scale at which to simulate them, to drive discovery, scale-up, and optimisation. We apply a diverse range of approaches, from DFT to AI-driven inverse problem solving, and simulate at every scale between atomistic and continuum.
Many AI companies are working on materials discovery. Most stop at a predicted property or a ranked list of candidates. We go further. We carry chemistry from the atom to the device, cell, reactor, and plant, so our customers can see whether a new material or process delivers the performance they need, at industrial scale, and within real manufacturing constraints.
This role is available in the UK or US. 
This Role
You’ll build this distinctive atoms-to-systems capability, coupling atomistic and molecular insight into the continuum and systems-scale models across PhysicsX, so our customers can industrialise novel materials and processes faster. This is a mandate to define and deliver a new era for chemists, materials scientists, process engineers, and operators.
To do this, you’ll own chemistry capabilities at PhysicsX, from the team to the technology. You’ll set the technical direction and standards for chemistry across the company, and lead the chemistry team across two streams:
• Capability: Direct the team building our chemistry capabilities. Work with Product to productise functionality, and with Research to keep pushing the frontier across chemistry and AI. Partner with our industry leads so the roadmap delivers the greatest value to our customers.
• Customers: Work with our Delivery leads to ensure the right people are on the right customer projects and well supported, and that we keep growing the team with the right skill sets. You are the hiring manager for the team across both streams.
You’ll be the foremost chemistry voice in conversations with prospective customers. You’ll work with industry leads and customers, read the signal from those interactions, and decide which technical directions to pursue, how best to support our customers’ chemistry needs, and which capabilities to use or develop.
You’ll also:
• Decide which machine learning approaches for chemistry we build, which we adopt, and how they couple into our continuum and systems-scale models
• Own the balance between capability development and time with our customers
• Stay hands-on enough to go deep with the team on hard technical problems
Your performance will be judged in equal parts by the success you drive with our customers and the uptake of new, distinctive capabilities.
This Role
You have a PhD in computational chemistry or computational materials science. Alternatively, your PhD is in a related field such as chemical engineering, materials science, electrochemistry, or applied physics, with substantial research in atomistic or multiscale modeling. You have 6+ years of deep technical work since your PhD, in industry or an industry-facing setting.
You have hands-on depth in atomistic simulation and machine learning interatomic potentials. You also have working knowledge of techniques at other scales, including molecular, mesoscale, phase-field, reactive flow, and process simulation. Just as importantly, you know how to connect them: which quantities must carry from one scale to the next, and where a surrogate can replace a simulation. You’ve applied this to real industrial problems and have direct experience in relevant industries. Semiconductors, electrochemistry, or catalysis would be ideal.

You’ll be the person on the ground for a portfolio of accounts, and the voice that brings what you learn back into our product.

General Summary:
Qualcomm is seeking a Staff-level Systems Analyst to join the EMEA IT organisation in a business-facing, technically grounded role focused on enterprise systems, process optimisation and AI enablement. The role will help business teams maximise the value of Qualcomm enterprise applications by understanding how work is done today, identifying opportunities for improvement, and translating business needs into clear requirements and recommendations for global IT delivery teams.
This is not a traditional application support role. It is a consultative technical role that combines enterprise systems analysis, business process understanding, AI opportunity identification and stakeholder influence across EMEA.
### ### Background:
* Qualcomm business teams rely on enterprise systems to execute critical processes across functions such as finance, sales, operations, HR, supply chain, engineering support and corporate services.
* As AI capabilities become embedded into enterprise applications and business workflows, IT needs strong regional business partners who can identify practical, value-driven use cases.
* EMEA requires a role that can understand regional business realities, ensure enterprise platforms are being used effectively, and represent business needs clearly to global application and delivery teams.
* The successful candidate will help bridge business intent, system capability, process adoption and technical execution.
Minimum Qualifications:
• 5+ years of IT-relevant work experience with a Bachelor's degree. OR 7+ years of IT-relevant work experience without a Bachelor’s degree. *Completed advanced degrees in a relevant field may be substituted for up to two years (Master’s = one year, Doctorate = two years) of work experience.
### Key Responsibilities
Enterprise systems analysis and optimisation
* Analyse complex business problems and identify how automated systems, enterprise applications and AI-enabled capabilities can help solve them.
* Assess existing business processes and system usage to identify opportunities for simplification, standardisation, automation and improved adoption.
* Provide technical expertise in evaluating, defining and improving systems and procedures that are cost effective and meet user requirements.
* Create and review functional and system specifications that translate business needs into actionable requirements for application owners and delivery teams.
* Support configuration analysis, user acceptance planning and validation of delivered changes where appropriate.
AI enablement and business process innovation
* Identify opportunities to apply AI, generative AI, intelligent agents, workflow automation and enterprise data capabilities to improve business efficiency and decision-making.
* Partner with business stakeholders to define practical AI use cases, expected outcomes, adoption considerations and measurable value.
* Promote responsible and effective use of Qualcomm-approved AI capabilities within enterprise business processes.
* Help business teams understand where AI can augment existing enterprise applications and where AI-specific solutions may deliver new efficiency or insight.
* Represent business problems and AI opportunities to technical teams in a clear, structured and prioritised way.
Business engagement and regional partnership
* Build trusted relationships with EMEA business leaders, functional teams and key users to understand priorities, pain points and operating models.
* Act as a regional IT advisor for enterprise business systems and AI-enabled process improvement opportunities.
* Facilitate workshops, discovery sessions and process reviews with business and technical stakeholders.
* Ensure EMEA business requirements are represented effectively to global IT delivery teams.
* Support change adoption by helping business teams understand, use and realise value from enterprise systems and new capabilities.
Cross-functional execution and influence
* Lead collaboration with systems analysts, application owners, business partners and subject matter experts to document recommendations and drive improvements.
* Participate in project review sessions to communicate status, discuss complex issues and support prioritisation decisions.
* May lead cross-functional linked teams to address business or systems issues.
* Help manage priorities, deadlines and deliverables for assigned initiatives, ensuring work is aligned to business outcomes.
* Use strong communication, influence, cooperation and diplomacy to resolve challenges across teams and geographies.
### ### Required qualifications
* IT-relevant work experience with a Bachelor's degree.
* Experience analysing complex business problems and defining system-based solutions.
* Strong understanding of enterprise applications, business processes and automated systems.
* Ability to create functional and system specifications that meet business user requirements.
* Experience working with business stakeholders, technical teams and subject matter experts.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex topics to audiences with varying levels of technical knowledge.
* Ability to work independently with little supervision and exercise sound judgement on moderately complex or high-impact decisions.
### ### Preferred qualifications and experience
* 2+ years of experience leading informal teams or cross-functional initiatives.
* Experience with enterprise platforms such as Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, Databricks, enterprise data platforms or similar business systems.
* Experience in business process improvement, digital transformation, application adoption or value realisation.
* Experience identifying automation, AI or analytics opportunities within business processes.
* Understanding of generative AI, enterprise copilots, intelligent agents, workflow automation or AI-enabled productivity tools.
* Experience operating in a global organisation and collaborating with distributed delivery teams across multiple regions.
* Experience presenting recommendations, business cases or solution options to senior stakeholders.
### ### Candidate Profile
* A technically credible systems analyst who is comfortable working directly with business teams.
* Curious about how business processes work and how technology can improve them.
* Able to move between strategic discussion, detailed process analysis and practical delivery follow-up.
* Comfortable influencing without formal authority across functions, regions and technical teams.
* Passionate about AI, but pragmatic about where AI adds real business value.
* Clear, structured and outcome-focused in communication and documentation.

Qube Research & Technologies (QRT) is a technology and data-driven quantitative investment manager. We build systems that directly support research, trading and engineering activity.
As our cloud estate scales, observability can no longer be treated as a set of dashboards or one-off integrations. We need standard patterns for telemetry collection, storage, alerting, service ownership, onboarding and team adoption across a large, multi-account AWS estate.
We already operate an established observability capability supporting our on-premises platforms. This role exists to help build the equivalent capability across our cloud estate. We are looking for engineers who have successfully built similar capabilities before and can apply those lessons here.
We are looking for hands-on Cloud Observability Platform Engineers to help build the foundations for cloud observability across AWS and EKS/Kubernetes.
This is a Platform Engineering role, not a dashboard-building role.
What You'll Do
- Help design and build the standard cloud observability patterns for AWS and EKS.
- Build telemetry collection and distribution at scale across a large, multi-account AWS estate.
- Translate AWS telemetry into patterns that integrate cleanly with our existing metrics, logs and alerting platforms.
- Deploy observability components, including patterns that avoid circular dependencies where the observability platform relies on itself to remain observable.
- Integrate cloud telemetry with inventory and service ownership data, so alerts and dashboards map back to real services and accountable owners.
- Build or integrate logs, metrics and alerting platforms, including storage, routing, retention and PagerDuty integration.
- Support retrospective deployment of observability standards across an existing cloud estate.
- Build repeatable onboarding patterns so new cloud workloads adopt observability consistently from day one.
- Build user configuration automation for alert rules, scrape targets, dashboards and standard team-consumable patterns.
- Reduce operational toil through automation, standardisation and clear platform patterns.
- Work closely with Observability, Cloud, Platform Engineering and service-owning teams to make the platform practical to adopt.
Success depends on making cloud observability easier to adopt than bespoke alternatives while continuously improving the platform as the cloud estate evolves.
Engineers Who Thrive In This Role
- You have previously built or significantly expanded cloud observability capabilities in production environments.
- You automate repetitive work rather than documenting manual processes.
- You ask questions before proposing solutions.
- You recognise when you do not yet understand the problem.
- You deliberately discover how systems actually work before committing to a design.
- You adapt your approach as new information becomes available.
- You like solving root causes rather than symptoms.
- You are comfortable working across infrastructure, cloud, Kubernetes, telemetry, automation and people.
- You are pragmatic about balancing engineering quality, usability and delivery.
- You can make progress without waiting for perfect requirements.
- You understand that platform adoption matters as much as technical design.
- You are comfortable owning outcomes, not just completing tickets.
Technologies And Areas We Expect You To Work Across
Our current environment includes technologies such as AWS, EKS/Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry, CloudWatch, Prometheus-compatible metrics, VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, Alertmanager, Grafana, PagerDuty, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, automation, service catalogues, inventory data, Terraform, Python and Go.
Experience with VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, Alertmanager, Terraform, Python, Go or similar tooling would be useful, but strong engineers usually learn missing tools quickly.

An awareness of changes in trends, policies and regulations applicable to fraud prevention and recoveries
An understanding of the industry and our customers, including products, processes and fraud prevention systems
Experience of managing stakeholder relationships

Client delivery

Look for opportunities to reflect these in your work and flag your ideas to your teams and wider team to raise your internal profile

job_title: Senior Data Product Manager - EPH Digital Products
job_description:
Are you passionate about turning complex data challenges into clear, scalable product solutions?
Do you enjoy leading through ambiguity, shaping roadmaps, and helping teams deliver high-quality outcomes in an evolving AI-enabled environment?
About our Team
DBS Product Management is a newly established team focused on products and data products. Our vision is a future where every colleague has trustworthy data they confidently use to streamline processes, drive smarter decisions and accelerate growth. We identify the products and data products that matter most to Elsevier and shape what they look like.
The Enterprise Product Hub (EPH) is central to that vision. It masters Elsevier’s saleable product data in a single governed model and publishes it to around thirty systems across the business. With books and journals established, the priority now is bringing digital products to the same standard as Elsevier transforms how it sells and invoices its products.
About the Role
The Senior Data Product Manager owns an evolving area of the EPH product estate – the attributes that enable us to sell a product, from what it’s called to how it’s identified and how it’s sold. You will report to the Head of Product Data.
This role complements the existing product management by taking responsibility for a current gap in our data estate: the ingestion and publication of digital product data. Fraud Risk Manager
Why this role matters
The Fraud Risk Manager protects Argos and Nectar by leading the proactive
identification, assessment and investigation of suspected and confirmed fraud.
The role helps safeguard financial performance, customers, colleagues, brand
reputation and legal and regulatory compliance by ensuring fraud risks are
understood and addressed effectively.
Reporting to the Head of Central Operations, the role provides Argos-wide fraud
oversight and works across Argos Retail, Digital, Technology, Contact Centres,
Logistics, Finance, People, Legal, Loss Prevention and Nectar. It leads complex
and sensitive investigations, turns intelligence into action and makes clear
recommendations that strengthen controls, reduce loss and prevent fraud from
recurring.
What I am accountable for
Lead the delivery of the Argos fraud risk plan, setting clear priorities and
translating emerging threats, intelligence and business change into
proportionate action.
Own the proactive identification, assessment and investigation of suspected and
confirmed fraud affecting Argos and Nectar, ensuring cases are handled
objectively, confidentially, lawfully and at appropriate pace.
Lead complex end-to-end investigations, securing and assessing evidence,
establishing the scale and cause of loss and making fact-based recommendations
on criminal, civil, disciplinary or control actions.
Use data and intelligence to identify fraud trends, control weaknesses and
vulnerabilities across stores, digital channels, contact centres, logistics,
payments, customer journeys and Nectar activity.
Provide clear fraud risk advice to senior leaders and cross-functional teams,
influencing commercial, customer, operational and technology decisions to reduce
exposure while protecting the Argos and Nectar experience.
Set and maintain effective Argos fraud governance, investigation standards,
policies, procedures and reporting, ensuring decisions and information-sharing
comply with relevant law and data protection requirements.
Lead, coach and develop Investigation Managers and Specialists, setting clear
accountabilities and performance expectations and building strong investigation,
analytical and fraud-risk capability.
Build productive relationships with Nectar teams, law enforcement, external
agencies, industry partners and third-party suppliers to improve intelligence,
investigation outcomes, asset recovery and fraud prevention.
Oversee relevant supplier performance and expenditure within delegated
authority, ensuring activity is risk-based, cost-effective and delivers
measurable value.
Turn investigation findings and root-cause analysis into practical
recommendations, tracking agreed actions and sharing learning to strengthen
controls and prevent repeat loss across Argos and Nectar.
 
What I need to know
These are key skills, experience and qualifications required to succeed in this
role:
Strong knowledge of fraud risk management and complex investigations, including
evidence gathering, interviewing, case management and root-cause analysis in a
commercial environment.
Sound knowledge of relevant criminal and civil law, the criminal justice system,
rules of evidence, data protection and lawful information-sharing.
Strong analytical, numerical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to
interrogate data, assess intelligence and communicate a clear risk narrative.
Experience of identifying weaknesses in systems, processes and controls and
translating findings into proportionate, commercially practical improvements.
Strong leadership and people-management skills, with the ability to set
direction, build capability and maintain high standards across sensitive
investigations.
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the judgement and
credibility to advise senior stakeholders and work effectively with law
enforcement, external agencies and suppliers.
Ability to make balanced decisions in complex or ambiguous situations,
prioritising activity according to risk, customer and colleague impact,
potential loss and likely value.
Knowledge of retail, digital, payments, loyalty or customer-service fraud risks
is valuable, but the ability to transfer relevant fraud and investigation
expertise into the Argos and Nectar environment is equally important.
Strong planning and prioritisation skills, with the flexibility to support
serious cases and travel to Argos locations when required.

* Significant experience leading complex end-to-end fraud investigations,
including evidence gathering, interviewing, case management and root-cause
analysis.
* Proven experience developing and delivering fraud risk plans or strategies,
using intelligence and emerging threats to set priorities and reduce fraud
exposure.
* Strong analytical experience using data and intelligence to identify fraud
trends, vulnerabilities and control weaknesses and translate these into
practical recommendations.
* Demonstrable experience identifying weaknesses in systems, processes or
controls and implementing improvements to prevent or reduce repeat fraud and
financial loss.
* Proven leadership and people-management experience, including setting
direction, managing investigation teams and developing fraud and
investigative capability.

external parties, such as law enforcement, external agencies, suppliers or
industry partners, on complex or sensitive fraud matters.

Who we are Digital Energy Software is a core business of Schneider Electric’s Energy Management business. We build operations software, software-defined control, IoT and analytics that help customers run, optimize and control buildings, power and energy, from small and medium buildings to large and mission-critical sites. EcoStruxure™ Foresight DataConnect is where our software meets every other system in a building. It brings operational data together, shares it, gives it a common meaning and normalizes it, so analytics, applications and AI-native energy intelligence can act on it, in the cloud, at the edge and in hybrid deployments that span both. Why this role matters Buildings are among the largest controllable costs an organization carries, yet most still run on systems that do not talk to each other. Building management, power monitoring, workplace and maintenance systems each hold part of the picture, and the value sits in the gaps between them. AI raises the stakes. An AI that informs is only as good as the data it can see, and an AI that acts needs trusted, governed paths into the systems it acts on. Integration is where that changes. Every third-party system, device and application that exchanges data with our software does so through DataConnect connectors, interfaces and APIs. They link operational technology (OT) on site, such as building automation, power and IoT systems, with IT systems and cloud services, and they carry data and events reliably in both directions. As Offer Leader for Software Integrations you own that entry point end to end, as its product manager and as its offer leader. You set the roadmap and own the backlog that R&D builds from. The manager translates regional priorities into clear operating standards, performance expectations and improvement plans. They create an inclusive, accountable environment in which teams with varied experience can develop, collaborate and deliver operational excellence.

Operational Leadership
Lead day-to-day SOC operations across EMEA, ensuring timely delivery of operational tasks, projects and regional priorities.
Establish and maintain consistent regional operating standards, service-delivery plans and governance routines.
Ensure SOC personnel have the tools, equipment, information, training and site documentation required to perform effectively.
Maintain a thorough understanding of each SOC’s role, operating model and contribution to effective monitoring, escalation and reporting.
Act as the regional operational lead and delegated escalation point in the SOC Director’s absence, within agreed authority levels.
People Leadership and Capability
Lead, coach and develop EMEA SOC managers and supervisors, enabling them to build capable, accountable and high-performing teams.
Set clear performance and conduct expectations, hold regular one-to-one meetings, provide timely feedback and recognise achievement.
Maintain appropriate performance and development records and implement improvement plans where required.
Partner with local Securitas branches to recruit, onboard, train and retain suitably qualified SOC personnel.
Promote formal, informal and peer-to-peer recognition and foster an inclusive environment that values different perspectives.

Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, contractual, client and Securitas requirements across all EMEA SOCs.
Maintain audit readiness, conduct regular assurance reviews and oversee timely closure of corrective actions.
Ensure incidents are assessed, responded to, escalated and reported in accordance with agreed standards.
Identify operational and workplace risks, prioritise safety and support effective business continuity and resilience arrangements.
Maintain professional composure when engaging authorities, executives, colleagues or members of the public during urgent or high-pressure situations.
Client and Stakeholder Management
Build trusted relationships with client leadership, local Securitas branches, the global SOC service team and other partners.
Align stakeholders on operational priorities, risks, decisions, service performance and corrective actions.
Hold regular service and staffing reviews with supporting branches to maintain agreed coverage and meet operational service-level agreements.
Represent the values, culture and professional standards of Securitas and the client in every interaction.
Performance, Reporting and Continuous Improvement

Deliver accurate, timely operational data, insights and recommendations for monthly and quarterly business reviews.
Support informed decision-making through reliable reporting, clear escalation and evidence-based recommendations.
Lead continuous improvement in processes, technology, service delivery and new-site mobilisation.
Take accountability for regional outcomes and adapt priorities and resources to meet changing operational needs.

Work flexibly across EMEA and global time zones to support operational priorities and stakeholder collaboration.
Provide occasional out-of-hours support for critical incidents, urgent escalations and essential global meetings.
Travel regularly within EMEA and internationally for site visits, new-site launches, audits and other operational requirements.

Achievement of agreed KPIs, SLAs and service-quality standards.
Strong audit and compliance performance, with timely closure of corrective actions.
Consistent incident-response quality, escalation discipline and reporting timeliness.
Stable staffing, effective onboarding and high completion of required training.
Improved consistency, resilience and continuous improvement across EMEA SOC operations.
Positive client and stakeholder feedback.

Willingness to complete required pre-employment screening, subject to applicable local law and company policy.

• Make decisions with incomplete information and adapt quickly.

About Snowplow
Snowplow is the real-time customer context layer that collects, validates, enriches, and delivers behavioral data for advanced analytics, ML, and AI agent decisioning. Snowplow's event tracking is leveraged across 2M+ websites and applications globally, processing over one trillion events per month.
More than 250 companies, including Experian, AutoTrader, Strava, Condé Nast, and HelloFresh, rely on Snowplow to build a well-governed, first-party data foundation that powers their customer-facing AI agents, in-session personalization and recommendations, and real-time analytics.
This Opportunity
Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work. AI-native transformation is the operating priority for the business, and the Applied AI team owns it: the platform every team's AI work runs on, the pattern for how a function's critical workflows move onto agents, and the measurement of whether it worked. Individual AI adoption is already high across the company. The next stage is redesigning functions so that agents run the recurring work and people set the goals and judge the output.
You are the first Forward Deployed Engineer on the team, reporting to the Senior Director of Applied AI. The team is also hiring a principal engineer to own the platform and an Applied AI engineer to embed with our Growth team. The Senior Director you report to still ships code. You are the one who moves between functions. You embed with one function at a time alongside its leader and the people who do the work by hand today, map how the work actually runs, build the agentic workflow that takes it on, tune it with the experts until they trust it, and hand it back to the function to own. Then you move to the next one.
You sit with our major business functions, one at a time. The Senior Director of Applied AI and the function's leader choose each engagement, and your workflow maps are the evidence they choose from. Priorities will shift as the transformation moves, and the role is designed for that.
This is the forward deployed model applied inside our own company. You write the code, and you also do the discovery a consultant would. The function's leader owns the decision to change how their team works. You own the engineering and the pattern. You'll spend as much time listening to someone walk through a task they do by hand every week as you will writing the agents that run it, and the deliverable is a function that works differently, understands why, and can run what you built.
What you will own
- The workflow map. You sit with the people who do the work and leave with how it actually runs today: where work enters, what moves between steps, who says yes, and what "good" means. It is the first thing you do in every engagement.
- The case for whether to build. Before anything gets built, you bring the evidence from the map and make the case for whether the workflow is worth moving onto agents, including when the answer is that it does not need AI. The decision sits with the function's leader and the Senior Director; the evidence is yours.
- The build. You design and build agentic workflows on Snowplow's shared factory framework, which Applied AI runs: declared queues and gates, focused agents, and a central ledger that records every agent run. Every factory you build is compatible with every other one, in any function.
- Approval gates. You decide where the agent acts on its own, where it proposes and a person approves, and what gets recorded so anyone can see what the agent did and why. The people in the function keep the judgment. The agents take the rest.
- Agent readiness. You make the function's knowledge, systems of record, and quality bar explicit enough for agents to work from. Often this is the real work, and the agents are the easy part.
- The last twenty percent. Most of the work comes after the prototype: reliability, edge cases, evaluation, and a team choosing it over the way they worked before. You tune the output alongside the domain experts and encode their judgment into checks that hold after they step back.
- The handoff. You train the function to run and evolve what you built, then leave. Where an Applied AI engineer is embedded in the function, you hand it to them. Success is a workflow still running months after you have moved on, owned by people who are not you. After the handoff you stay available: when the function sees a problem or a way to improve the workflow, you coordinate it with the embedded and platform engineers rather than taking it back, and you help build the platform those workflows run on.
- The pattern itself. You own how a workflow moves from map to agents to handoff, written down so the next engagement starts from it. What you build also goes back into the shared framework as reference implementations. The second factory in any function should be cheaper than the first.
We would love to hear from you if you have
- Shipped real software in someone else's stack. You are comfortable being dropped into an unfamiliar codebase, dataset, or business system and productive in it fast. You are fluent in at least one of Python, TypeScript, or Go, and you pick up the others as the work needs them.
- Built with LLMs in production. You have designed agents or agentic workflows that run real work, with prompts, tools, evaluation, and the failure modes that come with them. You know the difference between a demo and something a team relies on every day, and you have done the unglamorous work of closing that gap.
- An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, automation, or agent you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.
- Sat with non-engineers and understood their work. You can spend a day with a sales, marketing, or customer team and come back with the actual process, including the parts nobody wrote down. Active listening matters here as much as the stack.
- Self-direction and comfort with ambiguity. Engagements are time-boxed, functions differ, and the next one is decided by the business. You plan your own work inside an engagement and stay steady when the business changes what comes next.

job_description:
About Snowplow
Snowplow is the real-time customer context layer that collects, validates, enriches, and delivers behavioral data for advanced analytics, ML, and AI agent decisioning. Snowplow's event tracking is leveraged across 2M+ websites and applications globally, processing over one trillion events per month.
More than 250 companies, including Experian, AutoTrader, Strava, Condé Nast, and HelloFresh, rely on Snowplow to build a well-governed, first-party data foundation that powers their customer-facing AI agents, in-session personalization and recommendations, and real-time analytics.
This Opportunity
Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work, and the Applied AI team owns Firn, the single data and AI platform the whole company runs on. Firn already gives people and agents the same governed tools over our Snowflake warehouse through an MCP gateway, routes every model call through one LLM gateway with tracing, runs agentic workflows on a factory framework with a ledger that records every run, and holds the skills catalog the company draws on. Most of the company uses it every day. The platform is at its beginning, and the next stage is to expand it until it holds the company's commercial intelligence and lets agents act on it safely.
You are the principal engineer who leads that expansion. The first engagement is Go-to-Market, full time for about six months. Our buyers research with AI agents now, and reaching them means using our own data and AI to decide which accounts and people to engage, with what, and learning from every experiment. The GTM teams have built a lot: daily account and engagement scoring, signal feeds from Apollo, Vector and reo.dev, an always-on outbound engine, a paid-media loop, a curated GTM knowledge base, and the integrations between them. Much of it was built by operational teams to get results fast, and it did. You design how those services come onto Firn, unify and modernize them, build the agents and tools and learning loops on top, and make the whole thing production grade.
This is a principal role. You report to the Senior Director of Applied AI, who still ships code, and work as a peer. Marketing, Sales, Account Management and Partnerships are the platform's customers and set their own priorities. You decide how it gets built and whether it is sound. Once the GTM services run without you, they stay yours as their owner and most of your time goes to what Snowplow needs next.
What you will own
- The GTM intelligence engine on Firn. The data and AI that decide who we engage and with what, and that learn from the outcome of every action. You design it with our data engineers as a set of platform services with several internal customers, and you bring the GTM services that exist today onto the same foundation.
- Agents and tools. The agents that run GTM work and the tools people and other agents call, built on the factory framework with review steps and evaluations as the standard shape, so every agent on the platform can be trusted and inspected the same way.
- Platform architecture. The MCP gateway, LLM gateway, tracing, factory framework and ledger, and how they grow to hold more of the company's work. You decide what is built, what is bought, and what is retired.
- Production grade. Version control, CI, alerting and recovery, cost visibility, documentation, and handover for every service on the platform, including the ones that arrive from operational teams. You set the bar and you make it visible to the teams that depend on it.
- Logic as code. Rules that today live inside individual tools move into versioned code on the platform, where agents can read them and engineers can test them, and the tools become endpoints the platform drives.
- Learning loops. Every action the platform takes is recorded and tied to its outcome, so people and agents can see what worked and the next action is better. Metric definitions sit with our data engineers; the instrumentation that applies them is yours.
- Eval and tracing infrastructure. The harness the embedded and forward deployed engineers use to prove their agents work. You own the tooling; they own the checks.
- The technical bar and the roadmap. You set the engineering bar for the Applied AI team and own the platform roadmap, and you keep the long view of the platform at all times.
We would love to hear from you if you have
- Years of production software behind you. You have designed, shipped and run systems other teams depend on, in Python or TypeScript, with SQL, CI/CD and cloud infrastructure as everyday tools. This is a principal role and the bar is set there.
- Built LLM systems that real work runs on. Agents with tools, MCP servers, gateways, tracing and evaluation, and the failure modes that come with them. You can say what broke in production and what you changed.
- Platform instincts. You have built systems other people depend on, whether internal teams or customers, through interfaces you designed, and you know the difference between a platform and a pile of integrations.
- Data platform fluency. Snowflake or an equivalent warehouse, dbt, data contracts, and the pipelines that move warehouse data into SaaS tools and back.
- Operational discipline. Alerting, recovery, runbooks and cost tracking are things you add before anyone asks, and you have run systems where that discipline mattered.
- Judgment about where an agent belongs. You can tell which decisions should be deterministic code, which an agent can make, and which should stay with a person, and you can explain the reasoning to a non-engineer.
- An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, agent or tool you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.
- Comfort with internal customers who are not engineers. You can sit with a growth director, a seller or a marketer, take a requirement, and hold the line on how it gets built. No sales or marketing background is needed.
- Technical direction without a title. You have set direction for a platform that other engineers followed because the design was right, not because they reported to you.
How we hire for this role
The interview process includes a working session where you walk us through how you work with AI on a real task, using your own setup, and a design conversation on a system we run today. We work this way ourselves, and you are welcome to use AI when applying.
What you get in return for being awesome

- Enhanced Family leave

Sony Music is looking for a Senior Product Manager, Data to join our talented product team in our London office and lead the development of a portfolio of shared data products.
Our products and teams work with data spanning streaming, fan engagement, social and creator activity, and commerce. As new datasets and requirements emerge, we need to understand what the data contains, establish what it means and make it useful beyond the team or product where it originated.

Working with business stakeholders, source-product owners and data engineering, you will turn business needs into clear requirements, deliver dependable datasets and establish definitions and relationships that can be reused across products.

Understand needs across teams, identify valuable opportunities and prioritise a portfolio of initiatives that supports artist teams and the wider business.

- Lead delivery and adoption. Maintain a prioritised backlog and work with engineering through implementation, validation, launch and ongoing improvement. Ensure the teams receiving the data can use it to meet the agreed need.

Develop the shared semantic layer through the initiatives you deliver, so concepts such as artists, tracks, markets, campaigns and audiences can be understood consistently across products.

job_title: Engineering Manager, Homeowner and Partner Experiences
job_description:
About the Job
As the Engineering Manager for Homeowner and Partner Experiences at Splitero, you will lead the team responsible for the systems our homeowners and partners interact with, from marketing through origination, in a fintech and proptech ecosystem. You will report to our Director of Engineering and manage a team of full-stack engineers, including a technical lead who partners with you on day-to-day technical decisions. You will work closely with product, QA, our Salesforce team, and our offshore engineering team.
In this role, you'll split your time roughly 70/30 between hands-on engineering and people management. Your hands-on focus leans toward the foundation: cloud infrastructure, AWS CDK, security, and observability, making sure our systems are scalable, maintainable, and ready for where the business is going, not just where it is today. We're actively shaping what AI-first engineering looks like for this team, and this role will have a direct hand in defining it. You'll help us find the right balance between what LLMs do well and the quality, review, and maintainability standards a regulated fintech business requires. We care about what ships, and we care nearly as much about the systems that produce it.
• Own the architecture and evolution of our AWS infrastructure using AWS CDK, making sure our systems scale well beyond today's business needs.
• Drive security, observability, and reliability across our systems, including logging, monitoring, alerting, and incident response practices.
• Optimize AWS services for performance, cost, and scalability, including serverless applications built on AWS Lambda.
• Help define and roll out AI-first engineering practices for the team: the tooling, context, conventions, guardrails, and review processes that let engineers build with AI tools reliably and at scale.
• Build internal tools and workflows that reduce manual engineering effort and help the team get consistent, high-quality output from AI-assisted development.
• Contribute to product development across our homeowner and partner experiences using Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, and a modern React ecosystem (Next.js, Tailwind, Vercel).
• Partner with your technical lead to guide technical decisions, making sure tradeoffs are well understood and documented across product and engineering.
• Improve engineering lifecycle standards across the team, including code review, testing, deployment, documentation, and knowledge sharing.
• Manage and develop a team of full-stack engineers through regular 1:1s, feedback, goal setting, and performance management.
• Partner with product leads to plan work, set priorities, and deliver on a consistent and predictable pace.
• Partner with the Salesforce team on the data sync between Salesforce and our consumer applications to support GTM initiatives.
• Coordinate with our offshore engineering team and its technical lead to keep handoffs clean and work aligned with our standards.
• Partner with Engineering Leadership and People Operations to hire, onboard, and grow the engineering team.
The salary range for this position is $160,000 - $180,000. Within the range, individual pay is determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
About You
• 8+ years of experience as a full-stack or platform engineer with a strong focus on back-end and cloud infrastructure
• 3+ years managing engineers directly while remaining hands-on
• Deep experience with AWS, including production infrastructure built and maintained with AWS CDK
• Strong background in cloud security, observability, and building systems that scale and stay maintainable over time
• Strong proficiency in TypeScript and Node.js, with experience in PostgreSQL and database design
• Working experience with a modern React ecosystem (Next.js, Tailwind, Vercel)
• Demonstrated experience leading AI-first engineering practices on a team, not just using AI tools individually. You know where LLMs speed up the work, where they need guardrails, and how to keep quality high as output increases.
• Experience building internal tooling, automation, or developer workflows that help teams work more effectively with AI
• Strong technical judgment, with the ability to zoom in or out on projects and make decisions to keep work moving
• A track record of giving direct feedback and supporting engineers in their growth and performance
• Clear communication with product, QA, and non-technical stakeholders
• Experience working with offshore or distributed teams across time zones is a plus
• Experience with Salesforce platforms or integrations is a plus
• Candidates must be located in the United States. Working timezone in PST or MST preferred.
• Desire to participate in fast-paced early-stage startup
• Adaptability: Embraces changing circumstances with resiliency and positivity
• Team-Oriented: Prioritizes collaboration, inclusivity, and teammate support
About Us
Millions of homeowners in today’s economy are sitting on substantial home equity they are unable to access due to rising interest rates and strict qualification requirements of traditional lenders. That means millions of homeowners can’t convert their hard-earned equity into cash to pay off debt, start a home renovation, or pad their retirement to better their lives.
Splitero co-founders Michael Gifford and David Zvaifler witnessed the problem firsthand throughout their real estate careers. They set out to create a win-win product that could help those homeowners access their home equity but not make monthly payments like traditional financing options. And thus, Splitero was born.
As part of our team, you will join our quest to revolutionize the real estate industry while helping families in need. We offer a suite of benefits designed to help you thrive in all areas of life.
• OneTeam Culture - We foster a culture of transparency, innovation, and inclusivity, where every voice is heard and every team member is valued. We believe in celebrating our successes, doing the right thing, and helping each other so we grow as a team and as individuals.
• Generous Resources - We want to ensure you are set up to do your best work. In addition to a solid tech stack, and access to any WeWork location, you will receive a monthly cell and internet stipend.
• Premium Healthcare - We offer comprehensive healthcare plans for you and your family, which employees are eligible for on their first day.
• Flexible PTO and Parental Leave - We offer a generous PTO and encourage employees to take time off to recharge. We're proud to offer a parental leave policy that allows you to welcome your new addition without worry.
We are a workforce composed of individuals with diverse backgrounds, abilities, minds, and identities. In keeping with our commitment to inclusion, we will ensure that people with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodations are required when applying, interviewing, or performing the essential functions of this position, please contact People Operations, at peopleops@splitero.com.

About the Job
As a Full-Stack Engineer at Splitero, you will play a crucial role in architecting, developing, and maintaining our software from marketing through origination. Your expertise in modern back-end technologies, cloud computing, and the full software development lifecycle will be essential in delivering high-quality solutions in a fintech and proptech ecosystem. You will work closely with product, engineering, and QA teams to ensure our software meets the highest standards of functionality and performance while we scale our operations to meet team and organization goals. As an individual contributor, you will be able to balance pace with perfection and understand tradeoffs in how you deliver your work.
• Design and implement scalable and efficient back-end systems using Node, JavaScript, and TypeScript. Develop APIs and services that support robust application functionality.
• Utilize PostgreSQL to design and manage databases, ensuring data integrity and optimizing performance across a Heroku Connect/Salesforce-based data infrastructure.
• Develop and deploy serverless applications using AWS Lambda and IaC platforms such as Terraform and AWS CDK.
• Work with AI technologies for both your day-to-day role as an engineer and also for new product implementations, leveraging APIs with major AI platforms
• Collaborate with front-end developers to integrate back-end services with a modern React ecosystem (Next.js, Tailwind, Vercel, etc), ensuring a seamless and responsive user experience.
• Participate in all stages of the software development lifecycle, from requirements gathering and design to implementation, testing, and deployment.
• Work closely with product managers and QA teams to gather requirements, identify issues, and deliver high-quality software solutions.
• Maintain a high level of attention to detail, ensuring that software is reliable, efficient, and meets established standards and specifications.
• Stay current with industry trends and technologies, recommending improvements and adopting best practices for software development and cloud computing.
The salary range for this position is $140,000 - $155,000. Within the range, individual pay is determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
 
About You
• 4-6 years of experience as a full-stack engineer with a strong focus on back-end technologies
• Strong proficiency in JavaScript and TypeScript for front-end and back-end development
• Strong experience with Node.js for building server-side applications
• Expertise in PostgreSQL (or similar) and database design
• Experience with cloud computing platforms, specifically AWS Lambda
• Extensive experience working with Claude Code (or similar) to build tools and workflows that accelerate the development lifecycle; not just individual chat use or vibe coding

Hi there! We’re a small team of skilled tech enthusiasts working on a handful of large software projects, primarily in the finance, property and telco industries.

With many businesses keen to take full advantage of AI, a lot of our focus is on implementing agentic systems to ensure our clients stay well ahead in the AI race. We’re looking for new team members who are as excited about creating valuable technology partnerships as we are.
## The role
**In short: consultative business development for custom software, digital products and AI solutions.**
We’re looking for a Business Development Manager to help Sprint build new client relationships and identify opportunities where our technology expertise can create meaningful business value.
You’ll generate and qualify opportunities, understand prospective clients’ underlying needs and work with our technical team to shape credible solutions. You’ll manage relationships throughout the sales process—from initial contact and discovery through proposal, negotiation and handover into delivery.
This is not a high-volume, scripted sales role. Our projects are complex, consultative and often business-critical. Success depends on asking intelligent questions, building trust and being honest about what technology can realistically achieve.
You don’t need to be a software developer, but you must be comfortable discussing software, digital transformation and AI with both business and technical stakeholders. You’ll need the judgement to avoid overpromising and the curiosity to learn how our services can solve real operational and commercial problems.
AI-assisted tools can support research, prospecting and communication, but they do not replace expertise or judgement. You must verify their output, protect confidential information and take responsibility for the quality and accuracy of your work.
## What you’ll do
- Identify and develop new business opportunities for custom software, digital products, process automation and AI solutions.
- Build a healthy, well-qualified pipeline through targeted outreach, referrals, networking, partnerships and inbound enquiries.
- Research prospective clients, their industries and the commercial or operational challenges they may be facing.
- Lead initial discovery conversations and establish the underlying business need, desired outcome, urgency and decision-making process.
- Qualify opportunities carefully, focusing our time on work where Sprint can deliver genuine value.
- Explain Sprint’s services clearly to business and technical stakeholders without relying on jargon or exaggerated claims.
- Work with our technical team to shape appropriate solution options, estimates, proposals and presentations.
- Coordinate and contribute to tenders, proposals, statements of work and other commercial documentation.
- Manage opportunities through the sales process, maintaining momentum and agreeing clear next steps.
- Build trusted relationships with decision-makers and other stakeholders throughout longer sales cycles.
- Negotiate scope, commercials and contractual terms with support from Sprint’s leadership team.
- Maintain accurate, current records of opportunities, conversations, forecasts and follow-up actions.
- Produce realistic pipeline forecasts and communicate risks, dependencies and changes promptly.
- Ensure a clear, well-documented handover from business development into project discovery and delivery.
- Maintain relationships with existing clients and identify appropriate opportunities to provide further value.
- Represent Sprint professionally at meetings, networking events and industry activities.
- Use AI tools appropriately, verify their output and protect client data, credentials and proprietary information.
- Share market insight and client feedback to help improve our services, positioning and business development practices.
## What we’re looking for
### Essential
- Commercial experience in business development, consultative sales, account development or a comparable client-facing role.
- Experience selling software development, SaaS, digital services, technology consultancy or another complex business-to-business service.
- Evidence of generating and progressing your own opportunities rather than relying entirely on inbound leads.
- A consultative approach that begins with understanding the client’s objectives, constraints and underlying needs.
- The ability to communicate credibly with senior business stakeholders and collaborate effectively with technical specialists.
- Confidence discussing software, digital products, process improvement and AI at an appropriate business level.
- Experience managing a structured sales pipeline and maintaining accurate CRM or opportunity records.
- The ability to qualify opportunities objectively and recognise when Sprint is not the right fit.
- Experience contributing to proposals, presentations, commercial discussions and negotiations.
- Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain complex ideas clearly and persuasively.
- Good commercial judgement, including an understanding of scope, value, risk and delivery constraints.
- The confidence to challenge assumptions constructively without damaging the client relationship.
- Strong ownership, organisation, attention to detail and follow-through.
- The ability to work independently while involving technical or commercial colleagues at the right time.
- Real examples of building trust, managing objections and handling disagreement constructively.
- The judgement to evaluate information critically, whether it comes from a prospect, colleague, market source or AI tool.
- A commitment to honest, responsible selling without making promises the delivery team cannot support.
**You do not need to be a software developer, but you must be technically curious and able to hold credible conversations about software and AI.** This role is not suitable for someone who relies entirely on generic sales scripts, high-volume outreach or unsupported technical promises.
### Useful, but not essential
- An established network within the finance, property or telecommunications industries.
- Experience selling custom software development, product design, systems integration or process automation.

## Life at Sprint
We offer a flexible, trusting environment where motivated people can do their best work, keep learning and see the impact they create for clients. We value practical solutions, high standards and open collaboration—not technology for its own sake.
Additional benefits include:
- Bupa health insurance option or cash alternative after the probation period.

- Annual summer meet-up.
- Fast and fair progression for high performance.
## Our interview process
We aim to complete the process within four weeks. Every candidate follows the same stages and is assessed against the same evidence-based criteria.
1. ### Application and verification
We review your CV, short introduction and public professional profile on LinkedIn.
2. ### Introductory screen — 5 to 10 minutes
A structured conversation about your recent experience, motivation, availability and fit with the essential criteria.
3. ### Structured interview — 60 minutes
We ask every candidate questions covering pipeline development, opportunity qualification, consultative discovery, commercial judgement, stakeholder management, technical credibility and responsible AI use.
4. ### Practical business development exercise
You review a representative prospective-client scenario and explain how you would research the organisation, qualify the opportunity, conduct the initial discovery conversation and agree the next steps.
5. ### Decision and feedback
The interviewers score the evidence independently before comparing notes. We then make a prompt decision and confirm the outcome.

ABOUT STANDARD BOTS
Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.
ABOUT THE ROLE
*We're hiring a Lead, but if you're a strong functional safety engineer at Senior, Staff or Principal level, we still want to hear from you. We'll level the role and the offer to the person.
If you want a mature process to run, this isn't the role. If you want to build the safety organization behind the best cobot in the world, with the authority to do it, read on.
Standard Bots arms work right next to people, installed by customers who may have never set up a robot before, with no cage and no integrator's risk assessment to lean on. The robot has to be safe by design, and you'll be the one who proves it.
We want to build the best collaborative robot in the world, and that's impossible without building the safest one: a robot anyone can put next to their people on day one and trust. Most of the industry treats safety as paperwork at the end. We want it to be the thing our robots are known for — designed in from the first sketch and proven on real hardware.
Until now, safety has lived inside our hardware, firmware and test teams, like it does at most young companies that ship. That got our first robots out the door. It won't carry what's next: volume growing fast, several new products in development, and AI changing how robots are taught. So we're pulling safety into one strong team with its own mandate — and that team needs a leader.
📍 LOCATION
Remote within the US or Europe, with regular on-site time at our factory in Glen Cove, NY. Requires approximately one week a month onsite, more during validation rounds and assessor visits, since the verification work happens on real robots. Weekly on site is a plus, not a condition.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
- The safety case. You own it across our products — analysis, architecture, and the certification plan that gets each robot through third-party assessment.
- The relationship with assessors. You're our technical voice toward notified bodies and NRTLs, and you're the one in the room defending the argument.
- Verification on real robots. Every safety function gets tested on hardware you trust, fault injection included. You stay hands-on — this is not a reviewing job.
- The team. You hire and lead the functional safety engineers who join after you, starting with one who leans electronics and controls and one who leans software.
- Safety in the design, not at the gate. You report to the Head of System Architecture and work daily with hardware, embedded firmware and test. Safety sits in design reviews from the first sketch.
YOUR FIRST YEAR
- You've owned a safety case for a shipping robot and defended it to an external assessor.
- Every safety function has a verification on real hardware that you trust, including fault injection.
- Your decisions are in the safety architecture of our next generation of arms.
- Hardware and firmware engineers come to you early, because it saves them time.
- You've built a team that runs without you in the room, and set how Standard Bots works on safety.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
- You've taken collaborative robots, or machinery of similar complexity, through third-party safety assessment — and you can tell us what went wrong.
- You work fluently in ISO 10218-1 and -2, ISO 13849-1 and -2, ISO 12100 and IEC 61508, and you have an opinion on the 2025 revision of ISO 10218.
- You can read a schematic and a firmware architecture well enough to challenge the engineers who wrote them.
- You know the full toolkit (FMEA, FTA, HAZOP, STPA, SISTEMA) and which one to reach for.
- You'd rather be on the test floor with a robot and a force gauge than in a document review.
- You know the difference between what the standard requires and what actually makes the robot safe, and you deliver both.
- For the Lead seat: you've led or mentored safety engineers, or you're ready to build a team for the first time.
You don't need to tick every box. If you're close — at any level — apply anyway. We'd rather meet you.
Nice to have
- You've worked on the assessor side, at a notified body or NRTL.
- You know mobile manipulators and AMRs: ANSI/RIA R15.08, ISO 3691-4.
- You've built or specified a safety controller rather than bought one.
- You've shipped at a startup and liked it.
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $230,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.
