Who We’re Looking For
We are seeking an Associate Technical Product Manager to lead roadmap execution for foundational user interface capabilities within the Charles River and Alpha Platforms.
This role is ideal for a product professional with 4+ years of technical product management experience who is highly technical, curious, and comfortable using modern tools to solve problems independently. We are looking for someone fluent in generative AI tools, modern web technologies, APIs, data, and user experience, and who naturally looks for faster and better ways to get work done.
You do not need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable working with technology directly. For example, rather than defaulting to a PowerPoint presentation, you might use AI-assisted tools to quickly create a more compelling interactive presentation. Rather than requesting a new report, you might use an available API and tools such as VS Code and GitHub Copilot to prototype a simple web application that answers the question. Rather than manually analyzing a large set of product feedback, you might use an LLM to help identify themes and then validate the results yourself.
We are looking for someone who combines this builder mindset with strong product judgment, an understanding of user experience, and the ability to lead product discovery and execution in a complex enterprise environment.
Why This Role Is Important to Us
You will join the Platform UI Framework team within the Charles River Investment Management Solution (CRIMS), a market-leading SaaS platform that powers front-to-back investment workflows for some of the world’s largest financial institutions.
As we scale our platform, your talent will be critical in evolving our foundational UI capabilities, improving developer and user experiences, and enabling rapid innovation across the organization. Your ability to combine product leadership with practical technical fluency will help the team investigate product questions, communicate ideas, and validate solutions more quickly.
What You Will Be Responsible For
• Collect and refine business and functional requirements from clients, engineering, architecture, security, operations, and other stakeholders, ensuring platform capabilities meet user, performance, scalability, security, and compliance needs.
• Lead product discovery and technical deep dives, translating complex user and platform needs into clear product requirements, prioritized backlogs, and actionable roadmaps.
• Own roadmap execution for foundational UI capabilities such as reusable web components, desktop containers, interoperability, design systems, and core UI services.
• Engage with engineering and QA members throughout delivery to clarify requirements, evaluate trade-offs, remove ambiguity, and support the timely delivery of key initiatives.
• Partner with UX designers and engineers to create experiences that are intuitive, efficient, accessible, consistent, and technically achievable.
• Use modern technology, including AI-assisted tools, APIs, automation, and lightweight prototyping, to independently investigate product questions, analyze data, communicate ideas, and validate potential solutions.
• Create lightweight prototypes, scripts, visualizations, or web applications when a tangible artifact will produce better insight or stakeholder feedback than a traditional document or presentation.
• Promote a smooth developer experience by helping ensure platform services, components, documentation, and workflows are understandable and intuitive.
• Use product analytics, user feedback, and direct stakeholder engagement to understand adoption, identify friction, and shape roadmap priorities.
• Become a subject matter expert in the coverage area and provide informed recommendations that help shape product strategy and growth.
• Support sales, professional services, and client support activities to improve the client experience and inform future product investments.
Qualifications
• 4+ years of experience in technical product management, business analysis, platform engineering, UX, software development, or a related technology role within a SaaS or enterprise software environment.
• Strong understanding of product management practices, including discovery, requirements definition, user stories, prioritization, roadmaps, iterative delivery, and stakeholder management.
• Strong interest in user experience and interaction design, with the ability to understand complex workflows and identify opportunities to simplify them.
• Technical fluency with modern web applications, including familiarity with React, JavaScript or TypeScript, REST APIs, JSON, authentication, web services, and cloud-based applications.
• Demonstrated ability to use generative AI and AI-assisted tools as part of everyday work, including research, analysis, prototyping, communication, coding, and problem solving.
• Comfort using tools such as VS Code, GitHub, GitHub Copilot, command-line utilities, APIs, and browser developer tools to explore ideas and solve problems independently.
• Ability to create lightweight prototypes, scripts, visualizations, or web applications to explore a product idea or answer a business question. Production-level software engineering experience is not required.
• Comfort working with data and selecting the right tool for the problem, whether Excel, SQL, an API, Power BI, or a lightweight custom application.
• Proven ability to work with cross-functional teams to deliver scalable, secure, and high-impact platform capabilities.
• Strong technical acumen and the ability to engage meaningfully with engineers, architects, designers, security teams, and non-technical stakeholders.
• Experience with Azure cloud services and enterprise security or compliance requirements is beneficial.
• Experience with Jira, Confluence, Figma, GitHub, or similar product development tools is beneficial.
• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Human-Computer Interaction, Product Design, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Job Description
Join Us as a Regulatory Affairs Manager – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation
We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years. As part of our global team, you’ll have the opportunity to provide technical and project leadership over a region(s). As a Regulatory Affairs Manager, you'll offer innovative solutions, including regulatory affairs expertise and client interface, to provide strategic regulatory intelligence and guidance supporting product development from preclinical stages through registration and product optimization. You will provide strategic, expedient, and efficient preparation of client deliverables that meet current local, regional, and ICH regulatory and technical requirements. Additionally, you will act as a liaison with internal and external clients in the provision and marketing of these services.
As a Regulatory Intelligence Manager will play a pivotal role in monitoring, analyzing, and communicating global regulatory developments that impact client’s pipeline and operations. This individual will serve as a strategic partner to cross-functional teams, proactively identifying relevant developments and translating them into actionable insights to inform regulatory strategy and operational planning.
What You’ll Do:
• Monitor & Analyze: Track global regulatory changes, guidance documents, and policy trends across key markets (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.) or stakeholders (EU Commission, ICH, ISO, etc.).
• Impact Assessment: Proactively synthesize information from multiple regulatory sources and, in collaboration with relevant internal stakeholders, assess the implications for client’s development programmes and operational practices. Translate findings into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for client’s teams.
• Stakeholder Alignment: Interact with Regulatory Affairs, Clinical, Quality, Pharmacovigilance and Legal teams to ensure alignment and awareness with key areas of interest and hot topics.
• Communication: Contribute to the creation of and distribute client’s newsletters, alerts, and briefing documents tailored to various audiences. Publish relevant selected content to client’s Engage forum.
• Precedent Searches: Conduct targeted regulatory precedent searches and synthesize findings into clear responses that inform stakeholder decisions.
• Knowledge Management: Maintain a centralized repository of regulatory intelligence resources and ensure accessibility across teams.
• External Engagement: Participate in industry forums, working groups, and regulatory intelligence networks to stay ahead of emerging trends.
• Provides senior review and advice to prepare regional regulatory submissions and ensure high quality standards that meet or exceed client expectations, local and regional requirements.
• Acts as subject matter expert in providing regulatory strategy advice and technical expertise to internal and external clients and for key client projects ofmoderate to high complexity. Provides internal clients with up-to-date legislation and guidance as it becomes available.
• Ensures quality performance for key/managed projects.
• Manages project budgeting/forecasting functions.
• Identifies and recognizes out of scope activities in a contract in a timely manner and liaises with other departments to follow through on all aspects of contract modifications.
• Collaborates with business development in pricing and securing new business by making presentations to clients, and develops proposal texts and budgets in collaboration with other departments.

Typically appointed by the General Contractor, Main Contractor, or lead MEP sub-contractor, the CxM leads the on-site commissioning team and drives all commissioning activities from pre-construction through to formal handover and post-occupancy. The CxM ensures that all building systems are installed, tested, validated, and handed over in full compliance with the Owner's Project Requirements, Basis of Design, contract documents, and applicable industry standards. This role demands a combination of deep technical expertise, strong project management capability, and effective leadership and communication skills.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Programme Leadership & Strategy
Develop Commissioning Activities Schedule "CAS" as the determined schedule of all Cx activities. Lead and manage all commissioning activities across one or more projects, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, and quality standards.
Develop, own, and maintain the live inline with the holistic Commissioning Programme, integrating it with the overall construction schedule. This should be logic linked to all preceding activities and dependencies.
Chair commissioning progress meetings, attend GC/MEP static completion meetings; produce weekly and monthly progress reports for the project leadership team.
Define the commissioning strategy for each project, aligning with CIBSE Guide M, client objectives, regulatory requirements, and handover milestones.
Manage and mitigate commissioning programme risks, proactively communicating schedule impacts to the Project Manager.
2. Team Management & Coordination
Lead, coordinate the on-site commissioning team, including Commissioning Engineers (CxE), Commissioning Agents (CxA), and sub-contractor commissioning personnel.
Assign tasks specific commissioning related tasks, set performance expectations, and provide ongoing guidance and support throughout the project lifecycle.
Coordinate trades, specialist vendors, and sub-contractors to ensure seamless sequencing of commissioning activities.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and collaborative problem-solving within the commissioning team.
3. Technical Oversight & Quality Assurance
Oversee Pre-Functional Checks (PFC), Functional Performance Tests (FPT), and Integrated Systems Tests (IST) through to completion.
Produce a Commissioning Method Statement tracker. Collating all test scripts and methodologies aligned with the activities in the CAS
Read and interpret test scripts and methodologies to determine whether functional test results are genuinely acceptable or influenced by programme pressure.
Review and approve commissioning plans, test procedures, and commissioning documentation prepared by the team, Supplier, Manufacturer, and Sub-Contractors.
Identify and resolve system deficiencies in collaboration with design teams, contractors, and specialist vendors.
Ensure that all building systems—HVAC, electrical, BMS/BAS, plumbing, fire protection, and life safety—perform in accordance with design specifications.
4. Design Review & Pre-Construction Input
Review project designs, specifications, and equipment submittals to provide commissioning input and flag potential issues early.
Collaborate with clients, design engineers, and contractors to understand project requirements and develop robust commissioning plans.
Establish and document the Basis of Design (BoD) during pre-construction phases.
Ensure commissioning requirements are incorporated into construction documents and contractor scopes, CAS.

Communicate deficiencies clearly and professionally to contractors, maintaining constructive working relationships.
Prepare and own the contractor's sections of the Final Commissioning Report at project close-out.

Own the commissioning documentation management process, including use of customer-specific platforms (e.g., CxAlloy, BIM 360, Procore).
Provide checks to ensure all O&M manuals, as-built drawings, and systems documentation are complete, accurate, and formally handed over to the owner.
Manage and close out the deficiency/punch list, ensuring all items are resolved prior to practical completion.
Sign off and own the Final Commissioning Report, certifying that the building was delivered to design intent.

Oversee and coordinate training programmes for facility operations and maintenance staff on all commissioned systems.
Recommend and, where required, manage ongoing post-occupancy commissioning (Retro-Commissioning/RCx) to ensure long-term performance.
Stay current with ASHRAE Guidelines (Guideline 0, 1.x series), CIBSE guides, and relevant industry standards and best practices.
Support business development activities including preparation of commissioning proposals, fee estimates, and participation in client presentations.
Contribute to the development of internal commissioning standards, procedures, and quality management frameworks.

Background
This 1-year position is available to carry out research within a Wellcome
Trust-funded research programme, which aims to understand how transcription
regulation of genes drives mRNA diversification and diverse mRNA fates. The post
holder will carry out independent research in cancer genetics and aim to
understand how transcription regulation control mRNA fates upon metabolic stress
and metabolic regulation. They will use organoids models to characterise
transcriptome profiles of colorectal cancer organoids exposed to various
metabolic stresses (hypoxia, mTOR inhibition, nutrient deprivation) and develop
novel biomarkers that stratify colorectal cancer organoids responsiveness to
mTOR inhibition.
Working with Prof Ferenc Mueller and in collaboration with Professor Andrew
Beggs they will transfect organoids using lentiviral vectors to generate
fluorescence reporters and to interfere with transcription factor function. They
will operate in dedicated high specification tissue culture space with access to
in vivo 4D imaging by light sheet microscopy and high content microscopy.
The post holder will work closely with research fellows working in the
Wellcome-funded programme in the Mueller/Beggs laboratories. The postholder will
train postgraduate students in organoid culture and organoid manipulation tools.

* Work within specified research grant (Wellcome Trust funded programme)

Background
We are seeking to appoint a Quantitative Research Fellow to join the Women,
Crime and Justice Research Group. The Group are committed to delivering
high-quality research to improve outcomes for women involved in the criminal
justice system and to build the evidence base on what works best for them.
As part of the Effective Women’s Centre (Phase III) project (JABBS Foundation),
the role holder will work across multiple workstreams to turn research questions
into analysis plans, carry out the analyses, and write up methods and results
for reports and academic papers.  In addition, the role holder will also be
expected to develop their own lines of research enquiry within the group’s
programme, with support.
The role holder will be hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in criminology,
psychology, social policy, public health, or a related quantitative social
science. They will have experience conducting systematic reviews and evidence
syntheses, with a strong understanding of quantitative research methods and data
analysis.  Experience working with administrative or linked datasets, including
within secure research environments, would be advantageous. The role holder will
be confident in producing high-quality research outputs for a range of
disciplinary audiences and have experience contributing to academic publications
commensurate to your career stage. Given the policy focus of the Research
Group's work, the role holder will be able to turn research findings into
accessible briefings for policymakers, funders and practitioners.
Role Summary
* Design and undertake systematic reviews and meta-analyses on women in the
criminal justice system, including gender-responsive interventions,
diversion, trauma, and women’s centre outcomes. 
* Conduct literature searches, study screening, data extraction, risk of bias
assessments, and quantitative or narrative evidence synthesis.
* Work within specified research grants and projects and contribute to writing
bids 
* Operate within area of specialism
* Analyse and interpret research findings and results 
* Contribute to generating funding 
* Contribute to licensing or spin out deals with demonstrated commercial
success (such as revenues, asset or company sales, IP generated) and/or
public understanding of the discipline or similar
Main Duties
The responsibilities may include some but not all of the responsibilities
outlined below.
* Design and carry out systematic reviews and meta-analyses on women in the
criminal justice system, on topics such as gender-responsive interventions,
diversion, women’s centre outcomes, trauma and risk/need assessment. This
covers the whole review process: protocol registration, searches of academic
and grey literature, screening, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, and
synthesis of effect sizes (or structured narrative synthesis where studies
are too varied to pool).
* Contribute to data access applications to trusted research environments (for
example the ONS Secure Research Service, SAIL Databank and NHS England’s
Secure Data Environment). This includes writing project proposals, data
specifications and linkage requests, and handling information governance and
ethics requirements. Once access is granted, prepare and analyse the linked
datasets within these environments in line with data governance and
disclosure control rules.
* Develop research objectives and proposals for own or joint research, with
assistance of a mentor if required
* Contribute to writing bids for research funding
* Analyse and interpret data
* Apply knowledge in a way which develops new intellectual understanding
* Disseminate research findings for publication, research seminars etc
* Supervise students on research related work and provide guidance to PhD
students where appropriate to the discipline
* Contribute to developing new models, techniques and methods 
* Undertake management/administration arising from research
* Contribute to Departmental/School research-related activities and
research-related administration
* Contribute to enterprise, business development and/or public engagement
activities of manifest benefit to the College and the University, often under
supervision of a project leader
* Collect research data; this may be through a variety of research methods,
such as scientific experimentation, literature reviews, and research
interviews
* Present research outputs, including drafting academic publications or parts
thereof, for example at seminars and as posters

assisting with the research

At UnlikelyAI, we are building the future of AI: one that is reliable, explainable, and resistant to hallucination. Our patented neurosymbolic platform combines the expressive power of LLMs with the transparency and control of symbolic reasoning. This enables us to create AI systems that are accurate, auditable, and suitable for high-trust, high-stakes applications – where precision, traceability, and compliance are essential.
THE ROLE
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to be the Tech Lead for Uncheck, our accounting disclosure product, and lead its planning and delivery as it scales across customers and markets. You'll own the technical plan and sequencing, working with product and customers, and make sure it is delivered well and on time, while staying hands-on in the code.
Uncheck automates the checking of accounting disclosures. It reviews financial statements against the accounting standards and regulations that apply to them, and shows the evidence behind each finding. It is live in production at enterprise scale, and we are expanding it into new regions and markets.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys leading the delivery of software as much as building it, and takes pride in delivering what has been promised. You'll work on planning and building a product that customers rely on for regulatory decisions, writing code alongside an experienced engineering team, and collaborate with product and research colleagues.
Pioneering AI is one of our leadership principles. In every role we make AI our starting point for rethinking how work gets done, and you'll lead that for the Uncheck engineering team.
This is a hands-on position with real impact, offering the chance to shape Uncheck through its next stage of growth.

- Own the technical plan for Uncheck and lead delivery against the commitments we make to customers.

- Lead how the team builds with AI agents, including how agent-written code is reviewed, tested and shipped safely, and measure what it does for delivery.
- Make sure Uncheck runs reliably and securely in the cloud as it scales to new customers and regions.
- Lead technical conversations with customers' IT, security and architecture teams, from first evaluation through to live use.
- Work with product and research colleagues to turn new capabilities and customer feedback into clear priorities.
- Mentor engineers across the team.

- ...you already work AI-first. Agents write a large share of your code, and you have firm views on how a team should review and test that work, because customers rely on what we ship for regulatory decisions.
- ...you have led delivery for a team of 4 to 8 engineers, shipping to enterprise customers on time and to a high standard.
- ...you have mentored engineers and helped them grow.
- ...you communicate clearly with customers and non-engineers, and are comfortable leading technical conversations with enterprise teams.
- ...you have strong back-end experience in any language, including agent-written code, and able to make sound technical decisions.
- ...you have owned production cloud services, ideally on AWS, in a team with strong engineering practice: code review, automated testing, CI/CD and on-call.
- ...you understand what enterprise security and compliance teams expect.
OTHER SKILLS

- Experience shipping AI-powered products or features to customers, and making their output reliable at scale.
- Experience with Python, which our back end is written in.
- Experience in a regulated industry, such as financial or professional services, legal, insurance or healthcare.
- Experience taking a product into new regions.
- DevOps, infrastructure and SRE experience, such as infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines and observability.

Joining UnlikelyAI means working on technology that pushes boundaries while shaping your career:

- Work alongside researchers developing new approaches to trustworthy AI.

The Clinical Data Configuration Manager sits within R&D’s Testing, Innovation, and Data Enablement organisation and supports clinical study execution by configuring study-level clinical data extractions, transformations, visualisations, and transfers across multiple data sources in alignment with Data Transfer Agreements and technical specifications. This role partners with internal and external stakeholders (including data engineers) to deliver accurate, high quality data in required formats and frequencies , contributes to the development and training of transfer standards/ SOPs and best practices, and provides quality oversight and team capability support (including mentoring/training others and vendor /FSP oversight as needed) to ensure consistent, on time delivery.
 
Accountabilities:
• Configure study-level clinical data extraction, transformation, and transfer outputs across multiple data sources per Data Transfer Agreement/specifications.
• Partner closely with internal/external stakeholders (including Data Engineers) to deliver required data formats/frequencies with high quality and on time.
• Support implementation of sponsor-defined data transfer standards and specifications.
• Provide input to documentation and training materials as requested.
• Perform/coordinate quality review of configuration and deliverables, including oversight/review of vendor-performed work as needed.
• Support team capability by managing and training other team members; complete other assigned duties within timelines.
 
Education:
• Bachelor's degree  (e g., CS, Statistics,/Biostatistics, math, biology/heath related) plus minimum 5 years relevant experience (or equivalent experience).
• Experience with EDC build/data management or EDC extraction/configuration; strong understanding of clinical data flow (CDMS, vendor devices, CDR). 
• Familiarity with data cleaning tools (e.g. Veeva CDB, J Review, Elluminate); Strong clinical trial terminology and data transfer specification knowledge; understanding of SDTM.
• Data/Integration: XMLs, APIs, MDR (preferred); ETL/ELT experience
• Programming (preferred): One or more SQL, SAS, R or Python; R Shiny/Python app development.
• Tools/ways of working: Microsoft Office
• Independent and collaborative problem-solving; ability to prioritize and work in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong project management skills including: Initiative, deadline management, strong attention to detail, organization, time management; quick learner comfortable with new tech/systems.

We are seeking an experienced Clinical Data Enablement Manager (FSP) to support and enhance clinical data operations across modern cloud-based data platforms. This is an exciting opportunity for a data professional with strong technical expertise in data engineering, ETL/ELT development, cloud technologies, and clinical data environments to play a key role in enabling efficient, reliable, and compliant clinical data delivery.
Working within our Data Management team, you will help drive the operation, monitoring, maintenance, and continuous improvement of clinical data pipelines that underpin critical clinical development activities.
What You'll Be Doing
As a Clinical Data Enablement Manager, you will:
• Support end-to-end clinical data pipelines across data lake and data warehouse environments, ensuring reliable and traceable operations.
• Build, enhance, monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot ETL/ELT workflows and data integrations.
• Develop and support cloud-based data ingestion and transformation processes within AWS and/or Azure environments.
• Assist with operational support activities including monitoring, alert management, incident investigation, and root cause analysis.
• Implement automation solutions for scheduling, data ingestion, quality checks, and operational efficiency.
• Design and maintain operational dashboards and visualizations to monitor pipeline performance, data quality, and key operational metrics.
• Collaborate with internal teams, vendors, and stakeholders to support data transfers, validations, reconciliations, and issue resolution.
• Partner closely with Statistical Programming, SDTM, Clinical Data Programming, and Analytics teams to understand and deliver data requirements.
• Support KPI reporting and contribute to on-time, high-quality data delivery.
• Maintain controlled documentation, testing evidence, and traceability in support of regulated clinical processes.
• Apply data integrity principles and support compliance with GxP, audit readiness, security, access controls, and data governance standards.
Education & Competencies:
• Education/Experience: BS/BA (or equivalent) plus 5+ years in data engineering, pipeline
development/operations, and multi-source data integration (clinical/biopharma preferred).
• Core skills: Foundational SQL skills; understanding of basic data modelling and data quality checks;
familiarity with integration patterns (NoSQL exposure a plus).
• Programming/SDLC: Proficiency in Python (preferred) or R; exposure to building/supporting
pipelines with basic testing, logging, and monitoring; familiarity with Agile/SDLC
concepts; Jira/Confluence experience preferred (or ability to learn quickly).
• Visualization & Reporting (for Reporting role): Hands-on experience designing and supporting
operational dashboards and data visualizations using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, and/or
QlikView, with an understanding of data refresh, access controls, and performance considerations.
• Data standards (preferred): Awareness of CDISC/CDASH/SDTM concepts and willingness to learn
how standards impact downstream clinical deliverables.
• Data formats & Interfaces: Hands-on with CSV, JSON, XML and file/API-based integrations; able to
follow transfer specifications and validate outputs.
• Cloud/platforms (preferred): Exposure to AWS and/or Azure and modern data platforms
(e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, Spark); ability to implement within established frameworks and
standards.
• DevOps: Working knowledge of GitHub/GitLab version control; CI/CD exposure is a plus.
• GxP & Data integrity (preferred): Experience or exposure to GxP-regulated practices
(documentation, change control, audit readiness) and understanding of data integrity expectations;
able to follow controlled procedures and maintain required evidence.
• Ways of working / working style: Strong collaboration and communication; organised, detail orientated,
proactive; able to prioritise tasks, follow guidance, and deliver to deadlines in a fast-paced
environment.
• Preferred: Prior regulatory inspection/audit support experience; AWS/Azure and/or Python
certification.

Voltera is seeking a Security & EHS Operations Manager to lead day-to-day security and environmental, health, and safety (EHS) operations across all of Voltera’s workplace and commercial locations nationwide. This is a hands-on, full-time role, not a purely strategic one: you will directly supervise the Security Desk and embedded security staff, own the technology that runs physical security day to day, and build out the data and reporting function that gives leadership visibility into both programs.
You should be comfortable working hands-on with security-specific technology and systems on a daily basis, and equally comfortable managing the outsourced EHS expertise that supports workplace safety and the environmental requirements that come with operating EV charging sites. You don’t need to be the technical EHS expert yourself; you need to understand the requirements well enough to manage that vendor relationship and make sure its guidance translates into real execution on the ground. This role also partners closely with the teams supporting a site’s full development lifecycle — Real Estate, Development, and Construction — with People Operations and Workplace teams supporting Voltera’s distributed worker base, and with customer security and safety teams at partner locations.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Security Operations
• Directly supervise 24/7 Security Desk operations, including scheduling, performance, and day-to-day direction of embedded security staff.
• Own and operate Voltera’s core security technology stack nationwide — access control & badging systems, video management systems (VMS), and visitor management systems — including user provisioning, credentialing, and system health.
• Coordinate incident response, investigations, and post-incident reporting across all locations.
• Manage third-party physical security consulting engagements, including scope, deliverables, and program design and execution.
• Evaluate and expand security coverage models — embedded staffing, technology, and patrol — as new and newly acquired sites come online.
• Own security-related vendor budgets, invoicing, and SOW/PO administration.
Data & Reporting (Security + EHS)
• Own the data and reporting function for both security and EHS programs, building and maintaining the metrics, dashboards, and reporting cadence leadership uses to track both — pulling in vendor-supplied data as a key input.
• Serve as the source of truth for security and EHS KPIs — incidents, access activity, audit findings, and vendor performance — across the nationwide portfolio.
• Standardize status reporting and escalation flags so open issues in either function surface quickly.
Work Order & Vendor Coordination (Security + EHS)

About the role
Our backend layer is a set of Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) services, written in Java, that sit between
our clients and the vendor platform. They aggregate, shape and cache data for each client, handle
both request-response and real-time event traffic, and enforce security and regulatory rules before
anything reaches the player.
As a Principal Backend Engineer you set the reference architecture for these services and are
accountable for how fast and how reliably they run. You will write production code, make the hard
design calls, and raise the bar for every backend engineer who joins after you.
What you will own Our backend layer is a set of Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) services, written in Java, that sit between
our clients and the vendor platform. They aggregate, shape and cache data for each client, handle
both request-response and real-time event traffic, and enforce security and regulatory rules before
anything reaches the player.
As Principal Backend Engineer you set the reference architecture for these services and are
accountable for how fast and how reliably they run. You will write production code, make the hard
design calls, and raise the bar for every backend engineer who joins after you.
Scope
. BFF services and their APIs to all clients.
• Integration with EveryMatrix and other vendor APIs and event streams.
• Caching, data stores and messaging used by our backend.
• Backend observability, SLOs, load and capacity testing.
Must have
Seniority: 10+ years building backend systems, with at least 3 in a lead, staff or principal role
setting architecture across multiple services.
• Java at depth: modern Java (17+), JVM internals, memory and garbage-collection tuning,
concurrency (including virtual threads and reactive or non-blocking I/O), and profiling under load.
• Design patterns and architecture: practical command of GoF and enterprise integration
patterns, hexagonal or clean architecture, domain-driven design, and API gateway / BFF patterns,
plus the judgement to know when not to use them.
• Spring Boot (or equivalent framework) in production at scale.
• Sync and async communication: REST and gRPC; event streaming and messaging (Kafka,
Pub/Sub or similar); real-time push to clients (WebSockets or server-sent events); delivery
guarantees, ordering and idempotency.
• Caching: distributed caches (Redis or similar), multi-level caching, invalidation strategies, and
HTTP/CDN cache semantics.
• Data: relational databases (PostgreSQL or similar) including query and index tuning, and the
consistency trade-offs of distributed data.
• Performance engineering: load and soak testing, latency analysis at p95/p99, capacity planning,
and evidence of having made a production system measurably faster.
• Availability and observability: SLOs and error budgets, metrics, tracing and logging
(OpenTelemetry, Prometheus or similar), and hands-on incident leadership.
• Cloud-native delivery: containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD and safe deployment practices (canary,
feature flags, rollback).
• Security: OAuth2/OIDC, token handling, input validation and secure-by-default API design.
Strongly Preferred
. Other backend languages: Kotlin, Go or Node.js. We choose the BFF language per service, so breadth matters.
• Regulated or high-traffic real-time domains: iGaming, sports betting, payments, trading or similar.
• Experience with EveryMatrix or comparable iGaming platforms (wallet, cashier, casino ggregation, sportsbook feeds).
• Google Cloud (GKE, Cloud Run, Memorystore, Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL), Cloudflare, ArgoCD and Terraform.
• Server-driven UI or aggregation APIs serving several client platforms.
• Compliance-driven engineering: DGA SCP, PCI DSS, ISO 27001 or GDPR
What success looks like
First 30 days
• Understand the current BFF services, vendor integrations and traffic profile.
• Establish a performance and availability baseline and publish the gaps.
• Ship production code in at least one BFF service.
First 90 days
• Publish the BFF reference architecture covering service structure, sync/async patterns, caching
and data rules.
. Agree SLOs for player-critical journeys (login, deposit, bet placement, game launch) with
dashboards and alerts behind them.
• Run the first full load test against launch traffic forecasts and close the critical findings.
By launch
• BFF layer meets agreed SLOs under forecast peak load, with tested degradation paths for every vendor dependency.
• Runbooks and on-call in place; backend engineers designing new services to the reference architecture without your involvement
Compensation
Competitive base salary. Full range and benefits shared at first conversation.
Interview process
• Intro call (30 min): role, team and your background.
• Technical interview (2 hrs): a deep dive on Java, the JVM, concurrency and design patterns,
using a system you built; system design of a BFF for a real-time sportsbook or casino journey
covering sync and async flows, caching, data and SLOs; and a pair-programming exercise on a
realistic backend problem.

Could this be you? What we do
Everyone has an idea of what a water company does. Here in Yorkshire, we make sure that over 5.4 million people living in the region, and the millions of people who visit our region each year, can rely on our services. We provide clean and safe drinking water and ensure wastewater is safely taken away. But for us, it is so much more than this.

The Water Resources Strategy Team is responsible for developing and maintaining the plans that help ensure secure, resilient and sustainable water supplies. Accurate and transparent regulatory reporting is an essential part of demonstrating our performance against these plans and maintaining the confidence of our customers, Board and regulators.
As our Regulatory Reporting Lead, you will coordinate the data analysis and technical reporting required for Yorkshire Water’s water resources regulatory submissions. This includes the annual reviews of our Water Resources Management Plan and Drought Plan, the Water Environment Supply and Security Delivery metric within the Environmental Performance Assessment, relevant Annual Performance Report submissions, supply scheme Price Control Deliverables and responses to regulatory consultations and requests. Where you fit in
As our Regulatory Reporting Lead, you will work across Yorkshire Water, particularly with data owners and technical experts, to collate, analyse, validate and report the information required for regulatory submissions.
You will summarise our performance against the published Water Resources Management Plan and Drought Plan, support regulatory audits and contribute to the preparation of Board papers required to secure assurance over our data and submissions.
The role will involve extracting and analysing information from multiple datasets, reconciling complex data and ensuring consistency and traceability between different regulatory submissions.
